variations.note: Singular: моим соседом
A different instrumental: they are our partners

options.note: Zero copula with the nominative — the natural spoken version
Using по соседству (we live next door to each other)

paraphrases.simplest: Они мои соседи. — overwhelmingly the natural choice in speech.

takeaway.pattern: являться + instrumental (to be: the formal copula)
takeaway.note: Written register only. Speech says Он директор (zero copula, nominative), and the past takes the instrumental: Он был директором.

keyPoint: Крайний is an adjective meaning "end, last, outermost."

grammarFocus.construction: выбрать (perfective past plural выбрали) + adjective крайний + accusative (столик)
grammarFocus.note: крайний means 'the end one, outermost' and follows the soft declension (крайний/крайняя/крайнее). It also gives idioms like крайний случай (a last resort).

variations.note: With a feminine noun: крайнюю

variations.ru: Мы сели за крайний столик у окна.
variations.note: Adding у окна (by the window)

options.note: Using в углу (in the corner), more concrete
Using у самого окна (right by the window)

paraphrases.simplest: Они выбрали крайний столик. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: The -ний type gives -няя in the feminine and -нее in the neuter. крайний срок (the final deadline) is another frequent pairing.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Означать is a stative verb of meaning/relation with no perfective counterpart.

replies.gloss: I can explain it to them.

grammarFocus.construction: negation (не понимают) + что clause + означать (3sg означает)
grammarFocus.note: означать is the imperfective 'to mean', slightly more bookish than значить. что это означает is an indirect question.

variations.ru: Я не понимаю, что это означает.
variations.note: First person singular subject

variations.ru: Они не понимают, что это значит.
variations.note: With значит, more colloquial

options.note: Using непонятен with смысл (the meaning escapes them)
Using объяснить (they can't explain it)

paraphrases.simplest: Они не понимают, что это значит. — значит is the natural spoken choice.

takeaway.pattern: indirect questions (что это означает / где он / когда начнётся)
takeaway.note: The question word stays and the word order doesn't change; Russian always puts a comma before the clause.

keyPoint: Десять is the numeral "ten"; like 5 and up, the noun takes the genitive plural.

grammarFocus.construction: ждать (imperfective present 1sg жду) + adverb уже + numeral десять + genitive plural (минут)
grammarFocus.note: Numerals from five up take the genitive plural (десять минут). уже with the present tense marks how long something has been going on.

variations.note: A different numeral, still the genitive plural минут
With два the form is the genitive singular часа

options.note: Dropping the verb and naming the place
Switching perspective with опаздывать на + accusative

paraphrases.simplest: Я жду десять минут. — уже can be left out.

takeaway.pattern: уже + present tense (have been doing for ...)
takeaway.note: Russian uses the present for ongoing duration: Я живу здесь уже год (I've been living here a year).

keyPoint: Полностью is an adverb meaning "completely."

grammarFocus.construction: adverb полностью + с + instrumental (тобой) + short-form predicate (согласен)
grammarFocus.note: полностью means 'completely'. согласен is a predicate-only short form, and the person you agree with goes in с + instrumental.

variations.note: To a formal or plural addressee: с вами
A female speaker says согласна

options.note: Using абсолютно, a short way to agree
Using точно так же (I think exactly the same)

paraphrases.simplest: Полностью согласен. — two words are enough.

takeaway.note: All three mark strong agreement. The negative is совсем не согласен (I don't agree at all).

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Стараться is imperfective, meaning "to try/make an effort" (pairs with постараться).

grammarFocus.construction: frequency adverb всегда + стараться (imperfective present 1sg стараюсь) + perfective infinitive (помочь)
grammarFocus.note: стараться is a reflexive imperfective meaning 'to try' and takes an infinitive. помочь puts the person helped in the dative.

variations.note: First person plural: стараемся
The perfective постараюсь means 'I'll try this time'

options.note: Using готов + infinitive (always ready to help)

options.ru: Я никогда не отказываю в помощи.
options.note: Using не отказывать в + prepositional (I never refuse help)

paraphrases.simplest: Я всегда стараюсь помочь. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: стараться (try, imperfective) / постараться (try this once, perfective)
takeaway.note: Я стараюсь describes a standing habit; Я постараюсь is a promise about this occasion.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Хватать is imperfective, meaning "to be enough" (pairs with хватить).

grammarFocus.construction: знать (3pl знают) + чего clause + dative (им) + negated impersonal не хватает
grammarFocus.note: хватать is an impersonal verb of sufficiency taking a dative and a genitive. Under negation the thing lacking is genitive, hence чего.

variations.ru: Я знаю, чего мне не хватает.
variations.note: With the first person singular dative
Naming the genitive: they're short of time

options.note: Using слабые места (their weak points)
Using нужно with a noun (they need a bit more experience)

paraphrases.simplest: Они знают свои слабые места. — more direct and easier to follow.

takeaway.pattern: dative + не хватает + genitive (someone lacks something)
takeaway.note: Мне не хватает денег (I'm short of money). The same verb gives the exclamation Хватит! (that's enough).

keyPoint: Старший is a comparative-derived adjective meaning "older, elder."

replies.gloss: How many older brothers do you have?
Do you see each other often?

grammarFocus.construction: nominative (они) + dash + possessive мои + adjective старшие + predicate noun (братья)
grammarFocus.note: With no verb between subject and predicate noun, written Russian may insert a dash. старший ('older') comes from a comparative.

variations.note: Singular: мой старший брат
With младший (younger) and a feminine plural

options.note: Making это the subject, more colloquial
Using the comparative старше + genitive (they're older than me)

paraphrases.simplest: Это мои старшие братья. — the это version is the natural spoken one.

takeaway.pattern: a dash between subject and predicate noun (Москва — столица России)
takeaway.note: When both are nouns, written Russian joins them with a dash; with pronoun subjects it is often omitted (Он врач).

keyPoint: Неплохо is an adverb meaning "not bad, pretty good."

replies.gloss: What do you like to cook?

grammarFocus.construction: adverb неплохо + готовить (imperfective present 2sg готовишь)
grammarFocus.note: неплохо means 'not badly', with не fused onto плохо. In Russian it functions as understated praise.

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener
With хорошо, a plainer compliment

options.note: Using получаться (your food turns out delicious)
Using стоит + infinitive for exaggerated praise

paraphrases.simplest: Ты хорошо готовишь. — the straightforward compliment.

takeaway.pattern: неплохо (not bad = rather good: understated praise)
takeaway.note: неплохой фильм (quite a good film). Russian often prefers a не- understatement to direct praise.

skeleton.note: future 3rd person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Погибнуть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "perishing" (pairs with погибать).

replies.gloss: I hope it all works out.

grammarFocus.construction: бояться (imperfective present 3pl боятся) + что clause + perfective future (погибнет)
grammarFocus.note: бояться normally takes the genitive but can also introduce a что clause. погибнуть means dying violently or in an accident, more dramatic than умереть.

variations.note: First person singular: боюсь
With бояться за + accusative (they fear for the hero)

options.note: Using переживать за + accusative (they're anxious for him)
Using the impersonal страшно + dative

paraphrases.simplest: Они боятся за героя. — the за + accusative version is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: погибнуть (die violently or in an accident) / умереть (die of illness or age)
takeaway.note: погибнуть в аварии (die in a crash), умереть от болезни (die of illness). The cause decides the verb.

keyPoint: Клуб is a masculine noun meaning "club."

grammarFocus.construction: пойти (perfective future 1pl пойдём) + time adverb вечером + в + accusative (клуб)
grammarFocus.note: пойдём is the standard 'let's go'. The time of day is an instrumental adverb (вечером) and the destination takes в + accusative.

variations.note: Inviting a formal or plural group: пойдёмте
A different time and destination

options.note: давай plus the phrase alone — the most colloquial invitation
Using как насчёт + genitive (how about a club tonight?)

paraphrases.simplest: Давай вечером в клуб. — dropping the verb is the natural spoken form.

takeaway.pattern: instrumental time adverbs (утром, днём, вечером, ночью)
takeaway.note: A bare instrumental expresses 'in the morning, at night'. зимой and летом work the same way.

keyPoint: Чуть is an adverb meaning "almost, slightly"; чуть не means "almost (didn't happen)."

grammarFocus.construction: чуть не + perfective past (опоздал)
grammarFocus.note: чуть не means 'nearly': despite the не, the event did not happen — he almost was late but made it in time.

variations.note: A female speaker says опоздала
A different verb: we nearly fell

options.note: Using почти (almost)
Using успеть (I made it at the last minute), stated positively

paraphrases.simplest: Я чуть не опоздал. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: чуть не + perfective past (nearly did something)
takeaway.note: Я чуть не забыл (I nearly forgot). The не does not negate — it means the thing almost happened.

keyPoint: Дух is a masculine noun meaning "spirit."

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (тебя) + adjective сильный + nominative (дух)
grammarFocus.note: дух means 'spirit, mettle' and is masculine, so сильный agrees in the masculine singular nominative. сильный дух is a set pairing.

variations.note: With воля (will): сильная
With характер (character)

options.note: Using сильный человек (you're a strong person)
Using трудно сломать (you're hard to break)

paraphrases.simplest: Ты сильный. — two words carry it.

takeaway.note: сильный дух (a strong spirit), добрая душа (a kind soul). дух is will and nerve; душа is the seat of feeling.

keyPoint: Невозможно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's impossible."

grammarFocus.construction: говорить (3pl говорят) + что clause + impersonal predicate невозможно
grammarFocus.note: невозможно means 'it is impossible' and takes no subject, with не- fused onto возможно.

variations.note: A different main clause: I think so
Without the negation: they say it's possible

options.note: Using по их словам (according to them) with нереально
Using считать + accusative + instrumental

paraphrases.simplest: Они говорят, это невозможно. — что can be dropped.

takeaway.note: All take no subject and pair with an infinitive or a что clause: Невозможно понять (it's impossible to understand).

keyPoint: Устать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting tired" (pairs with уставать).

replies.gloss: What tired you out so much?

grammarFocus.construction: intensifier очень + устать (perfective past устал) + time adverb сегодня
grammarFocus.note: устать is perfective and marks the shift into tiredness. Russian uses its past tense for the present state: Я устал = I'm tired now.

variations.note: A female speaker says устала
A plural subject takes устали

options.note: Using без сил (I've no strength left)
The idiom валиться с ног (I'm ready to drop)

paraphrases.simplest: Я устал. — two words are enough.

takeaway.pattern: устать (the perfective past expresses a present state)
takeaway.note: Я устал means 'I am tired'. The same holds for Я проголодался (I'm hungry) and Я замёрз (I'm cold).

skeleton.note: neuter noun, genitive, the target word

keyPoint: Понятие is a neuter noun meaning "concept, notion," frequent in the fixed phrase не иметь понятия ("to have no idea").

grammarFocus.construction: negation не + иметь (imperfective present 1sg имею) + genitive (понятия)
grammarFocus.note: A classic genitive of negation. не иметь понятия (to have no idea) is a fixed phrase and always takes the genitive понятия.

variations.ru: Я не имею ни малейшего понятия.
variations.note: Strengthened with ни малейшего (not the faintest)

variations.ru: Они не имеют понятия об этом.
variations.note: Adding об этом (about it)

options.note: The reordered version — far more common in speech
The shortest colloquial form, with no verb at all

paraphrases.simplest: Понятия не имею. — this word order is the set phrase in speech.

takeaway.pattern: Понятия не имею (I haven't the faintest idea: a fixed phrase)
takeaway.note: Speech generally avoids иметь in favour of у меня есть, but it survives in idioms like this one.

keyPoint: Долгий is an adjective meaning "long" (in time).

grammarFocus.construction: провести (perfective past plural провели) + accusative (долгий вечер) + adverb вместе
grammarFocus.note: провести means 'to spend' of time. долгий is 'long' of duration, as against длинный for physical length.

variations.note: First person plural subject

variations.ru: Они провели долгий день в дороге.
variations.note: A different object and setting

options.note: Using пройти with вечер as the subject
Using весь вечер (all evening), simpler

paraphrases.simplest: Они провели вечер вместе. — dropping долгий is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: долгий (long in time) / длинный (long in space)
takeaway.note: долгий разговор (a long conversation), длинная дорога (a long road).

keyPoint: Скорый is an adjective meaning "soon, upcoming."

grammarFocus.construction: ждать (imperfective present 3pl ждут) + genitive (скорой встречи)
grammarFocus.note: ждать can take an abstract object in the genitive (ждать встречи). скорый means 'soon, imminent', and its feminine singular genitive is скорой.

variations.note: With a masculine noun: скорого ответа
A different subject and modifier

options.note: Using надеяться with увидеться (they hope to meet soon)
The set parting phrase (see you soon)

paraphrases.simplest: Они ждут встречи. — dropping скорой is shortest.

takeaway.note: ждать автобус (wait for the bus: accusative), ждать помощи (await help: genitive). До скорой встречи! is the standard farewell.

keyPoint: Питер is a colloquial nickname for St. Petersburg.

replies.gloss: I want to go there too.

grammarFocus.construction: ехать (imperfective present 1sg еду) + в + accusative (Питер) + time adverb завтра
grammarFocus.note: The imperfective present can express a near-future plan (еду завтра = I'm going tomorrow). Питер is the familiar nickname for St Petersburg.

variations.note: The perfective future поеду sounds slightly more settled
A different subject and destination: едем

options.note: Dropping the verb and using the prepositional (tomorrow I'm in Petersburg)

options.ru: У меня завтра поездка в Питер.
options.note: Using the noun поездка (trip)

paraphrases.simplest: Я завтра в Питер. — dropping the verb is the natural spoken form.

takeaway.pattern: the imperfective present for the near future (Я еду завтра)
takeaway.note: Just like the English present continuous, and especially common with motion verbs (ехать, идти, лететь).

keyPoint: Пропустить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "missing" something (pairs with пропускать).

grammarFocus.construction: negation не + хотеть (1sg хочу) + perfective infinitive (пропустить) + accusative (урок)
grammarFocus.note: пропустить means 'to miss' a lesson or event. A negative intention is expressed with не хочу plus an infinitive.

variations.note: A different object: I don't want to miss the meeting
First person plural: не хотим

options.note: Stated positively with обязательно приду (I'll definitely come)
Using нельзя with an imperfective infinitive (I mustn't miss lessons)

paraphrases.simplest: Я не хочу пропустить урок. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: пропустить урок (miss one lesson), не пропускать занятия (not miss classes). After нельзя the imperfective is the rule.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, prepositional, the target word

keyPoint: Здоровье is a neuter noun meaning "health."

grammarFocus.construction: заботиться (imperfective present 3pl заботятся) + о + prepositional (здоровье)
grammarFocus.note: заботиться means 'to take care of' and takes о + prepositional. здоровье is a -ье neuter noun whose prepositional stays здоровье.

variations.note: First person singular: забочусь
A different object: the prepositional plural детях

options.note: Using следить за + instrumental (they watch their health)

options.ru: Для них здоровье на первом месте.
options.note: Using на первом месте (health comes first for them)

paraphrases.simplest: Они заботятся о здоровье. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: заботиться о семье (look after the family). беспокоиться о + prepositional (worry about) takes the same case.

keyPoint: Выход is a masculine noun meaning "exit."

grammarFocus.construction: показать (perfective past plural показали) + accusative (выход) + dative (гостям)
grammarFocus.note: показать takes the thing shown in the accusative and the person shown in the dative. выход is masculine, so its accusative matches the nominative.

variations.note: With the first person plural dative
A different object: he showed them the way

options.note: Using проводить к + dative (they saw the guests to the exit)
Using объяснить with an indirect question

paraphrases.simplest: Они показали гостям выход. — the reordered version is just as natural.

takeaway.pattern: показать + accusative + dative (show something to someone)
takeaway.note: показать фотографию другу (show a photo to a friend). дать, сказать and объяснить follow the same pattern.

keyPoint: Свидетель is a masculine noun meaning "witness."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + adjective единственный + predicate noun (свидетель)
grammarFocus.note: единственный means 'the only'. свидетель is a masculine -ь noun; the feminine is свидетельница.

variations.note: To a woman: единственная свидетельница
Plural: единственные свидетели

options.note: Using кроме + genitive (no one but you saw it)
Using один (you alone saw it), simpler

paraphrases.simplest: Ты единственный свидетель. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: единственный шанс (the only chance). один counts; единственный stresses that there is no other.

keyPoint: Святой is an adjective meaning "holy, sacred."

grammarFocus.construction: считать (3pl считают) + accusative (этот день) + instrumental (святым)
grammarFocus.note: считать means 'consider X to be Y', with an accusative and an instrumental. святой is an adjective whose masculine singular instrumental is святым.

variations.note: With a feminine noun: святой as the feminine instrumental
A different instrumental: I consider the day special

options.note: A more natural version with для + genitive and a nominative predicate
Using the short form свят, rather literary

paraphrases.simplest: Для них это святой день. — the для construction is easier to follow.

takeaway.pattern: считать + accusative + instrumental (consider X to be Y)
takeaway.note: считать его другом (consider him a friend). The instrumental predicate is shared with назвать and называть.

keyPoint: Добраться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "reaching" a place (pairs with добираться).

replies.gloss: How long will the trip take?
I want to go with you.

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (3pl хотят) + perfective infinitive (добраться) + до + genitive (моря)
grammarFocus.note: добраться is a reflexive perfective meaning 'to get there, make it', with the destination in до + genitive.

variations.note: A different subject and destination: to get home
With доехать (to get there by vehicle)

options.note: Using попасть на + accusative (to get to the sea)
Using хочется with к + dative, verb dropped

paraphrases.simplest: Они хотят к морю. — dropping the verb is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: добраться до + genitive (make it as far as)
takeaway.note: добраться до работы (make it to work). The verb implies effort or a journey of some length.

keyPoint: Обнаружить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "discovering" (pairs with обнаруживать).

grammarFocus.construction: обнаружить (perfective past обнаружил) + accusative (ошибку)
grammarFocus.note: обнаружить means 'to detect, discover' and carries more of a sense of inspection than найти. The accusative of ошибка is ошибку.

variations.note: A female speaker says обнаружила
With a quantity phrase and the genitive plural

options.note: Using найти (to find), simpler
The shortest way to point it out, with no verb

paraphrases.simplest: Я нашёл ошибку. — найти is the everyday verb.

takeaway.note: обнаружить неисправность is technical; найти ключи (find your keys) is everyday.

skeleton.note: future 3rd person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Удаться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "working out" (pairs with удаваться).

grammarFocus.construction: надеяться (3pl надеются) + что clause + impersonal perfective future удастся
grammarFocus.note: удаться is an impersonal verb meaning 'to work out'. It takes no subject, and the person who succeeds can be named in the dative (нам удастся).

variations.note: First person singular: надеюсь

variations.ru: Они надеются, что им удастся договориться.
variations.note: Adding the dative им with an infinitive

options.note: Using надеяться на + accusative (they hope for success)
Using получится (it'll work out), softer

paraphrases.simplest: Надеюсь, всё получится. — получится is the natural spoken choice.

takeaway.pattern: удаться (work out: impersonal) / dative + удалось + infinitive
takeaway.note: Мне удалось найти (I managed to find it). A modest way of reporting success, often preferred to смог.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Сделка is a feminine noun meaning "deal, transaction."

grammarFocus.construction: обсуждать (3pl обсуждают) + accusative (сделку) + после + genitive (ужина)
grammarFocus.note: сделка is a feminine noun meaning 'deal', with the accusative сделку. после is a preposition taking the genitive.

variations.note: A different genitive: after work
The perfective обсудим makes it a single future act

options.ru: После ужина они говорят о сделке.
options.note: Using говорить о + prepositional with a reordered clause
An impersonal third person plural: the deal will be discussed later

paraphrases.simplest: Они обсуждают сделку после ужина. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: заключить сделку (close a deal), подписать договор (sign a contract). Worth keeping distinct in business contexts.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Благодарить is imperfective, meaning "to thank" (pairs with поблагодарить).

grammarFocus.construction: благодарить (1sg благодарю) + accusative (тебя) + за + accusative (всё)
grammarFocus.note: благодарить takes the person thanked in the accusative and the reason in за + accusative. It is more formal than спасибо.

variations.note: To a formal or plural addressee: вас
Dropping subject and object — formal but concise

options.note: Using спасибо + dative, everyday and warm
Using признателен (grateful), polite and formal

paraphrases.simplest: Спасибо за всё. — overwhelmingly the natural choice in speech.

takeaway.pattern: благодарить + accusative + за + accusative (thank someone for something)
takeaway.note: спасибо takes the dative (спасибо тебе), благодарить the accusative (благодарю тебя). Mind the difference.

keyPoint: Разный is an adjective meaning "different."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + intensifier очень + adjective разные + predicate noun (люди)
grammarFocus.note: разный means 'different, various'; in the plural разные it means 'different from each other'.

variations.note: With a third person plural subject
Recast with у + genitive: we see things differently

options.note: Using не похожи (we're not alike at all)
Using мало общего (we have little in common)

paraphrases.simplest: Мы очень разные. — dropping люди is shortest.

takeaway.note: разные люди (people who differ from each other), другие люди (other people). One marks difference, the other separateness.

keyPoint: Удар is a masculine noun meaning "a blow, strike."

grammarFocus.construction: видеть (perfective past plural видели) + accusative (сильный удар) + в + prepositional (боксе)
grammarFocus.note: удар is a masculine noun meaning 'blow', so its accusative matches the nominative. в боксе names the field in the prepositional.

variations.ru: Они видели сильный удар в хоккее.
variations.note: A different field: in hockey

variations.ru: Мы видели этот удар по телевизору.
variations.note: Using по + dative for the medium

options.note: Using the set phrase нанести удар (to land a blow)
With an instrumental predicate (the blow was very hard)

paraphrases.simplest: Они видели сильный удар. — в боксе can be dropped.

takeaway.pattern: нанести удар (land a blow: a fixed verb-noun pairing)
takeaway.note: удар takes its own verb нанести, and the target goes in по + dative (удар по столу).

keyPoint: Настолько is a degree adverb meaning "so, to such an extent."

replies.gloss: What tired them out so much?

grammarFocus.construction: intensifier настолько + устать (perfective past устали) + что clause + молчать (3pl молчат)
grammarFocus.note: настолько... что... links degree to result: 'so ... that ...'. так... что... means the same but is more colloquial.

variations.note: With так, more colloquial

variations.ru: Я настолько устал, что не могу говорить.
variations.note: First person singular subject

options.ru: Они устали до такой степени, что молчат.
options.note: Using до такой степени (to such a degree), formal
Using от + genitive (from exhaustion)

paraphrases.simplest: Они так устали, что молчат. — так is the natural spoken choice.

takeaway.note: так belongs to speech, настолько to writing. A comma always precedes the result clause.

keyPoint: Либо is a disjunctive conjunction meaning "or"; либо...либо means "either...or."

replies.gloss: Why does it have to be that way?

grammarFocus.construction: conjunction либо ... либо ... (either/or) + nominative (ты / я)
grammarFocus.note: либо... либо... marks an exclusive choice. или... или... means the same but sounds less formal.

variations.note: With или... или..., more colloquial
With time adverbs: now or never

options.note: Using один из нас (one of the two of us)
Adding выбирай (choose) to press the point

paraphrases.simplest: Или ты, или я. — или is the natural spoken choice.

takeaway.note: либо is the bookish option. то ли ... то ли ... is a separate pair expressing uncertainty.

keyPoint: Очевидно is a parenthetical adverb of certainty meaning "obviously, clearly."

grammarFocus.construction: parenthetical adverb очевидно + perfective past (устал)
grammarFocus.note: очевидно means 'evidently' and conveys the speaker's judgement of the whole sentence. As a parenthetical it can take commas (Ты, очевидно, устал).

variations.note: To a female listener: устала, with the commas
Formal or plural: устали

options.note: Using видно, что (one can see that)
Using кажется (apparently), a softer guess

paraphrases.simplest: Ты, видно, устал. — видно is more colloquial and natural.

takeaway.pattern: очевидно / видно / кажется (evidently, apparently, it seems)
takeaway.note: Confidence runs очевидно > видно > кажется. As parentheticals they take commas on both sides.

keyPoint: Куча is a feminine noun meaning "a pile, heap"; colloquially it also means "a lot of."

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + quantity noun куча + genitive plural (дел)
grammarFocus.note: куча literally means 'a heap'; colloquially it works as a quantity noun meaning 'loads of', and it takes the genitive.

variations.note: With an uncountable noun: the genitive singular работы
A different owner and noun: the genitive plural проблем

options.note: Using много, neutral
The idiom по уши (up to my ears in things to do)

paraphrases.simplest: У меня много дел. — the neutral option.

takeaway.note: куча дел (heaps to do), масса людей (masses of people), море времени (oceans of time). All take the genitive.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Шутка is a feminine noun meaning "joke."

grammarFocus.construction: рассказать (perfective past plural рассказали) + accusative (смешную шутку, feminine singular accusative)
grammarFocus.note: шутка is a feminine noun meaning 'joke', with the accusative шутку. смешной means 'funny'.

variations.note: A different noun: a funny story
With a masculine noun: смешной анекдот

options.note: Using пошутить (to crack a joke) with an adverb
Using рассмешить (to make laugh) with шутка as subject

paraphrases.simplest: Они рассказали смешную шутку. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: рассказать шутку / анекдот (tell a joke or a funny story)
takeaway.note: шутка is a quip, анекдот a story with a punchline. The verb шутить (to joke) is equally common.

keyPoint: Заставлять is imperfective, meaning "to force/make someone" (pairs with заставить).

grammarFocus.construction: negation не + хотеть (3pl хотят) + imperfective infinitive (заставлять) + accusative (тебя) + infinitive (ждать)
grammarFocus.note: заставлять means 'to make someone do something' and takes an accusative plus an infinitive: заставлять тебя ждать is 'keep you waiting'.

variations.ru: Я не хочу заставлять тебя ждать.
variations.note: First person singular subject
The perfective заставили makes it a single past act

options.ru: Они не хотят, чтобы ты ждал.
options.note: Using a чтобы clause with a past form
Using как можно быстрее (as fast as they can), stated positively

paraphrases.simplest: Они не хотят тебя задерживать. — задерживать is shorter.

takeaway.pattern: заставлять / заставить + accusative + infinitive (make someone do)
takeaway.note: Он заставил меня ждать (he kept me waiting). просить and позволить take the same accusative-plus-infinitive frame.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Половина is a feminine noun meaning "half."

grammarFocus.construction: давай + perfective future 1pl (возьмём) + the accusative quantity noun половину + genitive (торта)
grammarFocus.note: половина is a feminine noun meaning 'half'; its accusative is половину, and what it is half of goes in the genitive.

variations.note: A different genitive: half a pizza
Formal or plural with целый (a whole cake)

options.note: Using the adverb пополам (split it in half)
Using хватит + genitive (half will be enough for us)

paraphrases.simplest: Давай возьмём полторта. — the compound полторта also works.

takeaway.pattern: половина + genitive (half of) / пол- + genitive (полчаса, полгода)
takeaway.note: половина группы (half the group). The prefix пол- builds compounds: полдня (half a day), полкилограмма (half a kilo).

skeleton.note: neuter noun, plural, the target word

keyPoint: Доказательство is a neuter noun meaning "evidence, proof."

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (тебя) + есть + nominative plural (доказательства) + question intonation
grammarFocus.note: In an у existential sentence есть can be stated explicitly. доказательство is a -ство neuter noun whose nominative plural is доказательства.

variations.note: To a formal or plural addressee: у вас
In the singular: доказательство

options.note: Using доказать in the future — more of a challenge
Using есть чем + infinitive (anything to back it up?), colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Доказательства есть? — the reordered two-word version is shortest.

takeaway.note: All neuter, with -ства in the nominative plural. They are often built from verbs: доказать gives доказательство.

keyPoint: Бизнес is a masculine noun meaning "business."

grammarFocus.construction: давай + perfective future 1pl (обсудим) + accusative (бизнес) + за + instrumental (кофе)
grammarFocus.note: за + instrumental means 'over' something (за кофе = over coffee). кофе is indeclinable, so its form never changes.

variations.note: A different instrumental: over lunch
Formal or plural with чай (over tea)

options.note: Using поговорить о + prepositional

options.ru: Как насчёт кофе и разговора о делах?
options.note: Using как насчёт + genitive (how about coffee and some business talk?)

paraphrases.simplest: Обсудим за кофе. — dropping давай and the object is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: за + instrumental (over: за кофе, за обедом, за работой)
takeaway.note: It describes doing something while eating or working. за столом (at the table) is the same pattern.

keyPoint: Обязательно is an adverb meaning "definitely, without fail."

grammarFocus.construction: adverb обязательно + perfective future 1sg (приду)
grammarFocus.note: обязательно means 'definitely' and strengthens a promise. The future of прийти has a changed stem: приду, придёшь.

variations.note: First person plural: придём
A different verb: I'll definitely call

options.note: Using точно (for sure), near-identical
Using рассчитывать на + accusative (you can count on me)

paraphrases.simplest: Обязательно приду. — dropping the subject sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: the future of прийти (приду, придёшь, придёт, придут)
takeaway.note: An irregular stem from the идти family. обязательно, точно and непременно all mean 'definitely'.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Отель is a masculine noun meaning "hotel."

grammarFocus.construction: давай + perfective future 1pl (забронируем) + accusative (отель) + на + accusative (выходные)
grammarFocus.note: на + accusative marks the period something is for (на выходные = for the weekend). выходные is an adjectival noun used in the plural.

variations.ru: Давай забронируем отель на три ночи.
variations.note: Specifying the stay with на + accusative
Formal or plural with столик (a table for the evening)

options.note: Using снять (to take, rent)
Using заказать (to book) with онлайн

paraphrases.simplest: Давай забронируем отель. — dropping на выходные is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: на + accusative (for a period or purpose)
takeaway.note: на выходные (for the weekend), на неделю (for a week), на двоих (for two). An essential phrase pattern.

keyPoint: Дама is a somewhat formal feminine noun meaning "lady."

grammarFocus.construction: demonstrative эта + noun (дама) + intensifier очень + adjective predicate (красивая)
grammarFocus.note: дама is a somewhat formal feminine noun for a lady. The demonstrative эта and the predicate красивая both agree in the feminine singular.

variations.note: With a masculine noun: этот красивый
Plural: эти красивые

options.note: An exclamation with какой, more heartfelt
Using the noun красавица (a real beauty)

paraphrases.simplest: Эта дама очень красивая. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: дама (lady: formal) / женщина (woman: neutral) / девушка (young woman)
takeaway.note: дама suits social settings and card games (дама = queen). Everyday Russian uses женщина or девушка.

keyPoint: Занять is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "occupying" time (pairs with занимать).

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal можно + perfective infinitive (занять) + accusative (время) + instrumental (настольной игрой)
grammarFocus.note: занять means 'to fill, occupy' and names the means in the instrumental. настольная игра (board game) gives the instrumental настольной игрой.

variations.note: A different instrumental: fill the time with a book
With a person as object: keep the children occupied with a game

options.note: Using играть в + accusative — far more natural
Using заняться + instrumental (what shall we do while we wait?)

paraphrases.simplest: Давай поиграем в настольную игру. — the natural spoken version.

takeaway.pattern: занять + accusative + instrumental (fill or occupy with)
takeaway.note: занять ребёнка игрой (keep a child busy with a game). Note the contrast with играть в + accusative.

keyPoint: Немедленно is an adverb meaning "immediately."

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective imperative (приходи) + directional adverb сюда + adverb немедленно
grammarFocus.note: сюда means 'to here' (здесь is 'here' as a location). немедленно means 'immediately' and lends the command urgency.

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener
With the imperative of идти, shorter and sharper

options.note: No verb at all — the most urgent version
Using сейчас же (right now)

paraphrases.simplest: Иди сюда сейчас же! — the natural spoken version.

takeaway.note: The same split runs through там/туда and где/куда. немедленно, сейчас же and срочно all mean 'at once'.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, plural accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Наркотик is a masculine noun meaning "drug, narcotic."

grammarFocus.construction: читать (imperfective past читали) + accusative (роман) + про + accusative (наркотики)
grammarFocus.note: про is a colloquial preposition meaning 'about' and takes the accusative. наркотики is normally used in the plural.

variations.note: To someone you address as ты: ты читал
With о + prepositional and a different topic

options.ru: Вы читали эту книгу о наркотиках?
options.note: With о + prepositional and книга, closer to written style
Using знаком + dative (are you familiar with this novel?)

paraphrases.simplest: Вы читали этот роман? — про наркотики can be dropped.

takeaway.note: книга про войну (colloquial) versus книга о войне (standard). про is extremely frequent in speech.

skeleton.note: future 1st person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Отправиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "setting off" (pairs with отправляться).

grammarFocus.construction: time adverb завтра + отправиться (perfective future 1sg отправлюсь) + directional adverb домой
grammarFocus.note: отправиться is a reflexive perfective meaning 'to set off', somewhat formal. домой is a directional adverb taking no preposition.

variations.note: First person plural: отправимся
With в + accusative naming the destination

options.note: The present of уезжать expressing the near future
Using ехать — the most everyday version

paraphrases.simplest: Завтра я еду домой. — the natural spoken version.

takeaway.note: отправиться в путь (set out on a journey) is literary. Speech prefers поехать or уехать.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, instrumental, the target word

keyPoint: Удовольствие is a neuter noun meaning "pleasure," frequent in the fixed phrase с удовольствием ("gladly").

grammarFocus.construction: с + instrumental (удовольствием) + perfective future 1sg (помогу)
grammarFocus.note: с удовольствием ('with pleasure') is a fixed с + instrumental phrase, and the standard way to accept a request.

variations.note: First person plural: поможем
With с радостью (gladly), near-identical

options.note: Using конечно (of course) — the shortest acceptance
Using рад + infinitive (I'd be glad to help)

paraphrases.simplest: С удовольствием. — two words accept the request.

takeaway.pattern: с + instrumental (с удовольствием, с радостью, с трудом)
takeaway.note: с удовольствием (gladly), с трудом (with difficulty). A handy way to express manner.

keyPoint: Способный is an adjective meaning "capable, talented."

replies.gloss: What are you especially good at?

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + intensifier очень + adjective способный + predicate noun (ученик)
grammarFocus.note: способный means 'able, gifted', and also governs к + dative (способный к языкам, good at languages).

variations.note: Feminine: способная ученица
Plural: способные ученики

options.note: Using the noun способности (abilities)
Using схватывать (you pick things up fast), more concrete

paraphrases.simplest: Ты очень способный. — ученик can be dropped.

takeaway.note: способный ученик (a gifted pupil), Он способен на всё (he's capable of anything). The short form shifts the meaning.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, prepositional, the target word

keyPoint: Служба is a feminine noun meaning "service, duty (work-related)."

grammarFocus.construction: давай + perfective future 1pl (поговорим) + о + prepositional (службе)
grammarFocus.note: служба is a many-sided feminine noun — duty, military service, a church service — with the prepositional службе. поговорить means to have a talk.

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener: давайте
With работа (work), more everyday

options.note: Using рассказать о + prepositional (tell me about your service)
Using как у тебя с + instrumental (how are things at work?), colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Поговорим о службе. — давай can be dropped and it still invites.

takeaway.note: военная служба (military service), служба поддержки (support desk), церковная служба (a church service). Context decides.

keyPoint: Вытащить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "pulling out" (pairs with вытаскивать).

grammarFocus.construction: помочь (perfective imperative помоги) + dative (мне) + perfective infinitive (вытащить) + accusative (это)
grammarFocus.note: помочь takes the person helped in the dative and the task in an infinitive. вытащить is the perfective 'to pull out'.

variations.note: Asking a formal or plural addressee: помогите
A different infinitive: help me lift it

options.note: Using подержать (hold it) to split the job
Using нужна with помощь (I need your help)

paraphrases.simplest: Помоги вытащить. — dropping мне and это is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: помочь + dative + infinitive (help someone do something)
takeaway.note: Помоги мне понять (help me understand). помочь takes the dative, not the accusative.

keyPoint: Наконец is an adverb meaning "finally, at last."

grammarFocus.construction: adverb наконец + perfective past (пришёл) + exclamatory intonation
grammarFocus.note: наконец means 'at last' and marks arrival after a long wait. наконец-то adds more feeling.

variations.note: To a female listener: пришла
Formal or plural: пришли

options.note: With наконец-то and здесь, warmer
Using заждаться (I'd given up waiting)

paraphrases.simplest: Наконец-то! — one word carries the relief.

takeaway.pattern: наконец / наконец-то (at last: -то heightens the feeling)
takeaway.note: в конце концов means 'after all, in the end' and introduces a conclusion — a different thing entirely.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Уезжать is imperfective, meaning "to leave/depart" (pairs with уехать).

grammarFocus.construction: уезжать (imperfective present 1sg уезжаю) + time adverb завтра + instrumental time adverb (утром)
grammarFocus.note: The imperfective present expresses a near-future plan. Parts of the day take a bare instrumental: утром, днём, вечером.

variations.note: A different instrumental: tomorrow evening
First person plural: уезжаем

options.ru: Завтра утром меня здесь не будет.
options.note: Using не будет (I won't be here) to say it indirectly
The perfective уеду makes the plan sound more settled

paraphrases.simplest: Я уезжаю завтра утром. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: Я уезжаю (I'm off, I'm due to leave) versus Я уехал (I've gone). Motion verbs use the present for the near future.

keyPoint: Девчонка is a colloquial feminine noun meaning "girl."

replies.gloss: Have you talked to her yet?

grammarFocus.construction: demonstrative эта + noun (девчонка) + dative (мне) + нравиться (3sg нравится)
grammarFocus.note: нравиться means 'to please': the thing liked is the subject and the person liking it goes in the dative. девчонка is a colloquial, affectionate form of девочка.

variations.note: With a masculine noun: этот парень
Plural subject takes нравятся

options.note: Using симпатична + dative (I find her likeable), more restrained
Using неравнодушен к + dative (I'm not indifferent to her), indirect

paraphrases.simplest: Она мне нравится. — dropping эта and девчонка is shortest.

takeaway.note: Subject and object are the reverse of English. Мне нравятся эти книги (I like these books — plural, so нравятся).

keyPoint: Защита is a feminine noun meaning "protection, defense."

replies.gloss: What do you need protecting from?

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + short form нужна + nominative (твоя защита)
grammarFocus.note: нужен agrees with the thing needed. защита is feminine, hence нужна, and the possessive твоя agrees too.

variations.note: With a masculine noun: нужен
With the first person plural dative

options.note: Using the imperative of защитить (protect me), more direct
Using без + genitive (I can't manage without you)

paraphrases.simplest: Мне нужна твоя защита. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: dative + нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны + nominative
takeaway.note: The thing needed is the subject, so нужен agrees with it: Мне нужны деньги (I need money).

skeleton.note: masculine noun, prepositional, the target word

keyPoint: Бар is a masculine noun meaning "bar."

grammarFocus.construction: встретиться (perfective future 1pl встретимся) + в + prepositional (баре) + instrumental time adverb (вечером)
grammarFocus.note: встретимся is the standard 'let's meet'. The place takes в + prepositional and the time an instrumental adverb; давай is optional.

variations.note: Adding давай makes the invitation explicit
With у + genitive and в + accusative for place and time

options.note: Using ждать + accusative (I'll be waiting for you)
Using как насчёт + genitive (how about the bar tonight?)

paraphrases.simplest: Встретимся вечером в баре. — the reordered version is just as natural.

takeaway.pattern: the perfective future 1pl as an invitation (Встретимся! Пойдём! Начнём!)
takeaway.note: Even without давай it means 'let's ...'. The most compact way Russian makes a suggestion.

keyPoint: Штат is a masculine noun meaning "state" (as in a U.S. state).

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal можно + perfective infinitive (выбрать) + accusative (штат) + для + genitive (поездки)
grammarFocus.note: для + genitive expresses purpose. штат is a masculine noun for an American state, with the accusative the same as the nominative.

variations.note: A different object: a city for the trip
A different purpose: a state to work in

options.note: A direct question with в + accusative, far more natural
Using куда with an infinitive

paraphrases.simplest: В какой штат поедем? — the natural spoken version.

takeaway.note: для поездки (for the trip), для работы (for work). чтобы + infinitive builds a purpose clause instead.

keyPoint: Абсолютно is an intensifying adverb meaning "absolutely."

grammarFocus.construction: intensifier абсолютно + short-form predicate (уверен)
grammarFocus.note: абсолютно is the loanword 'absolutely', close to полностью and совершенно. уверен is a predicate-only short form.

variations.note: A female speaker says уверена
A plural subject takes уверены

options.note: Using the negation of сомневаться (I have no doubt)
Using сто процентов (a hundred per cent), colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Абсолютно уверен. — dropping the subject is shortest.

takeaway.note: Я уверен в себе (I'm confident), Я уверен в этом (I'm sure of it). абсолютно, полностью and совершенно all intensify it.

keyPoint: Действовать is a stative/durative imperfective verb; the related подействовать means "to take effect/act for a while," a distinct sense.

replies.gloss: Agreed, there's no time to wait.

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal надо + imperfective infinitive (действовать) + manner adverb быстро
grammarFocus.note: действовать means 'to act, to take effect' and has no perfective partner. надо + infinitive states an obligation with no subject.

variations.note: The dative нам names who must act
For the past tense add было

options.note: Using срочно with делать (we must do something urgently)
The idiom время не ждёт (time won't wait)

paraphrases.simplest: Надо действовать быстро. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: действовать (act, take effect: no perfective partner)
takeaway.note: Лекарство действует (the medicine is working), действовать по плану (act according to plan). For a single act use поступить.

skeleton.note: future 1st person plural, the target word

keyPoint: Собраться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "gathering" (pairs with собираться).

grammarFocus.construction: давай + perfective future 1pl (соберёмся) + в + accusative clock time (семь)
grammarFocus.note: собраться is a reflexive perfective meaning 'to gather'. Clock times take в + accusative (в семь = at seven).

variations.note: Formal or plural: давайте
With у + genitive for the place (at my place)

options.note: Using встретиться (let's all meet)
Using the noun сбор (assembly at seven), notice-style

paraphrases.simplest: Собираемся в семь. — the imperfective present works as a plan too.

takeaway.note: Мы собрались (we gathered) versus Он собрал нас (he gathered us). собраться + infinitive also means 'intend to'.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Приезжать is imperfective, meaning "to come (by vehicle)" (pairs with приехать).

grammarFocus.construction: frequency adverb часто + приезжать (imperfective present 2sg приезжаешь) + directional adverb сюда
grammarFocus.note: приезжать is the imperfective 'to come by vehicle', used for repeated visits. сюда means 'to here'.

variations.note: To a formal or plural addressee: приезжаете
With приходить (to come on foot)

options.note: Using бывать (do you come here often?)
Using обычное место (is this your usual spot?)

paraphrases.simplest: Часто здесь бываешь? — бываешь is the natural spoken choice.

takeaway.pattern: приезжать (come by vehicle) / приходить (come on foot)
takeaway.note: The verb changes with the means of travel; приехать and прийти are the matching perfectives.

keyPoint: Слава is a feminine noun meaning "glory, fame," frequent in the fixed phrase слава богу ("thank goodness").

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal надо + perfective infinitive (сказать) + colon + parenthetical слава богу + zero copula (всё хорошо)
grammarFocus.note: слава богу ('thank goodness') is a fixed phrase in which богу is dative. Inside a sentence it is set off by commas.

variations.note: Starting with the parenthetical — the commonest form
With к счастью (fortunately), without the religious flavour

options.note: Using обошлось (it all turned out fine)
Using в порядке (everything's in order)

paraphrases.simplest: Слава богу, всё хорошо. — dropping the first clause sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: слава богу (thank goodness: богу is a fixed dative)
takeaway.note: не дай бог (heaven forbid) and дай бог (God grant) follow the same pattern. The religious sense has faded; they're ordinary parentheticals now.

keyPoint: Переживать is imperfective, denoting the general state of worrying, with no true perfective counterpart; попереживать exists as a delimitative meaning "to worry for a while," not a true pair.

grammarFocus.construction: negated imperfective imperative (не переживай) + за + accusative (меня)
grammarFocus.note: переживать means 'to worry' and takes за + accusative. Prohibitions and reassurances use the imperfective imperative.

variations.note: Formal or plural: не переживайте
A different object: don't worry about them

options.note: Using волноваться о + prepositional (don't worry about me)
Reassuring with со мной всё будет хорошо (I'll be fine)

paraphrases.simplest: Не переживай. — dropping за меня is shortest.

takeaway.note: волноваться о and беспокоиться о also mean 'worry'. переживать sounds the most emotionally involved.

keyPoint: Лето is a neuter noun meaning "summer."

grammarFocus.construction: instrumental time adverb летом + ездить (imperfective present 1sg езжу) + на + accusative (море)
grammarFocus.note: летом means 'in summer'. ездить is the multidirectional motion verb, right for repeated round trips — going to the sea every year.

variations.note: A different season and destination: to the mountains in winter
First person plural: ездим

options.note: Dropping the verb and using the prepositional for the state
Using отдыхать у + genitive (I holiday by the sea)

paraphrases.simplest: Летом я езжу на море. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: ездить (multidirectional, repeated) / ехать (one direction, this time)
takeaway.note: Я езжу на море каждый год (I go to the sea every year) versus Я еду на море (I'm on my way there now).

keyPoint: Известно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it is known."

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal можно + perfective infinitive (проверить) + indirect question (известно ли расписание)
grammarFocus.note: The particle ли forms an indirect yes-no question. With no question word, ли goes straight after the word being checked (известно ли).

variations.note: With ли on a different word: whether the order is ready
With the imperative of узнать (find out)

options.note: A direct question — the shortest version
Using новости о + prepositional (any news on the timetable?)

paraphrases.simplest: Расписание уже известно? — asking directly is most natural.

takeaway.pattern: the particle ли in indirect questions (whether)
takeaway.note: Я не знаю, придёт ли он (I don't know whether he'll come). ли always follows the word in question.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Роль is a feminine noun meaning "role."

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal можно + perfective infinitive (выбрать) + accusative (роль) + в + prepositional (игре)
grammarFocus.note: роль is a feminine -ь noun, so its accusative matches the nominative. в игре gives the setting in the prepositional.

variations.note: A different setting: a part in a film
With поменять (change roles)

options.note: Using играть за + accusative (who can you play as?), gamer phrasing
Using персонажи (what characters are there?)

paraphrases.simplest: Можно выбрать роль? — в игре can be dropped.

takeaway.pattern: играть роль (play a part) / играть за + accusative (play as)
takeaway.note: роль в игре (a role in the game), главная роль (the lead). играть в + accusative means playing a game, a different pattern.

keyPoint: Нечего is a negative pronoun meaning "nothing to," used together with an infinitive.

replies.ru: Это всё, что нужно было сказать.
replies.gloss: That's all that needed to be said.

grammarFocus.construction: можно + perfective infinitive (сказать) + colon + negative pronoun нечего + perfective infinitive (добавить)
grammarFocus.note: нечего means 'there is nothing to' and pairs with an infinitive: нечего добавить (there's nothing to add).

variations.note: With the dative мне naming the person
A different infinitive: we have nothing to hide

options.note: Adding больше (there's nothing more to say)
Using это всё (that's all) — the shortest option

paraphrases.simplest: Нечего добавить. — dropping the first clause sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: нечего / некого / негде + infinitive (there's nothing, no one, nowhere to ...)
takeaway.note: нечего делать (nothing to do), некого спросить (no one to ask), негде сесть (nowhere to sit). The stress falls on не-.

keyPoint: Поиск is a masculine noun meaning "search."

replies.gloss: Did you find what you were looking for?

grammarFocus.construction: nominative (поиск) + занять (perfective past занял) + accusative (целый день)
grammarFocus.note: занять means 'to take' of time, with the duration in the accusative. целый means 'a whole'.

variations.note: A different duration: two hours
With a feminine noun: целую неделю

options.note: Using искать with весь день, making the searchers the subject
Using уйти на + accusative (a whole day went on the search)

paraphrases.simplest: Поиск занял целый день. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: Это займёт пять минут (that'll take five minutes). The duration is a bare accusative.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, genitive, the target word

keyPoint: Покой is a masculine noun meaning "peace, calm."

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (1sg хочу) + quantity adverb немного + genitive (покоя)
grammarFocus.note: немного means 'a little' and takes the genitive. покой is a masculine noun meaning peace or calm, with the genitive покоя.

variations.note: A different genitive: a little quiet
A different subject and genitive: a little rest

options.note: Using the set phrase оставить в покое (leave me alone)
Using нужна with тишина (I need quiet)

paraphrases.simplest: Хочу покоя. — dropping немного is shortest.

takeaway.note: немного воды (a little water), много времени (a lot of time). оставить в покое is a fixed prepositional phrase.

keyPoint: Съесть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "eating (all of)" something (pairs with есть/съедать).

grammarFocus.construction: мочь (1sg могу) + perfective infinitive (съесть) + accusative (всё)
grammarFocus.note: съесть is the perfective of есть and means eating something up. мочь plus an infinitive expresses ability or possibility.

variations.note: A more specific object: the whole pizza
First person plural: можем

options.note: Using голоден (I'm starving) to state the reason
The hyperbole съесть слона (I could eat an elephant)

paraphrases.simplest: Я могу съесть всё. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: Я ел суп (I was eating soup) versus Я съел суп (I finished the soup). The perfective implies it's all gone.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Называться is an imperfective verb meaning "to be called," a stative sense; the related назваться mostly means "to identify oneself by name."

grammarFocus.construction: давай + perfective future 1pl (узнаем) + indirect question (как называется кафе)
grammarFocus.note: называться is the reflexive verb for what a thing or place is called. For people's names Russian uses звать instead.

variations.note: A different object: the name of the street
As a direct question

options.note: Using что это за + nominative (what sort of cafe is this?), colloquial
Using название (look up the cafe's name)

paraphrases.simplest: Как называется это кафе? — asking directly is most natural.

takeaway.pattern: называться (names of things) / звать (names of people)
takeaway.note: Как называется этот город? versus Как тебя зовут? The verb depends on what is being named.

keyPoint: Приказ is a masculine noun meaning "order, command."

replies.ru: Что будет, если его не выполнить?
replies.gloss: What happens if it's not followed?

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal нельзя + imperfective infinitive (игнорировать) + accusative (приказ)
grammarFocus.note: нельзя expresses prohibition with an imperfective infinitive ('you mustn't') and impossibility with a perfective one ('it can't be done').

variations.note: A different object: you mustn't ignore the rules
With the dative нам naming who is bound

options.note: Stated positively with надо выполнять (orders must be carried out)
Using не обсуждаются (orders are not up for discussion)

paraphrases.simplest: Нельзя игнорировать приказ. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: Здесь нельзя курить (no smoking) versus Это нельзя открыть (this can't be opened). The aspect decides the meaning.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Сомневаться is imperfective, meaning "to doubt" (pairs with усомниться).

grammarFocus.construction: в + prepositional (этом) + сомневаться (imperfective present 1sg сомневаюсь)
grammarFocus.note: сомневаться means 'to doubt' and takes в + prepositional, not an accusative object — a point worth fixing.

variations.note: A different prepositional: I doubt his words
First person plural: сомневаемся

options.note: Using кажется + instrumental (it strikes me as odd), indirect

options.ru: Я не очень верю в это.
options.note: Using the negation of верить в + accusative

paraphrases.simplest: Я сомневаюсь. — dropping в этом is shortest.

takeaway.note: уверен в + prepositional (be sure of) takes the same case, making the two a natural pair. Я не сомневаюсь (I have no doubt).

keyPoint: Многое is the neuter form of многий, used substantively to mean "many things."

grammarFocus.construction: the accusative pronoun многое + хотеть (1sg хочу) + perfective infinitive (сказать)
grammarFocus.note: многое means 'much, a great deal' and declines as a neuter adjective (многое / многого / о многом).

variations.note: A different verb: I understood a great deal
With о + prepositional: we talked about a lot

options.note: Using есть что + infinitive (I have things to say)
Using много вопросов (I have a lot of questions), more concrete

paraphrases.simplest: Мне есть что сказать. — the more natural spoken version.

takeaway.pattern: многое (a great deal: an adjectival pronoun)
takeaway.note: многое изменилось (much has changed), о многом (about many things). много is a separate word, a quantity adverb taking the genitive.

keyPoint: Сложно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's difficult."

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal можно + perfective infinitive (сделать) + accusative (паузу) + если clause + impersonal predicate сложно
grammarFocus.note: сделать паузу is the set phrase for taking a pause. сложно is a subjectless predicate meaning 'it's hard'.

variations.note: With перерыв (a break) and устал
With давай отдохнём (let's rest)

options.note: Using a dash for the condition, compact and colloquial
Using передохнуть (take a breather)

paraphrases.simplest: Если сложно, сделаем паузу. — dropping можно sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: сделать паузу / перерыв (take a pause or a break)
takeaway.note: сделать паузу is a break in speech or work; перерыв is a scheduled break. сложно and трудно are both impersonal 'it's hard'.

keyPoint: Блин originally means "pancake" but is also used as a mild interjection of surprise or frustration.

grammarFocus.construction: interjection Блин (set off by a comma) + adverb уже + place adverb здесь (zero copula)
grammarFocus.note: блин literally means 'pancake', but as an interjection it works as a mild oath — a stand-in for much coarser words.

variations.note: With a different clause: damn, I'm late
With чёрт (damn), a slightly stronger interjection

options.note: Using the particle да to convey irritation
Using же with говорю for emphasis

paraphrases.simplest: Я уже здесь. — dropping the interjection makes it neutral.

takeaway.note: чёрт, блин and ёлки-палки all stand in for coarser swearing. They are extremely common in speech.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Заботиться is imperfective, meaning "to take care of" (pairs with позаботиться).

grammarFocus.construction: заботиться (imperfective present 1sg забочусь) + о + prepositional (своей семье)
grammarFocus.note: заботиться means 'to take care of' and takes о + prepositional. The reflexive possessive свой points back to the subject, giving the feminine prepositional своей.

variations.note: Third person singular: заботится
A different object: the prepositional plural родителях

options.ru: Семья для меня на первом месте.
options.note: Using на первом месте (family comes first for me)
Using содержать (to support), narrowing it to money

paraphrases.simplest: Я забочусь о семье. — dropping своей is shortest.

takeaway.note: свой is used whenever the owner is the subject, and its form doesn't change with person: Я забочусь о своей семье / Он заботится о своей семье.

keyPoint: Лгать is imperfective, meaning "to lie" (pairs with солгать).

grammarFocus.construction: negation не + short form должен + dative (мне) + imperfective infinitive (лгать)
grammarFocus.note: не должен + infinitive means 'must not'. лгать takes the person lied to in the dative, hence мне.

variations.note: To a female listener: не должна
Formal or plural: не должны

options.note: Using the negated imperative of врать, more colloquial and direct
Stated positively: I want to hear the truth

paraphrases.simplest: Не ври мне. — overwhelmingly the natural choice in speech.

takeaway.pattern: лгать + dative (lie to someone) / не должен + infinitive
takeaway.note: лгать мне, врать мне — the person lied to is dative. должен is a short-form adjective agreeing with the subject.

skeleton.note: 1st person plural present, the target word

keyPoint: Убираться is imperfective, meaning "to clean up" (pairs with убраться).

grammarFocus.construction: time adverb сегодня + убираться (imperfective present 1pl убираемся) + adverb вместе
grammarFocus.note: убираться means 'to tidy up, clean' and is reflexive, taking no object. The transitive убирать needs one.

variations.note: First person singular: убираюсь
The transitive убирать takes an accusative object

options.note: Using the noun уборка (cleaning), more compact
Using the set phrase наводить порядок (put things in order)

paraphrases.simplest: Сегодня убираемся вместе. — the subject can be dropped.

takeaway.pattern: убираться (clean up: reflexive) / убирать + accusative (clear away: transitive)
takeaway.note: Я убираюсь (I'm cleaning) versus Я убираю со стола (I'm clearing the table). The -ся decides whether an object follows.

keyPoint: Спасть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "subsiding" (pairs with спадать).

grammarFocus.construction: заметить (perfective past plural заметили) + что clause + спасть (perfective past спал)
grammarFocus.note: спасть means 'to subside, drop' of water, noise or heat, and is somewhat literary. Its past спал looks exactly like the past of спать (to sleep), so context decides.

variations.note: A different subject: the heat has eased
To someone you address as ты: ты заметил

options.note: Using стать тише (it's got quieter), simpler
Using кажется with стало тише (it seems quieter)

paraphrases.simplest: Заметили, что стало тише? — тише is easier to follow.

takeaway.note: вода спала (the water went down), жара спала (the heat eased). Identical in the past to спать, so read the context.

keyPoint: Сумасшедший is an adjective meaning "crazy, insane."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the particle что (ты что = 'what on earth') + adjectival predicate noun (сумасшедший)
grammarFocus.note: Ты что...? is the set opener for astonishment or reproach. сумасшедший is a noun with adjective endings.

variations.note: To a female listener: сумасшедшая
Using the perfective past of сойти с ума (have you gone mad), stronger

options.note: The idiom в своём уме (are you in your right mind?)
Using серьёзно (seriously?), the mildest option

paraphrases.simplest: Ты серьёзно? — two words carry the disbelief.

takeaway.pattern: Ты что, ...? (what, are you ...?: astonishment or reproach)
takeaway.note: сумасшедший is an adjectival noun, feminine сумасшедшая. The verb phrase сойти с ума (go mad) is equally common.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, dative, the target word

keyPoint: Шеф is a masculine noun meaning "boss, chief."

grammarFocus.construction: adverb уже + позвонить (perfective past plural позвонили) + dative (шефу)
grammarFocus.note: звонить takes the person called in the dative. шеф means 'boss' and its dative is шефу.

variations.note: To someone you address as ты: ты уже позвонил
A different dative: called the director

options.note: Using в курсе (does the boss know?)
Using связаться с + instrumental (have you got through to him?)

paraphrases.simplest: Шефу звонили? — dropping the subject is shortest.

takeaway.note: позвонить маме (phone your mother). One of the dative verbs, along with помогать and доверять.

keyPoint: Ввиду is a preposition meaning "in view of, because of," combined with the genitive case.

grammarFocus.construction: preposition ввиду + genitive (этого) + perfective past (остались) + place adverb дома
grammarFocus.note: ввиду means 'in view of, owing to' and takes the genitive. It belongs to written and official style; speech uses из-за + genitive.

variations.note: A different genitive: owing to the weather
With из-за + genitive, more colloquial

options.note: Using поэтому (so), the plainest version

options.ru: В связи с этим мы остались дома.
options.note: Using в связи с + instrumental, formal

paraphrases.simplest: Поэтому мы остались дома. — the natural choice in speech.

takeaway.note: ввиду обстоятельств suits documents. Compare из-за (because of, often negative) and благодаря + dative (thanks to).

keyPoint: По-моему is a parenthetical adverb meaning "in my opinion."

grammarFocus.construction: parenthetical по-моему (set off by a comma) + zero copula + short-form predicate (готов)
grammarFocus.note: по-моему means 'in my view' and grew out of по- plus a dative. готов is a predicate-only short form.

variations.note: To a female listener: готова
With по-твоему (in your view)

options.note: Using я думаю, more explicit
Using мне кажется, more tentative

paraphrases.simplest: Думаю, ты готов. — two words do the same job.

takeaway.pattern: по-моему / по-твоему / по-вашему (in my, your view)
takeaway.note: As a parenthetical it takes commas. Note that по мне is a separate, colloquial expression meaning 'as for me'.

keyPoint: Связаться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting in touch" (pairs with связываться).

grammarFocus.construction: negation не + смочь (perfective past смог) + perfective infinitive (связаться) + с + instrumental (ним)
grammarFocus.note: связаться means 'to get in touch' and takes с + instrumental. не смог + infinitive reports one failed attempt.

variations.ru: Я не смогла с ним связаться.
variations.note: A female speaker says не смогла

variations.ru: Мы не смогли с ней связаться.
variations.note: First person plural, with a woman as the other party

options.note: Using не берёт телефон (he isn't answering), giving the reason
Using the negated infinitive of дозвониться (you can't get through to him)

paraphrases.simplest: Я не смог до него дозвониться. — clearer when the phone is meant.

takeaway.pattern: связаться с + instrumental (get in touch with)
takeaway.note: связаться по телефону (get in touch by phone). Same root as связь (connection) and связать (to tie).

keyPoint: Ух is an interjection of surprise or amazement.

grammarFocus.construction: сказать (perfective past plural сказали) + a quoted interjection («ух»)
grammarFocus.note: ух expresses surprise, admiration or weariness. A word in quotation marks doesn't decline — it stands in its base form as the object.

variations.note: To someone you address as ты: ты сказал
With ох (oh), a sigh

options.note: Using что-то (did you say something?), more neutral
Using вздохнуть (was that you sighing?)

paraphrases.simplest: Вы сказали «ух»? — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: quoted words do not decline (Он сказал «да»)
takeaway.note: ух, ох, ах and эх are all exclamatory interjections. A quoted word escapes the usual case government.

keyPoint: Выжить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "surviving" (pairs with выживать).

grammarFocus.construction: без + genitive (тебя) + negation не + смочь (future 1sg смогу) + perfective infinitive (выжить)
grammarFocus.note: без means 'without' and takes the genitive. выжить is the perfective 'to survive'.

variations.ru: Без вас я не смогу выжить.
variations.note: To a formal or plural addressee: без вас
A different genitive and subject: we won't survive without money

options.note: Using необходим + dative (I can't do without you)
The colloquial idiom без тебя никуда (I'm lost without you)

paraphrases.simplest: Без тебя мне не выжить. — the impersonal infinitive version is shorter.

takeaway.note: без воды (without water), без него (without him). One of the genitive prepositions, with для, до, около and после.

keyPoint: Уволить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "firing" someone (pairs with увольнять).

grammarFocus.construction: мочь (2pl можете) + perfective infinitive (уволить) + accusative (сотрудника, animate masculine = genitive form)
grammarFocus.note: уволить means 'to dismiss' and takes an accusative object. сотрудник is animate, so its accusative matches the genitive.

variations.note: With a pronoun object: can you dismiss her?
To someone you address as ты: ты можешь

options.note: Recast impersonally with можно + infinitive
Using the noun увольнение, formal and cautious

paraphrases.simplest: Его можно уволить? — the impersonal version is shorter.

takeaway.note: Его уволили (he was sacked) versus Он уволился (he resigned). The -ся marks whose decision it was.

skeleton.note: future 1st person plural, the target word

keyPoint: Постоять is perfective, a delimitative form of стоять meaning "to stand for a while."

replies.gloss: Okay, the view is nice here.

grammarFocus.construction: давай + perfective future 1pl (постоим) + quantity adverb немного + place adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: постоять means 'to stand for a while': the prefix по- bounds the action to a short stretch of time.

variations.note: Formal or plural: давайте
With посидеть (sit for a while)

options.note: Using подождать (let's wait a minute)
Using остановиться (let's stop here a moment)

paraphrases.simplest: Постоим здесь. — dropping немного is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: по- + verb (do something for a little while)
takeaway.note: постоять (stand a while), посидеть (sit a while), поговорить (talk a while). The prefix по- supplies the 'for a bit'.

keyPoint: Избавиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting rid of" something (pairs with избавляться).

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (1sg хочу) + perfective infinitive (избавиться) + от + genitive (этой проблемы)
grammarFocus.note: избавиться means 'to get rid of' and takes от + genitive, which marks what you are freeing yourself from.

variations.ru: Я хочу избавиться от этой привычки.
variations.note: A different genitive: get rid of this habit

variations.ru: Мы хотим избавиться от лишних вещей.
variations.note: A different subject and genitive: clear out surplus things

options.note: Using решить проблему (solve the problem), more constructive
Using покончить с + instrumental (time to put an end to this)

paraphrases.simplest: Хочу решить эту проблему. — more constructive and clearer.

takeaway.pattern: избавиться от + genitive (get rid of, be free of)
takeaway.note: избавиться от страха (overcome a fear), избавиться от мусора (get rid of rubbish). The от is always needed.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Рождество is a neuter noun meaning "Christmas."

grammarFocus.construction: на + accusative (Рождество) + future of быть 1pl (будем) + place adverb дома
grammarFocus.note: Holidays take на + accusative (на Рождество = at Christmas). The future of быть gives 'we'll be'.

variations.ru: На Новый год мы будем дома.
variations.note: A different holiday: at New Year

variations.ru: На Рождество я буду у родителей.
variations.note: With у + genitive for the place: at my parents'

options.note: Using провести (we'll spend Christmas at home)
Using на праздники (we're staying home over the holidays)

paraphrases.simplest: На Рождество мы дома. — the verb can be dropped.

takeaway.pattern: holidays take на + accusative (на Рождество, на Новый год, на Пасху)
takeaway.note: Days take в + accusative (в субботу) and months в + prepositional (в январе). Time expressions vary by word.

keyPoint: Блядь is an extremely strong vulgar swear, also used as an emotional interjection.

grammarFocus.construction: the obscene interjection Блядь (set off by a comma) + negation не + мочь (1sg могу)
grammarFocus.note: блядь is among the strongest Russian obscenities and works here as an interjection of frustration. It must be avoided in public or with strangers; learners need only recognise it.

variations.note: With блин, the euphemism — the usable version
With чёрт (damn), stronger but acceptable

options.note: No interjection — usable anywhere
Using нет сил (I've no strength left)

paraphrases.simplest: Я не могу. — dropping the obscenity is the only safe option.

takeaway.pattern: Russian obscenity (мат) has very narrow limits of use
takeaway.note: блядь, чёрт and блин run from strongest to mildest. Recognise them all, but stop at блин in your own speech.

keyPoint: Наконец-то is a colloquial, emphatic form of наконец meaning "finally, at long last."

grammarFocus.construction: adverb наконец-то + perfective past (пришёл)
grammarFocus.note: наконец-то is наконец with the particle -то, which adds relief or exasperation. It is more subjective than plain наконец.

variations.note: To a female listener: пришла
Formal or plural: пришли

options.note: Adding ну to heighten the feeling further
The reproachful idiom сколько можно (how long must one wait?)

paraphrases.simplest: Наконец-то! — one word carries the feeling.

takeaway.note: In наконец-то it adds emotion; in где-то and кто-то it creates indefiniteness. The same particle, two jobs.

keyPoint: Неважно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it doesn't matter."

grammarFocus.construction: думать (2pl думаете) + что clause + impersonal predicate неважно
grammarFocus.note: неважно means 'it doesn't matter', with не- fused onto важно. It takes no subject and simply states an assessment.

variations.note: To someone you address as ты: ты думаешь
Without the negation: do you think it matters?

options.note: Using мелочь (does it seem trivial to you?)

options.ru: Для вас это не имеет значения?
options.note: Using не имеет значения (does it carry no weight for you?), formal

paraphrases.simplest: Думаете, это неважно? — что can be dropped.

takeaway.note: None of them take a subject: Это неважно (it doesn't matter), Неважно, кто (it doesn't matter who).

keyPoint: Сожалеть is imperfective, meaning "to regret" (pairs with пожалеть, which can also mean "to pity").

grammarFocus.construction: adverb ещё + future of быть 2sg (будешь) + imperfective infinitive (сожалеть)
grammarFocus.note: ещё means 'still, yet'. будешь plus an imperfective infinitive forms the compound future of ongoing action. сожалеть means 'to regret'.

variations.note: To a formal or plural addressee: будете
With the perfective пожалеешь, shorter and sharper

options.note: Adding об этом to name what will be regretted
Using потом будет поздно (it'll be too late later) as a warning

paraphrases.simplest: Ты ещё пожалеешь. — the perfective is shorter and more forceful.

takeaway.pattern: future of быть + imperfective infinitive (ongoing or repeated future)
takeaway.note: Я буду работать (I'll be working). Perfectives form no compound future — their present forms are already future (Я поработаю).

keyPoint: Ублюдок is a masculine noun that is a strong insult, meaning "bastard."

replies.gloss: Why did you get so angry?

grammarFocus.construction: сказать (perfective past plural сказали) + a quoted term of abuse («ублюдок»)
grammarFocus.note: ублюдок is a strong insult, roughly 'scum' or 'bastard'. In quotation marks it doesn't decline, and the sentence simply checks whether the word was said.

variations.note: To someone you address as ты: ты сказал
With негодяй (scoundrel), older and milder

options.note: Using оскорбить (did you just insult me?), keeping it calm
Using повторите (say that again) to check

paraphrases.simplest: Что вы сказали? — lets you check without repeating the insult.
