takeaway.note: The thing objected to takes против + genitive (возражать против решения); the person objected to takes the dative (возражать начальнику). Keep the two frames apart.

keyPoint: Извиняться is imperfective, meaning "to apologize" (pairs with извиниться).

replies.ru: Ты уверен, что всё в порядке?

grammarFocus.construction: не надо + imperfective infinitive извиняться
grammarFocus.note: надо is an impersonal predicate; не надо + infinitive is a gentle "there's no need to / don't". Like negative imperatives it takes the imperfective, извиняться. Negating a necessity leaves no room for a subject.

variations.note: The base form — the standard way to wave off someone's apology.
нужно means practically the same, just slightly more formal than надо.
Adding the dative тебе makes it explicit: "you don't need to apologise".

options.note: Using the negative imperative directly, with Всё в порядке in front to soften it.
The set phrase "no harm done"; страшного is genitive, as in negated quantity expressions.

paraphrases.simplest: Не надо извиняться.

takeaway.pattern: не надо / не нужно + imperfective infinitive
takeaway.note: Negated necessity takes the imperfective. A perfective there sounds off (Не надо сказать), so pair "no need to" with the imperfective in your mind.

keyPoint: Предупредить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "warning" (pairs with предупреждать).

grammarFocus.construction: должен + perfective infinitive предупредить + accusative тебя
grammarFocus.note: должен is a short-form adjective meaning "must", agreeing with the subject (должен / должна / должны). предупредить (to warn) is perfective and takes the accusative; what you warn about is added with о + prepositional.

variations.note: A female speaker says должна.
вас is polite, or addresses several people.

variations.ru: Я должен предупредить тебя об опасности.
variations.note: о + prepositional об опасности gives the content of the warning; о becomes об before a vowel.

options.note: Dative + нужно, impersonal: "I need to warn you".
With хочу it is intention rather than duty: "I want to give you a warning".

paraphrases.simplest: Я должен тебя предупредить.

takeaway.pattern: должен is a short adjective and agrees in gender and number
takeaway.note: Я должен (m) / Я должна (f) / Мы должны (pl). It is not a verb, so the past is должен был and the future буду должен — tense comes from быть.

keyPoint: Сукин is the possessive adjective of сука (female dog), normally used only in the curse phrase "сукин сын."

grammarFocus.construction: the possessive adjective сукин + inserted ты + сын, as an insult
grammarFocus.note: сукин is a possessive adjective from сука ("of a bitch"), and сукин сын is a strong insult. Wedging ты in — Сукин ты сын! — is an older, more emphatic pattern. Covered here for recognition only; do not use it.

variations.note: The base form without ты — still a strong insult.
негодяй (scoundrel) is literary and contains no obscenity.
подлец (cad) is also abusive but belongs to literary vocabulary, not мат.

options.note: Reproach without abuse; поступить (to act) is perfective.
The predicate adverb подло judges the act itself: "that's despicable".

paraphrases.simplest: Как ты мог так поступить?

takeaway.pattern: сукин сын is a strong insult — recognition only
takeaway.note: The grammar worth keeping is how possessive adjectives are formed: сука → сукин, мама → мамин, папа → папин. As abuse it burns bridges, so choose a literary word like негодяй or simply judge the action.

keyPoint: Конченый is a derogatory colloquial adjective meaning "a wreck, done for."

grammarFocus.construction: считать + accusative + instrumental (to consider X a Y)
grammarFocus.note: считать кого кем means "to consider someone something", with the assessment in the instrumental. его is the animate accusative, and конченый (finished, washed up) becomes конченым in the masculine instrumental. The word is colloquial and strongly negative.

variations.note: Adding человеком makes the instrumental agreement visible: "a man who's finished".
For a woman, the feminine instrumental конченой.
A что clause puts the predicate back in the nominative, конченый — a neat illustration of how the construction decides the case.

options.note: The negated possessive у + genitive + нет + genitive: "do you think he has no chance?"
безнадёжный (hopeless) is more neutral and formal; its instrumental is безнадёжным.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы думаете, что он конченый?

takeaway.note: Я считаю его другом (I consider him a friend). With думать you need a что clause and the nominative instead (Я думаю, что он друг). Same thought, different case frame.

keyPoint: Рисковать is imperfective, meaning "to take risks" (pairs with рискнуть).

grammarFocus.construction: не хочу + imperfective infinitive рисковать
grammarFocus.note: рисковать (to take risks) is imperfective, and what you stake goes in the instrumental (рисковать жизнью, to risk one's life). With no object, не хочу рисковать is the set "I don't want to take the chance".

variations.note: The instrumental жизнью, "to risk one's life" — the typical complement.
зря (for nothing) adds "I don't want to run pointless risks".
A plural subject takes хотим; the infinitive is unchanged.

options.note: The imperfective future states the decision: "I'm not going to risk it".
The predicate adverb рискованно judges the action: "that's too risky".

paraphrases.simplest: Я не хочу рисковать.

takeaway.note: ×рисковать жизнь is wrong. Whatever you stake goes in the instrumental (рисковать здоровьем, деньгами, репутацией), in keeping with the instrumental's sense of means and stake.

keyPoint: Джентльмен is a masculine noun borrowed from English "gentleman."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + long-form adjective + predicate noun настоящий джентльмен
grammarFocus.note: No present-tense "to be". настоящий (genuine) is the long form agreeing with джентльмен (masculine singular nominative). A predicate noun stays nominative in the present; it shifts to the instrumental only when быть is expressed.

variations.note: The base form — a standard compliment.
With the past были, the predicate noun turns instrumental: настоящим джентльменом.
The same pattern with друг: "you're a real friend".

options.note: воспитанный (well brought up) comes from a passive participle: "you're a very well-mannered person".
The predicate adverb благородно judges the deed: "that's very noble".

paraphrases.simplest: Вы настоящий джентльмен.

takeaway.pattern: predicate nouns: nominative in the present, instrumental in past and future
takeaway.note: Он врач (present, nominative) / Он был врачом (past, instrumental) / Он будет врачом (future, instrumental). The moment быть appears, the instrumental takes over.

keyPoint: Here хрен functions as a vulgar intensifier meaning "the hell."

grammarFocus.construction: Какого хрена + a zero-copula question (crude colloquial)
grammarFocus.note: Какого хрена is a rough fixed question frame, "what the hell", frozen in the genitive. хрен (horseradish) is a euphemistic stand-in for an obscenity: not мат, but plainly coarse, so it depends entirely on who you are talking to.

variations.note: The full version with делаешь, which is what people actually say.
The neutral version with the coarse word removed — the only one to use with strangers or at work.
Swapping in чёрт is slightly milder but still rough.

options.note: The most neutral "why are you here?"
Dative + не место: "this is no place for you" — rejection without coarse language.

paraphrases.simplest: Что ты здесь делаешь?

takeaway.pattern: хрен is a euphemistic substitute for obscenity
takeaway.note: хрен, чёрт and блин all stand in for stronger words. They are not мат, but they are still out of place in public or professional settings. Recognise them; say Что ты здесь делаешь? yourself.

keyPoint: Забавно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's amusing."

replies.gloss: I don't know, not really for me.

grammarFocus.construction: Вы думаете + omitted что + the predicate adverb забавно
grammarFocus.note: Colloquially что can be dropped, but the comma stays (Вы думаете, это забавно?). забавно is the short neuter form working as a predicate adverb, "funny, amusing", with это as its implicit subject.

variations.note: With что restored — the standard written form.
казаться takes the instrumental, hence забавным: "does that seem funny to you?"
Dative + смешно, impersonal, asking more bluntly whether it's a joke to you.

options.note: по-вашему is parenthetical and takes a comma: "in your view".
считать + accusative + instrumental шуткой ("a joke"), with a sharper note of reproach.

paraphrases.simplest: Вам это смешно?

takeaway.pattern: что can be dropped; the comma cannot
takeaway.note: In Вы думаете, это забавно? the conjunction is gone but the comma before the clause remains. Russian punctuation marks clause boundaries, not conjunctions.

keyPoint: Влюбить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "making someone fall in love" (pairs with влюблять).

grammarFocus.construction: влюбить + accusative + в себя (to make someone fall for you)
grammarFocus.note: влюбить is the transitive counterpart of влюбиться (to fall in love): "to make someone fall in love". It takes влюбить кого в кого, and when the target is the subject herself, the reflexive pronoun себя is used (в себя). себя has no nominative and always points back to the subject.

variations.ru: Она хочет влюбить его в себя.
variations.note: The base form; себя refers back to the subject она.
The reflexive влюбиться в + accusative reverses the direction: "she fell for him".
The short passive participle влюблён + в + accusative describes the state: "he is in love with her".

options.ru: Она хочет, чтобы он в неё влюбился.
options.note: чтобы + past means "so that he would fall for her" — a wish clause always takes the past form.
понравиться + dative, "to make a good impression on him" — gentler.

paraphrases.simplest: Она хочет, чтобы он её полюбил.

takeaway.pattern: себя is the reflexive pronoun pointing back to the subject
takeaway.note: There is no nominative: genitive/accusative себя, dative себе, instrumental собой, prepositional себе. Он влюбил её в себя (he made her fall for him) needs себя because the reference returns to the subject.

keyPoint: Предать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "betraying" (pairs with предавать).

replies.gloss: What are they asking of you?

grammarFocus.construction: не могу + perfective infinitive предать + animate accusative друга
grammarFocus.note: предать (to betray) is perfective and takes the accusative. друг is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive: друга. не могу + infinitive also covers moral impossibility — "I couldn't bring myself to".

variations.note: The base form: "I can't betray a friend".
The animate accusative plural likewise matches the genitive: друзей.
The perfective future предам with никогда makes it an emphatic vow: "I will never betray a friend".

options.ru: Я не могу так поступить с другом.
options.note: поступить с + instrumental, "to act that way towards a friend", without naming betrayal.
The comparative важнее + для + genitive gives the reason: "friendship matters more to me".

paraphrases.simplest: Я не могу предать друга.

takeaway.pattern: animate nouns take accusative = genitive in both numbers
takeaway.note: друг → друга (sg) / друзей (pl), человек → человека / людей. Inanimates match the nominative instead (дом → дом / дома), so check animacy first.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Ботинок is a masculine noun meaning "boot/shoe."

grammarFocus.construction: negated question Вы не видели + accusative мой ботинок
grammarFocus.note: Russian asks about lost things in the negative — it is the polite formula. ботинок is masculine inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative, and the possessive мой takes the same masculine accusative form.

variations.note: Shoes normally come as a pair, so the plural ботинки is what you would actually say.
With ты it is видел for a man, видела for a woman.

variations.ru: Вы случайно не видели мой ботинок?
variations.note: Inserting случайно (by any chance) makes it even more tentative and polite.

options.ru: Вы не знаете, где мой ботинок?
options.note: Вы не знаете, где... is the polite way to ask where something is; the comma is obligatory.
Framing it as your own problem; найти is perfective.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы не видели мои ботинки?

takeaway.pattern: ask about lost things with a negated question
takeaway.note: Вы не видели...? / Вы не знаете...? presuppose nothing and put no burden on the hearer. The affirmative Вы видели...? can come across as interrogation.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Люк is a masculine noun meaning "hatch/manhole."

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present вижу + accusative люк
grammarFocus.note: видеть (to see) takes the accusative. люк (hatch, manhole) is masculine inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative. The present вижу reports a state of perception, not a deliberate action.

variations.note: The base form: "I can see a hatch".
здесь adds the location; being an adverb it takes no case.
Under negation the object goes genitive: люка — a textbook genitive of negation.

options.note: The есть + nominative existential: "there's a hatch here".
The imperative смотри draws attention; the noun is simply presented in the nominative.

paraphrases.simplest: Я вижу люк.

takeaway.pattern: видеть (to see, perception) vs. смотреть (to look, volition)
takeaway.note: Я вижу картину (I can see the picture) vs. Я смотрю на картину (I'm looking at the picture). смотреть needs на + accusative and is deliberate; видеть takes a bare accusative and describes perception.

keyPoint: Гей is a masculine noun borrowed from English "gay."

replies.ru: Это ничего не меняет между нами.
replies.gloss: That doesn't change anything between us.

grammarFocus.construction: Вы знаете, что + the zero-copula nominal predicate он гей
grammarFocus.note: The comma before a что clause is obligatory. With no present-tense copula, он гей is simply "he is gay". гей is a neutral borrowing and standard in public use; it is a nominative predicate noun.

variations.note: The base form, asking neutrally about a fact.
The past знали implies "did you know?" — surprise at learning it now.
быть в курсе (to be aware) is a set phrase using в + prepositional.

options.note: о + prepositional его ориентации, "about his orientation" — more careful and neutral.
об этом keeps the content vague, stating instead whether he is open about it.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы знаете, что он гей?

takeaway.pattern: гей is neutral — keep it apart from slurs
takeaway.note: гей and гомосексуал are the neutral standard words. Russian also has plenty of slurs on this topic, all of them aggressive, so use none of them. Raising someone's private characteristics depends heavily on the company, so if you must, go indirect with о его ориентации.

keyPoint: Запереть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "locking" (pairs with запирать).

replies.gloss: We should go back and check.

grammarFocus.construction: забыл + perfective infinitive запереть + accusative дверь
grammarFocus.note: забыть + infinitive means "forgot to do something", and the forgotten action takes the perfective (запереть = finish locking). дверь is a feminine noun in -ь, so its accusative stays дверь. забыл shows a male speaker.

variations.note: A female speaker says забыла.
закрыть is "to close", запереть "to lock" — worth keeping apart.
забыть о + prepositional means forgetting about the thing itself, not the action.

options.note: остаться + instrumental незапертой describes the resulting state: "the door was left unlocked".
Кажется is parenthetical and takes a comma: "I don't think I locked it".

paraphrases.simplest: Я забыл закрыть дверь.

takeaway.pattern: забыть + perfective infinitive (forgot to do) vs. забыть о + prepositional (forgot about)
takeaway.note: Я забыл позвонить (I forgot to call) vs. Я забыл о звонке (I forgot about the call). An action takes the infinitive, a thing takes о + prepositional.

skeleton.note: 3rd person plural present, the target word

keyPoint: Угрожать is imperfective, meaning "to threaten" (pairs with пригрозить).

replies.gloss: It makes the plot more interesting.

grammarFocus.construction: a где relative clause + угрожать + dative героям
grammarFocus.note: где here is a relative adverb, "in which", referring back to фильмы. угрожать (to threaten) governs the dative, hence героям (dative plural of герой). In the main clause фильмы is the accusative plural object of любить.

variations.ru: Вы любите фильмы, где герои побеждают?
variations.note: побеждать takes the accusative: "films where the heroes win".

variations.ru: Вы любите фильмы, в которых злодеи угрожают героям?
variations.note: в которых (prepositional plural) is the more formal written equivalent of где.
Dative + нравятся + nominative plural: "do you like films like that?"

options.note: Compressing it into a genre name; триллеры is accusative plural, identical to the nominative for inanimates.
Dative + интересны + с + instrumental: "are you interested in films with threats in them?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вам нравятся фильмы, где злодеи угрожают героям?

takeaway.note: угрожать героям оружием — threaten the heroes (dative) with a weapon (instrumental). ×угрожать героев is wrong.

keyPoint: Кое-кто is an indefinite pronoun meaning "someone" specific but unnamed.

grammarFocus.construction: the indefinite pronoun кое-кому (dative) + perfective past написали
grammarFocus.note: кое-кто refers to "a certain someone" whom the speaker knows but will not name; here it is the dative complement of написать, since писать кому governs the dative. кое- is a fixed prefix, and only the кто part declines.

variations.note: кому-нибудь means "anyone at all"; кое-кому implies one particular person.
Naming the addressee outright with the dative ему.
With ты, написал (m) or написала (f).

options.note: отправить + accusative сообщение — "have you sent the message?", with no need to name anyone.
связаться с + instrumental, "have you got in touch with him?", without specifying the means.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы уже написали ему?

takeaway.pattern: кое-кто = a specific someone the speaker won't name
takeaway.note: кое-кто / кое-что are specific but undisclosed, кто-то is unknown, кто-нибудь is any at all. кое- stays put while the pronoun declines: кое-кому, кое-кого, кое с кем.

keyPoint: Отдохнуть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "resting a bit" (pairs with отдыхать).

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive отдохнуть + the quantity adverb немного
grammarFocus.note: отдохнуть is the perfective of отдыхать, and with немного (a little) it frames a bounded completion — "to take a short break". немного is an adverb of quantity and does not decline. хотите + infinitive makes a polite offer.

variations.note: Dropping Вы is natural; the -те ending already marks the polite addressee.
The negated question suggests without pressing.
давайте + perfective first person plural: "let's take a short break".

options.note: сделать перерыв (to take a break) is set; Может is parenthetical and takes a comma.
Dative + нужен + nominative; нужен agrees with отдых (masculine).

paraphrases.simplest: Хотите немного отдохнуть?

takeaway.pattern: немного + perfective = a bounded, limited completion
takeaway.note: немного отдохнуть / немного поспать / немного подождать. With a perfective, немного frames "do a bit and be done"; with an imperfective it means keeping at it in small amounts.

keyPoint: Умолять is imperfective, meaning "to plead" (pairs with умолить).

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective future не буду + умолять + accusative тебя
grammarFocus.note: умолять (to beg, to implore) is imperfective, so the future is буду + infinitive, with не on буду. It takes the accusative, and the thing begged for is added with о + prepositional (умолять о прощении).

variations.note: The base form: "I'm not going to beg you".
стать + infinitive also builds the future; не стану sounds more pointedly deliberate.
вас is polite, or addresses several people.

options.ru: Я не буду тебя просить дважды.
options.note: просить + accusative with дважды (twice): "I won't ask you twice".
An imperative that hands it over: "decide for yourself"; сам/сама by gender.

paraphrases.simplest: Я не буду тебя просить.

takeaway.note: просить is neutral, умолять is emotionally charged pleading from below. The frame is the same — просить кого о чём / умолять кого о чём — but the intensity is not, so pick by situation.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, plural accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Проклятие is a neuter noun meaning "curse."

grammarFocus.construction: верить в + accusative (to believe in the existence of)
grammarFocus.note: верить в + accusative means believing in the existence or worth of something. проклятия is the accusative plural of проклятие (curse), a neuter noun, so it matches the nominative. By contrast верить + dative means believing what a person says.

variations.note: The base form; the plural generalises — "in curses as such".
судьба (fate) has the accusative судьбу; the frame takes any object.
в это substitutes a demonstrative — the colloquial "do you believe that?"

options.note: Spelling it out with существовать (to exist); the что clause takes a comma.
The short plural суеверны of суеверный: "are you superstitious?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы верите в проклятия?

takeaway.pattern: верить в + accusative (believe in) vs. верить + dative (believe someone)
takeaway.note: Я верю в Бога (I believe God exists) vs. Я верю тебе (I believe what you say). A crucial contrast that hangs on one preposition.

keyPoint: Чёртов is a slang curse-word modifier derived from чёрт (devil).

grammarFocus.construction: the expletive adjective чёртов + accusative телефон, in a negated question
grammarFocus.note: чёртов (damned) comes from чёрт via a possessive adjective and agrees with its noun in gender, number and case (чёртов телефон, masculine singular accusative). It is mild swearing — not мат — but still out of place in public.

variations.note: The neutral version with the expletive dropped — the only one for work or strangers.

variations.ru: Вы не видели мой чёртов телефон?
variations.note: The negated question keeps the irritation but makes the asking itself polite.
где asks outright — commonly heard muttered to oneself.

options.ru: Я никак не могу найти телефон.
options.note: никак не (just can't) conveys the frustration with no swearing.
Colloquial, with деться: "this phone has disappeared again".

paraphrases.simplest: Вы не видели мой телефон?

takeaway.pattern: чёртов is an expletive adjective and declines
takeaway.note: чёртов телефон / чёртова машина / чёртово место, agreeing with the noun. Related: проклятый, and the coarser грёбаный. Understand them, but vent with something like никак не могу instead.

keyPoint: Принцесса is a feminine noun meaning "princess."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the possessive моя + the predicate noun принцесса
grammarFocus.note: No present-tense "to be". моя принцесса is feminine singular nominative, and the predicate noun stays nominative. принцесса is feminine. The phrase works as an intimate term of endearment.

variations.note: The base form — affectionate address.
With the past была, the predicate noun turns instrumental: моей принцессой.
вы is polite, though ты is the norm for something this intimate.

options.note: для + genitive + всё: "you are everything to me".
The adjective дорогая used as a noun of address: "my dear".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты моя принцесса.

takeaway.pattern: predicate nouns: nominative in the present, instrumental in past and future
takeaway.note: Ты моя принцесса (present) vs. Ты была моей принцессой (past). Once быть has a form, the instrumental takes over — endearments follow the same rule as everything else.

keyPoint: Док is a masculine noun meaning "dock" (from English).

grammarFocus.construction: вижу + accusative этот док (a borrowed masculine noun)
grammarFocus.note: док (dock) is borrowed from English, but because it ends in a consonant it declines like any masculine noun (дока, доку...). As an inanimate, its accusative matches the nominative, and этот takes the masculine singular accusative too.

variations.note: The base form; этот points to a particular dock.
отсюда (from here) is an adverb: "I can see the dock from here".
к + dative доку, "we're approaching the dock" — the loanword takes a normal dative ending.

options.note: Вот и ... is the set "there's the ... at last"; the noun stays nominative.
видно is an impersonal predicate adverb: "the dock is visible now", with no subject.

paraphrases.simplest: Я вижу док.

takeaway.pattern: loanwords ending in a consonant decline as masculine nouns
takeaway.note: док, сайт, файл, банк all decline normally (в банке, на сайте). Only vowel-final neuter borrowings stay fixed (такси, кафе, метро).

skeleton.note: masculine noun, plural accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Принц is a masculine noun meaning "prince."

grammarFocus.construction: верить в + animate accusative plural принцев
grammarFocus.note: верить в + accusative again, but принц is animate masculine, so the accusative plural copies the genitive: принцев. Set beside в проклятия (neuter inanimate, matching the nominative), it shows animacy deciding the form.

variations.note: The base form: "do you believe in princes?"

variations.ru: Вы верите в принца на белом коне?
variations.note: The singular принца is likewise genitive-shaped; на белом коне (on a white horse) is a set prepositional phrase.
любовь is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative; only настоящую shows the case.

options.note: сказки is an inanimate accusative plural matching the nominative — figuratively, "do you believe in fairy tales?"
A zero-copula predicate noun: "are you a romantic?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы верите в принцев?

takeaway.pattern: animate accusative plurals also copy the genitive
takeaway.note: принцев, друзей, людей (animate) vs. дома, книги, сказки (inanimate, matching the nominative). The rule applies in the plural exactly as in the singular.

keyPoint: Мамочка is an affectionate diminutive of мама (mom).

grammarFocus.construction: the diminutive address Мамочка + the adverb дома
grammarFocus.note: мамочка is an affectionate diminutive of мама, and as a form of address it takes a comma. дома means "at home" and is an adverb, not a case form of дом. No copula appears in the present.

variations.note: мама is the neutral choice; мамочка sounds cooing.
The perfective пришёл states the arrival; пришла for a female speaker.
The shortest version, with the address dropped — the standard call on getting home.

options.note: Мам is the clipped colloquial vocative of мама; вернуться is "to come back".
Adding the negative imperative не волнуйся: "don't worry".

paraphrases.simplest: Я дома!

takeaway.pattern: дома (at home, location) vs. домой (homewards, direction)
takeaway.note: Я дома (I'm home) vs. Я иду домой (I'm going home). Both are adverbs that never decline, but location and direction take different forms; в доме means something else — inside that particular building.

keyPoint: Лить is imperfective, meaning "to pour." Its perfective varies by meaning; налить means "to pour into a container."

replies.gloss: Don't spill it on the floor.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective future буду лить + accusative воду
grammarFocus.note: лить (to pour) is imperfective, so the future is буду + infinitive. The accusative of вода is воду, with the stress shift typical of such feminine nouns. Note that лить воду is also an idiom for padding out empty talk.

variations.ru: Я буду лить воду в кастрюлю.
variations.note: в + accusative кастрюлю names where the water goes.
The perfective налить makes it a single completed future: "I'll pour the water".
A negative imperative takes the imperfective лей; на + accusative shows direction.

options.note: поливать is "to water (plants)" and takes the accusative — the purpose becomes clear.
Reordering foregrounds the agent: "I'll be the one pouring the water".

paraphrases.simplest: Я налью воду.

takeaway.note: Не лей воду, говори по делу means "stop padding and get to the point". Since the idiom is well known, adding a destination (в кастрюлю) keeps the literal sense unambiguous.

keyPoint: Путешествовать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart. Попутешествовать exists as a delimitative meaning "to travel for a while," not a true pair.

replies.gloss: Where do you like to go?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + imperfective infinitive путешествовать + adverb вместе
grammarFocus.note: любить + infinitive means "to like doing", and the infinitive must be imperfective, since a preference is a habit. путешествовать is an -овать verb and conjugates as путешествую. вместе is an adverb.

variations.note: The base form: "we love travelling together".
по + dative means "around, across" — the standard way to give the range of movement.
один (alone) agrees with the subject: одна, одни.

options.note: Dative + нравится + infinitive: "we enjoy travelling together".

options.ru: Мы часто вместе ездим в путешествия.
options.note: ездить в путешествия, "to go on trips", with the multidirectional verb marking repetition.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы любим путешествовать вместе.

takeaway.note: A preference is habitual, so ×любить поехать is impossible: Я люблю читать / готовить / гулять. For a one-off wish, switch to хотеть + perfective (хочу поехать).

keyPoint: Заслужить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "earning" something (pairs with заслуживать).

replies.gloss: What do I need to do?

grammarFocus.construction: должен + perfective infinitive заслужить + accusative это
grammarFocus.note: должен is a short-form adjective agreeing with the subject (должен / должна / должны). заслужить means to earn or deserve something through effort and takes the accusative as a perfective. Its imperfective заслуживать often takes the genitive instead.

variations.note: должна for a female addressee.
Object before the infinitive — the natural colloquial order.
доверие (trust) is neuter with an identical accusative — a typical object of заслужить.

options.note: Impersonal нужно + infinitive states it as a general truth with no subject.
The reflexive passive даётся with просто так (for nothing): "it isn't handed over for free".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты должен это заслужить.

takeaway.note: The imperfective usually takes the genitive (заслуживать внимания, to be worthy of attention) while the perfective takes the accusative (заслужить награду, to earn a prize) — a rare case where aspect shifts the preferred case.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Инспектор is a masculine noun meaning "inspector."

replies.gloss: What does he need to know?

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past вызвали + animate accusative инспектора
grammarFocus.note: вызвать (to call, to summon) is perfective and takes the accusative. инспектор is animate masculine, so its accusative copies the genitive: инспектора. уже pairs naturally with the perfective, asking whether the result is in place.

variations.note: врача is likewise an animate accusative: "have you called the doctor yet?"
такси is indeclinable and never changes — a neat contrast with the animate forms.
ещё не adds a nudge: "haven't you called the inspector yet?"

options.note: в пути (on the way) is a set prepositional phrase: "is the inspector already on his way?"
сообщить кому governs the dative: "have you informed the inspector?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы уже вызвали инспектора?

takeaway.note: Summoning takes the accusative, informing takes the dative: вызвать врача / сообщить врачу. The frame belongs to the verb, so learn them together.

keyPoint: Папочка is an affectionate diminutive of папа (dad).

grammarFocus.construction: the diminutive address Папочка + imperative иди + directional adverb сюда
grammarFocus.note: папочка is an affectionate diminutive of папа and, as an address, takes a comma. иди is the imperative of идти (imperfective). сюда means "to here", standing in contrast with the locational здесь.

variations.note: папа is the neutral form; папочка sounds childlike and coaxing.
подойти is the perfective "to come over"; подойди is the more concrete "come over here".
пожалуйста makes it polite; the address can be dropped entirely.

options.note: можешь + infinitive frames it as a request: "can you come over?"
Пап is the clipped colloquial vocative; на минутку (for a minute) is на + accusative.

paraphrases.simplest: Папа, иди сюда.

takeaway.pattern: сюда (to here, direction) vs. здесь (here, location)
takeaway.note: Иди сюда (come here) vs. Я здесь (I'm here). туда/там and домой/дома form the same direction-location pairs; learn them two by two.

keyPoint: Отвратительный is an adjective meaning "disgusting, repulsive."

grammarFocus.construction: считать + accusative этот запах + instrumental отвратительным
grammarFocus.note: считать кого/что кем/чем means "to consider X to be Y", with the assessment in the instrumental. запах is masculine inanimate (accusative = nominative), and the masculine instrumental of отвратительный is отвратительным — the adjective goes instrumental too.

variations.note: приятным reverses the verdict; the instrumental ending is the same.
казаться also takes the instrumental, with the dative Вам as the one perceiving.

variations.ru: Вы думаете, что этот запах отвратительный?
variations.note: A что clause returns the predicate to the nominative, отвратительный.

options.note: Dative + нравится; the negated question asks tentatively.
раздражать takes the accusative: "does this smell irritate you?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вам не нравится этот запах?

takeaway.note: Both nouns and adjectives go instrumental (считать это ошибкой / считать запах отвратительным). Recast with a что clause and the case returns to the nominative — feel how the construction decides it.

keyPoint: Наслаждаться is imperfective, meaning "to enjoy" (pairs with насладиться).

replies.ru: Что для тебя значит наслаждаться жизнью?
replies.gloss: What does enjoying life mean to you?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + imperfective infinitive наслаждаться + instrumental жизнью
grammarFocus.note: наслаждаться (to enjoy, to savour) is a reflexive verb governing the instrumental; the instrumental of жизнь is жизнью. The imperfective means savouring on and on; the perfective насладиться means savouring one occasion to the full.

variations.note: The base form: "I want to enjoy life".
The perfective насладиться + instrumental этим моментом: "savour this moment".
The instrumental of тишина is тишиной: "we are enjoying the quiet".

options.note: радоваться takes the dative, hence жизни — the differing case is the real lesson here.

options.ru: Я хочу жить в своё удовольствие.
options.note: в своё удовольствие (for one's own pleasure) is a set в + accusative phrase.

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу наслаждаться жизнью.

takeaway.note: Two near-synonyms of enjoying, two cases: наслаждаться музыкой (instrumental) / радоваться успеху (dative). Memorise the case along with the emotion verb.

keyPoint: Застрелить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "shooting (someone) dead" (pairs with застреливать).

replies.gloss: Yes, the tension keeps you hooked.
That usually happens at the end.

grammarFocus.construction: an impersonal plural хотят inside a где clause + perfective застрелить + animate accusative героя
grammarFocus.note: хотят with no subject is an impersonal third-person plural: "someone wants to". застрелить (to shoot dead) is perfective and takes the accusative, and герой is animate, hence героя. где is the relative adverb referring back to фильмы.

variations.ru: Вы любите фильмы, где хотят убить героя?
variations.note: убить is the general "to kill"; застрелить specifies shooting.

variations.ru: Вы любите фильмы, где героя спасают?
variations.note: An impersonal plural with спасать; fronting героя foregrounds the object.
с + instrumental перестрелками, "films with shootouts" — no clause needed.

options.note: боевики is the accusative plural of боевик (action film) — the whole thing in one genre word.
про + accusative is the colloquial "about", more spoken than о + prepositional.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы любите фильмы, где хотят убить героя?

takeaway.pattern: the impersonal plural leaves the subject out
takeaway.note: Говорят, что... (they say), Здесь не курят (no smoking here), Его уволили (he was fired). Where the agent is unknown or irrelevant, Russian prefers this over a passive.

keyPoint: Виновный is an adjective meaning "guilty."

grammarFocus.construction: вижу + animate accusative виновного человека
grammarFocus.note: видеть takes the accusative. человек is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive — человека — and the modifier follows as виновного. виновный (guilty) can also stand alone as a noun, "the culprit".

variations.note: The adjective used on its own as a noun: "I can see the guilty one".
For a feminine noun, виновную женщину; animate feminine singular accusative ends in -ую / -у.
Animate accusatives already look genitive, so negation changes nothing visible.

options.note: Using the short form виноват (m) / виновата (f): "I know who is to blame".
виновник (the culprit) is a noun; Вот он points him out.

paraphrases.simplest: Я знаю, кто виноват.

takeaway.pattern: adjectives used as nouns (виновный, больной, знакомый)
takeaway.note: виновный = culprit, больной = patient, знакомый = acquaintance. They keep adjectival endings (виновного, больному), so recognise them by shape.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, instrumental, the target word

keyPoint: Безумие is a neuter noun meaning "madness."

grammarFocus.construction: считать + accusative это + instrumental безумием
grammarFocus.note: The считать что чем frame again, this time with a noun as the assessment, so it goes instrumental: безумие (madness) → безумием. An adjective would work the same way as безумным — either way, instrumental.

variations.note: The base form, with the noun безумием: "do you consider this madness?"
The adjective безумным gives "do you consider this insane?" — practically the same.
In a что clause the word returns to the nominative, безумие.

options.note: сумасшествие is another word for madness; по-вашему is parenthetical with a comma.
казаться + instrumental, with the dative Вам as the perceiver.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы думаете, что это безумие?

takeaway.pattern: the instrumental of assessment works with nouns and adjectives alike
takeaway.note: считать это ошибкой (noun) / считать это ошибочным (adjective). The noun sounds categorical, the adjective evaluates a quality — but both take the instrumental.

keyPoint: ДНК is an indeclinable acronym meaning "DNA."

grammarFocus.construction: сдавать тест на + accusative (to take a test for something)
grammarFocus.note: сдавать тест / анализ на + accusative is the set way to say you take a test for something. ДНК is an abbreviation and indeclinable, so на ДНК never changes. The imperfective past сдавали asks whether you have ever done it.

variations.note: In medical contexts анализ (a lab test) is more natural than тест.
The perfective сдали points to one specific occasion: "did you take that test?"
делать тест is also common in speech, with much the same meaning.

options.note: проходить тест is "to undergo a test"; ДНК-тест is a compound.
A noun-centred recast: "are the DNA results in yet?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы сдавали тест на ДНК?

takeaway.pattern: imperfective past = any experience; perfective past = one specific occasion
takeaway.note: Вы сдавали тест? asks whether you have ever taken it; Вы сдали тест? asks whether you passed that one. сдать also means "to pass", so aspect changes the question itself.

keyPoint: Потратить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "spending it all" (pairs with тратить).

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive потратить + accusative всё
grammarFocus.note: потратить is the perfective of тратить (to spend) and takes the accusative. всё is the neuter pronoun, identical in nominative and accusative. The prefix по- here supplies the sense of using it all up.

variations.note: The base form: "I want to spend it all".
все деньги (accusative plural) is "all the money" — mind the всё (neuter singular) vs. все (plural) contrast.
Under negation the imperfective тратить is more natural: "I don't want to be spending everything".

options.note: израсходовать is "to use up" — bureaucratic and formal.
пусть + third-person perfective: "let it all go on this"; уйти на + accusative means "to be spent on".

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу потратить всё.

takeaway.pattern: всё (everything, neuter singular) vs. все (everyone, plural)
takeaway.note: Всё готово (everything is ready) vs. Все готовы (everyone is ready). Stress and meaning both differ, and the agreeing verb or adjective gives it away.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Грузовик is a masculine noun meaning "truck."

grammarFocus.construction: видели + the demonstrative тот + accusative грузовик
grammarFocus.note: тот points to something distant or already known — "that one" — in contrast with этот ("this"). грузовик is masculine inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative and тот stays unchanged. The perfective видели asks about the fact of having seen it.

variations.note: этот shifts it to "this truck, right here" — a different sense of distance.

variations.ru: Вы видели тот грузовик, который стоял здесь?
variations.note: A который clause pins it down; тот ... который is the standard correlative pair.
With ты, видел for a man, видела for a woman.

options.note: заметить is "did you notice" — about attention rather than mere visibility.
With всё ещё (still), asking whether it is still around.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели тот грузовик?

takeaway.note: тот also covers "the other" and "the one in question" (тот же = the same, не тот = the wrong one). Learn it as a pair with этот.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Холодильник is a masculine noun meaning "refrigerator."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past купили + accusative холодильник + the adverb уже
grammarFocus.note: купить (to buy) is perfective and takes the accusative; холодильник is masculine inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative. уже + perfective past is how Russian expresses the English present perfect, asking whether the result is in.

variations.note: The base form, asking about the result.
ещё не adds a nudge: "haven't you bought one yet?"
The imperfective past asks about the activity or experience of buying one.

options.note: The у + genitive + есть possessive: "do you have one already?"
The impersonal plural привезли shifts focus to delivery: "has it been delivered?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы уже купили холодильник?

takeaway.pattern: уже + perfective past does the work of the present perfect
takeaway.note: Russian has no present perfect tense; "have you already..." is уже + perfective past, and the negative is ещё не + perfective past (ещё не купили, haven't bought it yet).

keyPoint: Проклятый is an adjective meaning "cursed, damn."

replies.gloss: Yes, I just can't find it.

replies.ru: Где ты его видел последний раз?
replies.gloss: Where did you last see it?

grammarFocus.construction: опять + imperfective present ищете + the expletive adjective проклятый ключ
grammarFocus.note: искать (to look for) takes the accusative, and the imperfective present means the search is under way. опять (again) signals irritation at the repetition. проклятый (damned) is a mild expletive adjective agreeing in gender, number and case — avoid it in formal settings.

variations.note: The neutral version without the expletive — the one for the workplace.
всё ещё (still) turns irritation into a plain check on progress.

variations.ru: Ты опять ищешь этот проклятый ключ?
variations.note: With ты, ищешь — only the ending changes.

options.ru: Вы так и не нашли ключ?
options.note: так и не + perfective: "so you never found the key?"
The reflexive потеряться makes the key the subject: "has the key gone missing again?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы опять ищете ключ?

takeaway.note: искать is the process and exists only as an imperfective; найти is the perfective result. Я ищу ключ (I'm looking) / Я нашёл ключ (I found it). Keep expletive adjectives like проклятый at recognition level.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, plural accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Шериф is a masculine noun borrowed from English "sheriff."

grammarFocus.construction: про + animate accusative plural шерифов
grammarFocus.note: про + accusative is the colloquial "about" (the spoken counterpart of о + prepositional). шериф is animate masculine, so the accusative plural copies the genitive: шерифов. фильмы is the accusative plural object of любить.

variations.note: о + prepositional о шерифах is the bookish equivalent, same meaning.
война is inanimate feminine, so the accusative is войну — a visible contrast with animates.
вестерны (westerns) sums it up; dative + нравятся.

options.note: смотреть + accusative asks about habit rather than preference.

options.ru: Вам интересны истории про Дикий Запад?
options.note: про + accusative Дикий Запад — proper nouns take the accusative too.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы любите фильмы про шерифов?

takeaway.note: книга про войну and книга о войне are both fine, but про belongs to speech and о to neutral or formal style. After про the case is always accusative, so animates look genitive.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Мэр is a masculine noun meaning "mayor."

replies.gloss: Yes, he was giving a speech.

grammarFocus.construction: видели + animate accusative мэра + по + dative телевизору
grammarFocus.note: мэр is animate masculine, so its accusative copies the genitive: мэра. по телевизору (on television) is the set по + dative pattern for a medium, as in по радио and по телефону.

variations.note: The base form: "did you see the mayor on TV?"
по радио is likewise по + dative; радио is indeclinable, so the form stays put.
вчера is an adverb — a time reference instead of a medium.

options.note: выступление мэра (the mayor's speech) uses the genitive as a modifier; смотреть takes the accusative.
The impersonal plural показывали: "the mayor was on TV", with мэра still accusative.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели мэра по телевизору?

takeaway.note: по телевизору / по радио / по телефону / по интернету. Russian routes "via" through по + dative; ×в телевизоре is not an option.

keyPoint: Отвести is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "taking someone" somewhere (pairs with отводить).

grammarFocus.construction: могу + perfective infinitive отвести + accusative тебя + directional adverb домой
grammarFocus.note: отвести means to take someone somewhere on foot and takes the accusative. домой (homewards) is a directional adverb, so it needs no preposition and no case. могу + infinitive frames the offer.

variations.note: The base form — offering to walk you home.
отвезти is to take someone by vehicle; the choice depends on the means.
The perfective future states the decision: "I'll take you home".

options.note: проводить is "to see someone off, to accompany"; Давай + first person makes the offer.
Хочешь, ... is the comma-separated "shall I ...?" proposal pattern.

paraphrases.simplest: Я могу отвести тебя домой.

takeaway.pattern: вести (lead on foot) vs. везти (carry by vehicle)
takeaway.note: отвести/отвезти, привести/привезти — the motion verbs split by means. Walking someone there uses вести, driving them uses везти.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Чашка is a feminine noun meaning "cup."

grammarFocus.construction: видели + the possessive мою + accusative чашку
grammarFocus.note: чашка is feminine with the accusative чашку (-а → -у), and the possessive мою is feminine singular accusative. The perfective видели asks whether you saw it. For lost items a negated question works just as well.

variations.note: The negated question is the polite, tentative way to ask about something lost.
In the plural, чашки with мои — inanimate, so identical to the nominative.
With ты, видел for a man, видела for a woman.

options.ru: Вы не знаете, где моя чашка?
options.note: Вы не знаете, где... politely asks where something is; inside the clause the noun is nominative, моя чашка.
пропасть is the perfective "to vanish" — framing it as your own problem.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы не видели мою чашку?

takeaway.pattern: feminine nouns in -а take -у in the accusative
takeaway.note: чашка → чашку, книга → книгу, машина → машину. Modifiers follow with -ую / -ю (мою, эту, новую). Unlike masculine inanimates, feminine nouns show the accusative clearly.

keyPoint: Опасно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's dangerous."

replies.gloss: Yes, we need to be careful.

grammarFocus.construction: Вы думаете + omitted что + the predicate adverb опасно
grammarFocus.note: что can be dropped in speech but the comma stays. опасно is a short neuter form used as a predicate adverb, building a subjectless impersonal clause, "it is dangerous". The place is given by the adverb здесь.

variations.note: With что restored — the written standard.
Dative Вам + кажется: "does it seem dangerous to you?", with the perceiver in the dative.
The shortest version — the impersonal clause stands on its own.

options.note: The long form опасное modifies место; по-вашему is parenthetical.
The есть + nominative existential: "is there any risk here?"

paraphrases.simplest: Здесь опасно?

takeaway.note: Здесь опасно / Сегодня холодно / В комнате тихо — describing a situation with no subject is the Russian default. Add a person in the dative (Мне холодно, I'm cold).

skeleton.note: neuter noun, genitive, the target word

keyPoint: Нападение is a neuter noun meaning "attack."

grammarFocus.construction: accusative сцену + genitive modifier нападения + в + prepositional фильме
grammarFocus.note: сцена нападения, "the attack scene", puts the second noun in the genitive — the noun + genitive modifier pattern. сцену is the feminine accusative, and в фильме is в + prepositional for location.

variations.ru: Вы видели сцену нападения в фильме?
variations.note: The base form, showing a genitive modifier and a locative prepositional at once.

variations.ru: Вы видели эту сцену в фильме?
variations.note: эту сцену lets you drop the genitive modifier.
помнить + accusative: "do you remember the attack scene?", with the location dropped.

options.note: с + instrumental нападением turns the genitive modifier into a prepositional phrase.

options.ru: В фильме была сцена нападения, помните?
options.note: была + nominative states existence, with помните? as the tag.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели эту сцену в фильме?

takeaway.note: сцена нападения, дверь машины, конец фильма. Russian expresses English "of" with the genitive alone — no preposition required.

keyPoint: Невеста is a feminine noun meaning "bride/fiancée."

replies.gloss: How long have you been together?

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the adverb дома + the adverb уже
grammarFocus.note: No present-tense "to be". дома means "at home" and is an adverb, not a case form of дом. невеста (fiancée, bride) is feminine, and the possessive моя agrees with it.

variations.note: The base form: "my fiancée is already home".
The past takes была (feminine singular); дома is unchanged.
A male fiancé is жених, with the possessive мой.

options.note: The perfective past of вернуться: "she's already back".
A pronoun plus the negative imperative не волнуйся — the everyday phrasing.

paraphrases.simplest: Моя невеста уже дома.

takeaway.pattern: locational дома is an adverb and never declines
takeaway.note: Я дома / Она дома / Мы были дома, always one form. To stress the building use в доме; for direction switch to домой.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Прокурор is a masculine noun meaning "prosecutor."

grammarFocus.construction: смотреть + accusative сериал + про + animate accusative прокурора
grammarFocus.note: смотреть (to watch) takes the accusative. про + accusative is the colloquial "about". прокурор is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive: прокурора. The imperfective present describes an ongoing habit.

variations.note: The base form, asking whether you follow the series.
о + prepositional о прокуроре is the bookish version; про is more spoken.
The imperfective past смотрели asks about the experience: "have you watched it?"

options.note: следить за + instrumental is "to keep up with" — made for serials.
Dative + нравится + nominative, asking about preference directly.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы смотрите сериал про прокурора?

takeaway.note: сериал про врачей / статья о врачах. про is friendly and spoken, о neutral to formal. After про the case is always accusative, so animates look genitive.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Рана is a feminine noun meaning "wound."

replies.gloss: How did he get that wound?

grammarFocus.construction: видели + accusative рану + в + prepositional фильме
grammarFocus.note: рана (wound) is feminine with the accusative рану. в фильме is the locative prepositional. The perfective видели asks about the single fact of seeing it. An accusative object beside a prepositional location is the basic shape here.

variations.note: The base form: "did you see the wound in the film?"
Adding the indeclinable possessive его: "his wound".

variations.ru: Вы видели раны на его руках?
variations.note: The plural раны (inanimate, so nominative-shaped) with на + prepositional руках giving the place.

options.note: The impersonal plural показывали: "was the wound shown in the film?"

options.ru: Вы заметили рану в этой сцене?
options.note: заметить is "to notice"; в этой сцене is a prepositional phrase narrowing it to one scene.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели рану в фильме?

takeaway.pattern: в + prepositional = location; в + accusative = direction
takeaway.note: в фильме (in the film) and в фильм (into the film) mean entirely different things. The same в switches roles by case, so check first whether the verb is static or a movement.

keyPoint: Внутрь is an adverb of direction meaning "inward."

grammarFocus.construction: the perfective first-person plural invitation Пойдём + directional adverb внутрь
grammarFocus.note: Пойдём is the first person plural of пойти and works on its own as "let's go" (давайте is optional). внутрь means "inwards" and contrasts with the locational внутри.

variations.note: The base form; вместе (together) is an adverb.
Adding Давай makes it sound more like a proposal.
The -те ending makes it polite, or addresses several people.

options.note: зайти is the perfective "to step in, to drop in": "let's go inside".
войти (to enter) with the parenthetical Может makes a tentative suggestion.

paraphrases.simplest: Пойдём внутрь.

takeaway.note: Пойдём внутрь (let's go in) / Мы внутри (we're inside). наружу/снаружи form the same pair — direction and location take different adverbs.

keyPoint: Ошибиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "making a mistake" (pairs with ошибаться).

grammarFocus.construction: могу + perfective infinitive ошибиться (могу of possibility)
grammarFocus.note: ошибиться (to make a mistake) is a reflexive perfective. могу expresses not only ability but possibility, "I might". The sentence is the standard way of hedging: "I could be wrong".

variations.note: The base form, conceding that you might get it wrong.
The imperfective ошибаться means "I may be wrong right now" — the more frequent hedge.
Возможно is parenthetical with a comma: "possibly I'm mistaken".

options.note: The short form уверен (m) / уверена (f): "I'm not sure".

options.ru: Поправьте меня, если я не прав.
options.note: An imperative plus an если clause — the set "correct me if I'm wrong".

paraphrases.simplest: Я могу ошибаться.

takeaway.pattern: могу covers possibility as well as ability
takeaway.note: Я могу ошибиться (I may be mistaken), Это может случиться (that could happen). One verb мочь does both jobs, so let context decide which.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Призрак is a masculine noun meaning "ghost."

grammarFocus.construction: видел + animate accusative призрака + the instrumental time expression ночью
grammarFocus.note: призрак (ghost) is usually treated as animate, so its accusative copies the genitive: призрака. ночью is the instrumental of ночь, used with no preposition to mean "at night" — the instrumental of time.

variations.note: The base form, with the animate accusative призрака.
видела for a female speaker; утром is likewise an instrumental of time.
The plural is animate too, so again genitive-shaped: призраков.

options.note: показаться + dative, "appeared to me", with призрак as the nominative subject.
кого-то (animate indefinite accusative) keeps it vague: "I saw someone".

paraphrases.simplest: Я видел призрака ночью.

takeaway.pattern: the instrumental of time (утром, днём, вечером, ночью, зимой)
takeaway.note: No preposition — the instrumental alone means "at that time". Days take в + accusative (в среду) and months в + prepositional (в мае), so learn time expressions unit by unit.

keyPoint: Бакс is a colloquial masculine noun borrowed from English "buck" (dollar).

grammarFocus.construction: заплатили + the numeral один + accusative бакс
grammarFocus.note: заплатить (to pay) is perfective, and the sum goes in the accusative. один behaves like an adjective, agreeing with its noun (один бакс, masculine singular). бакс is colloquial for a dollar and declines like any masculine noun.

variations.note: доллар is the standard word; бакс is casual slang.
After 2-4 the noun goes into the genitive singular: бакса.
From five up it is the genitive plural, баксов — the classic three-tier pattern.

options.note: с + genitive with the impersonal plural взяли: "were you charged a dollar?"
стоить + accusative gives the price: "did it cost a dollar?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы заплатили один доллар?

takeaway.note: один бакс / два бакса / пять баксов. Only один agrees like an adjective (одна книга, одно слово); from two up the numeral governs the noun's case.

keyPoint: Убежать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "running away" (pairs with убегать).

replies.gloss: Where do you want to go?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive убежать + от + genitive этой жары
grammarFocus.note: убежать (to run away) takes от + genitive, and the genitive of жара (heat) is жары. The prefix у- means moving off from a place, and от + genitive marks the point you are escaping.

variations.ru: Вы хотите убежать от этой жары?
variations.note: The base form: "do you want to escape this heat?"
спрятаться от + genitive is "to take shelter from the heat" — the same от frame.

variations.ru: Я хочу уехать от этой жары.
variations.note: уехать is to leave by vehicle — natural for going away somewhere cooler.

options.note: надоесть + dative, "to be fed up with", with эта жара as the subject.
где прохладно is a relative clause built on a predicate adverb: "somewhere cool".

paraphrases.simplest: Вы хотите убежать от жары?

takeaway.pattern: от + genitive = the point you move away from
takeaway.note: убежать от собаки / спрятаться от дождя / уйти от проблем. Verbs with the prefixes у- and от- pair up with от + genitive to mean "away from".

keyPoint: Обвинять is imperfective, meaning "to accuse" (pairs with обвинить).

grammarFocus.construction: не надо + imperfective infinitive обвинять + accusative меня
grammarFocus.note: не надо + infinitive is a gentle prohibition and takes the imperfective. обвинять (to accuse) governs the accusative, and the charge is added with в + prepositional (обвинять в краже, to accuse of theft).

variations.note: Object before the infinitive — the natural colloquial order.
A direct negative imperative with the imperfective обвиняй.

variations.ru: Не надо обвинять меня во всём.
variations.note: во всём (for everything) is в + prepositional; в becomes во before the consonant cluster.

options.note: ни при чём is the set phrase "I have nothing to do with it", built on при + prepositional.
A zero-copula nominal: "it isn't my fault".

paraphrases.simplest: Не обвиняй меня.

takeaway.pattern: обвинять кого в чём (accusative + в + prepositional)
takeaway.note: обвинять его в обмане, to accuse him of deception. The two-slot frame mirrors English "accuse someone of something", with the charge always in в + prepositional.

keyPoint: Чертовски is a slang intensifying adverb meaning "damn, incredibly."

grammarFocus.construction: the intensifier чертовски + adjective хороший + predicate noun друг
grammarFocus.note: чертовски (damn, awfully) is an intensifying adverb derived from чёрт and strengthens the adjective. It comes from mild swearing but works as praise in speech. The predicate noun друг stays nominative in the present.

variations.note: очень is fully neutral — the version for work or for older people.
For a woman, хорошая подруга; чертовски is an adverb and never changes.
With the past был the predicate noun turns instrumental: хорошим другом.

options.note: настоящий (true, real) gives neutral praise.
A что clause supplies the reason: "thank you for being there".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты очень хороший друг.

takeaway.pattern: чертовски is a colloquial intensifier, positive or negative
takeaway.note: чертовски вкусно (damn tasty) / чертовски сложно (awfully hard). Not мат, but strictly colloquial — swap in очень or крайне for formal settings.

keyPoint: Пугать is imperfective, meaning "to scare" (pairs with напугать).

grammarFocus.construction: не надо + imperfective infinitive пугать + animate accusative ребёнка
grammarFocus.note: не надо + imperfective makes a gentle prohibition. пугать (to frighten) takes the accusative, and ребёнок is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive: ребёнка. The reflexive пугаться means being frightened oneself.

variations.note: A direct negative imperative; пугай is the imperfective form.
The plural детей is animate too, hence genitive-shaped.
With the pronoun его — an animate accusative identical to the genitive.

options.note: The perfective future of the reflexive испугаться states the consequence: "you'll scare the child".
The comparative adverb спокойнее offers the alternative: "speak to him more calmly".

paraphrases.simplest: Не пугай ребёнка.

takeaway.pattern: пугать кого (transitive) vs. пугаться (to be frightened)
takeaway.note: Не пугай ребёнка (don't scare the child) / Ребёнок пугается (the child gets scared). -ся removes the object and turns the action back on the subject — the standard pattern for emotion verbs.

keyPoint: Мена is an archaic/literary feminine noun meaning "exchange, trade."

grammarFocus.construction: past была + the instrumental predicate noun хорошим делом
grammarFocus.note: Whenever быть has a form, a predicate noun goes into the instrumental. дело (matter, thing) is neuter with the instrumental делом, and the adjective follows as хорошим. The subject мена (barter, exchange) is feminine, hence была.

variations.note: The base form — the classic past + instrumental.
In the present there is no быть and the predicate noun stays nominative, хорошее дело; a dash separates subject and predicate.
The future будет keeps the instrumental; only the present goes nominative.

options.note: обмен (exchange) is masculine, hence был, with the masculine instrumental выгодным (profitable).
обменяться, reciprocal -ся, takes the instrumental; the adverb хорошо carries the judgement.

paraphrases.simplest: Мена — хорошее дело.

takeaway.pattern: nominative predicate in the present, instrumental in past and future
takeaway.note: Он врач / Он был врачом / Он будет врачом. The instrumental kicks in the moment быть appears. Note that a bare adjective predicate can stay short instead (Он был болен).

keyPoint: Подходящий is an adjective meaning "suitable, fitting."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past нашёл + accusative подходящий дом
grammarFocus.note: найти (to find) is perfective and takes the accusative; its masculine past is the irregular нашёл. дом is masculine inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative, and подходящий (suitable) matches too.

variations.note: нашла for a female speaker; the forms are нашёл / нашла / нашло / нашли.
квартира is feminine, so the accusative is квартиру and the adjective подходящую.
наконец (at last) implies a long search behind it.

options.note: подобрать is "to pick out", implying a choice among candidates.
The short passive participle найден: "the house has been found".

paraphrases.simplest: Я нашёл подходящий дом.

takeaway.pattern: the past of найти is нашёл / нашла
takeaway.note: Verbs whose past stem departs from the infinitive (найти → нашёл, идти → шёл, есть → ел) have to be memorised. The ё appears only in the masculine; elsewhere it reverts to е (нашла, нашли).

keyPoint: Мм is an interjection used while thinking or agreeing.

grammarFocus.construction: the interjection Мм + the short-form adjective готовы, as a question
grammarFocus.note: готовы is the short plural of готовый, the predicate form agreeing with Вы. No быть in the present. Мм is the interjection for pausing or checking, placed at the front with a comma.

variations.note: The base form without the interjection: "are you ready yet?"
With ты, готов for a man and готова for a woman — short forms agree in gender and number.
готовы + infinitive is "ready to do something".

options.note: собраться is the perfective "to get oneself ready", used before setting out.
можем + infinitive: "can we go now?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы уже готовы?

takeaway.pattern: готов / готова / готовы are short-form predicates
takeaway.note: Я готов (m) / Я готова (f) / Мы готовы (pl). The long form готовый modifies nouns (готовый ужин, a ready-made dinner); predicates take the short form.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, prepositional, the target word

keyPoint: Рак is a masculine noun meaning either "cancer" or "crayfish" — context determines which.

replies.gloss: Yes, it's a very serious topic.

grammarFocus.construction: читать о + prepositional раке
grammarFocus.note: читать о + prepositional is "to read about". The prepositional of рак (cancer; also crayfish) is раке. The imperfective past читали asks whether you have ever read about it. о becomes об before a vowel.

variations.note: The base form: "have you read about cancer?"
про + accusative рак is the colloquial equivalent — same meaning, more spoken.

variations.ru: Вы прочитали эту статью о раке?
variations.note: The perfective прочитали points to one specific article finished.

options.note: знать о + prepositional: "do you know anything about it?"; что-нибудь is an indefinite accusative.
изучать + accusative тему, "have you studied this subject?" — not limited to reading.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы читали о раке?

takeaway.note: говорить о работе / думать о тебе / читать о раке. о always takes the prepositional, becoming об before a vowel (об этом, об опасности) and обо before всём (обо всём).

keyPoint: Кошмар is a masculine noun meaning "nightmare."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past пережили + accusative настоящий кошмар
grammarFocus.note: пережить (to live through, to survive) takes the accusative; the prefix пере- supplies the sense of passing through. кошмар is masculine inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative, and so does настоящий.

variations.note: The base form: "did you live through a real nightmare?"
With ты, пережил for a man, пережила for a woman.
The imperfective переживать means something else — "to worry"; из-за + genitive gives the cause.

options.note: Dative + пришлось + infinitive is "you had to"; пройти через + accusative is "to go through".

options.ru: Это был настоящий кошмар для вас?
options.note: A nominative predicate with для + genitive: "was it a real nightmare for you?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы пережили настоящий кошмар?

takeaway.note: A rare case where aspect shifts the meaning itself: the perfective is living through something, the imperfective is fretting over it. Не переживай! — "don't worry!" — is the commonest use of all.

keyPoint: Побыть is a perfective delimitative of быть, meaning "to stay a while."

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive побыть + locational adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: побыть is быть with по-, a perfective meaning "to stay a while". здесь is a locational adverb. Because по- imposes a time frame, the implication is a short stay, not settling in.

variations.note: The base form: "I'd like to stay here a bit".
один agrees with the subject (одна, одни): "I want to be alone" — a very common phrase.
остаться is "to stay on" — longer than побыть, and framed as choosing not to leave.

options.note: посидеть (sit a while) with немного; Можно я... is the colloquial way to ask permission.
дать + dative + accusative: "give me a minute".

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу побыть здесь.

takeaway.note: побыть / посидеть / постоять / погулять all mean "do it for a while". Because the prefix bounds the time, they clash with долго and pair with немного or минутку.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Мяч is a masculine noun meaning "ball."

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Дай + dative мне + accusative этот мяч
grammarFocus.note: The imperative of дать is дай (singular) and дайте (polite/plural). As a verb of giving it takes two slots: the recipient in the dative (мне) and the thing in the accusative (этот мяч). мяч is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative.

variations.note: дайте is the polite form — the one for a stranger.
пожалуйста makes it polite and is set off by commas.
передать is "to pass" — right when the thing is handed over from a distance.

options.note: можно + dative + accusative drops the verb entirely: "could I have that ball?"
The imperative of бросить (to throw), with the same dative + accusative frame.

paraphrases.simplest: Дай мне мяч.

takeaway.note: In дай мне воды the object turns partitive genitive ("some water"). The two slots stay put while the object's case shifts with the meaning.

keyPoint: Потрясающе is an intensifying adverb meaning "amazingly."

grammarFocus.construction: the manner adverb потрясающе + imperfective present поёте
grammarFocus.note: потрясающе (stunningly) is the manner adverb from потрясающий and modifies the verb. петь conjugates irregularly with ё: пою / поёшь / поёт ... / поёте. With an exclamation mark it is pure praise.

variations.note: The base form: "you sing wonderfully!"
With ты, поёшь — only the ending changes.
прекрасно fits the same slot; swap the adverb to tune the degree.

options.note: The у + genitive + nominative possessive, with the long adjective потрясающий modifying the noun.

options.ru: Мне очень понравилось, как вы пели.
options.note: Dative + понравилось plus a как clause: "I really liked the way you sang".

paraphrases.simplest: Вы прекрасно поёте!

takeaway.pattern: praise a verb with an adverb (-о), a noun with an adjective
takeaway.note: Вы потрясающе поёте (adverb on the action) vs. У вас потрясающий голос (adjective on the thing). Pick the form by what you are modifying.

keyPoint: Полно is an impersonal predicate meaning "plenty of," combined with the genitive case.

grammarFocus.construction: полно + genitive plural людей (quantity word government)
grammarFocus.note: полно (plenty, packed) is a quantity predicate adverb, and the noun after it goes genitive. The genitive plural of люди is the irregular людей. A comma separates it from the main clause Вы видите, and тут is the colloquial здесь.

variations.note: The base form; что may be absent but the comma remains.
много also governs the genitive; полно is more colloquial, suggesting "crammed".
народу is a colloquial partitive genitive: "the place is heaving".

options.note: сколько also takes the genitive; as an exclamation it conveys surprise at the crowd.
людно is a predicate adverb, "it's crowded here" — a subjectless impersonal clause.

paraphrases.simplest: Здесь много людей.

takeaway.pattern: quantity words (много, мало, полно, сколько) + genitive
takeaway.note: много людей / мало времени / полно дел. Countables take the genitive plural, uncountables the genitive singular (много воды). State a quantity, then switch to the genitive automatically.

keyPoint: Неправда is a feminine noun meaning "an untruth, falsehood."

replies.ru: Я знал это с самого начала.
replies.gloss: I knew it from the start.

grammarFocus.construction: Вы понимаете + omitted что + the zero-copula nominal это неправда
grammarFocus.note: Dropping что in speech leaves the comma in place. неправда (untruth) is feminine, and with no present copula это неправда simply means "that is not true". Predicate nouns are nominative.

variations.note: With что restored — the written form.
ложь (a lie) is stronger, a feminine noun in -ь.
The particle же adds emphasis: "but that's simply not true!"

options.ru: Вы же понимаете, что это не так.
options.note: не так (not so) as the recast, with же pressing "you do realise".
соответствовать + dative, a formal "this does not correspond to the facts" — for documents.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы понимаете, что это неправда?

takeaway.pattern: не + noun fuses into one word (неправда, неудача, несчастье)
takeaway.note: правда → неправда: when не attaches as a prefix to a noun it is written solid. Negating a verb or predicate keeps не separate.

keyPoint: Драться is imperfective, meaning "to fight" (pairs with подраться).

grammarFocus.construction: не надо + imperfective infinitive драться + locational adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: драться (to brawl, to fight) carries reciprocal -ся, and the opponent is named with с + instrumental (драться с ним). не надо + imperfective makes a mild prohibition. здесь is locational.

variations.note: The polite/plural negative imperative; драться forms дерись / деритесь with a stem change (драть- → дер-).
с + instrumental names the opponent — obligatory for reciprocal verbs.
нельзя + infinitive, impersonal: "fighting is not allowed here", stated as a rule.

options.note: перестать + imperfective infinitive: "stop fighting" — halting something in progress.
давайте + perfective first person plural offers the alternative: "let's settle this calmly".

paraphrases.simplest: Здесь нельзя драться.

takeaway.pattern: reciprocal -ся names the other party with с + instrumental
takeaway.note: драться с кем / ссориться с кем / мириться с кем / встречаться с кем. These verbs never take an accusative (×драться его).

keyPoint: Честной is the instrumental form of честная (honest).

replies.gloss: That means a lot to me.

grammarFocus.construction: past была + instrumental честной + с + instrumental с тобой
grammarFocus.note: An adjective predicate with past быть can go instrumental (честной, feminine instrumental). The short form честна is also possible, but the instrumental is the more modern way of stating a quality. The other person takes с + instrumental.

variations.note: A male speaker: был + честным, with the instrumental agreeing in gender.
The short form честна is equally correct — a touch firmer and more literary.

variations.ru: Я всегда была честной с тобой.
variations.note: всегда (always) turns it into a sustained quality.

options.note: врать (to lie) takes the dative: "I didn't lie to you".
The говорить кому что frame: "I was telling you the truth".

paraphrases.simplest: Я была честна с тобой.

takeaway.pattern: a past adjective predicate takes the instrumental or the short form
takeaway.note: Он был умным (instrumental, a general quality) vs. Он был умён (short form, how he was at that moment). The present allows long and short forms; once быть appears, the instrumental joins the options.

keyPoint: Отменить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "canceling" (pairs with отменять).

grammarFocus.construction: надо + perfective infinitive отменить + accusative нашу встречу
grammarFocus.note: надо is a subjectless impersonal predicate, "it is necessary to". отменить (to cancel) is perfective and takes the accusative; встреча is feminine with the accusative встречу, and нашу is the matching feminine accusative possessive.

variations.note: The base form, stating the necessity with no subject.
Adding the dative нам makes it explicit who has to do it.
придётся is "we'll have to" — a stronger sense of no choice, still impersonal.

options.note: перенести is "to postpone" — rescheduling rather than cancelling.
The reflexive passive отменяется: "the meeting is cancelled" — the standard notice wording.

paraphrases.simplest: Надо отменить встречу.

takeaway.pattern: надо / нужно + infinitive is impersonal; the person goes dative
takeaway.note: Надо идти (one must go) / Мне надо идти (I have to go). There is no subject; the one under obligation is added in the dative. The negative не надо means "no need to".

keyPoint: Секретный is an adjective meaning "secret."

replies.ru: Да, он был спрятан за дверью.
replies.gloss: Yes, it was hidden behind a door.

grammarFocus.construction: видели + adjective agreement секретный вход
grammarFocus.note: вход (entrance) is masculine inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative, as does секретный. The perfective видели confirms the fact of seeing it. The noun itself comes from в + ход, the motion of going in.

variations.note: The base form: "did you see the secret entrance?"
Switching to найти shifts the focus to finding it.
Вы знаете, где... is the polite way to ask location; inside the clause the noun is nominative.

options.note: The есть + nominative existential: "is there a secret entrance here?"
незаметно (unnoticed) is a manner adverb; this asks about the method instead.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели секретный вход?

takeaway.note: The prefix contrast в- (in) / вы- (out) runs through nouns as well as verbs: входить/выходить, вход/выход. Learn the prefixes and the vocabulary multiplies.

keyPoint: Поработать is a perfective delimitative of работать, meaning "to work for a while."

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive поработать + locational adverb дома
grammarFocus.note: поработать is работать with по-, a perfective meaning "to do a bit of work". дома means "at home". The prefix sets a time frame, so the sense is getting some work done at home rather than working there permanently.

variations.note: The base form: "I'd like to get some work done at home".
The imperfective работать makes it a standing wish — to work from home as an arrangement.
работать над + instrumental is "to work on something" — the standard frame for naming the task.

options.ru: Я хочу остаться дома и поработать.
options.note: Pairing it with остаться (to stay) spells out the choice not to go out.
из дома (from home) is из + genitive — the modern way to ask about remote work.

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу поработать дома.
