takeaway.pattern: работать над + instrumental (work on) vs. работать в + prepositional (work at)
takeaway.note: работать над статьёй (on an article) / работать в банке (at a bank) / работать с клиентами (with clients). One verb, different prepositions, different meanings — learn the frames whole.

keyPoint: Спрятать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "hiding" (pairs with прятать).

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past спрятал + accusative ключ + locational adverb дома
grammarFocus.note: спрятать (to hide something) takes the accusative; the reflexive спрятаться means hiding oneself. ключ is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. дома (at home) is a locational adverb and does not decline.

variations.note: спрятала for a female speaker — the past agrees in gender.
в + prepositional в столе gives the precise place: "in the desk".
The plural ключи is inanimate, so again identical to the nominative.

options.note: лежать states where a thing lies, with ключ as the nominative subject.
оставить is "I left it at home" — implying forgetfulness rather than hiding.

paraphrases.simplest: Я спрятал ключ дома.

takeaway.pattern: дома covers location regardless of the verb
takeaway.note: дома takes no preposition, so it looks the same whether the verb is static or dynamic. в доме instead stresses the inside of that particular building.

keyPoint: Пострадать is perfective, with the resultative meaning "to suffer harm" (a related verb to страдать).

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past пострадал + на + prepositional работе
grammarFocus.note: пострадать (to be hurt, to suffer harm) is по- + страдать, a perfective intransitive with no object. на работе is the set на + prepositional for "at work" — ×в работе is not an option.

variations.note: пострадала for a female speaker.
в аварии (in an accident) uses в + prepositional, naming the event behind it.
сильно (badly) adds degree; as an adverb it never declines.

options.note: получить травму (to sustain an injury) takes the accusative and is more specific.
произойти с + instrumental, "happened to me"; несчастный случай is the formal word for an accident.

paraphrases.simplest: Я пострадал на работе.

takeaway.pattern: на работе / на заводе / на почте take на + prepositional
takeaway.note: Buildings as interiors take в (в доме, в банке), but words naming a workplace or institution as a sphere of activity take на (на работе, на уроке, на вокзале). It is fixed per word, so memorise the phrase.

keyPoint: Штаны is a plural-only noun meaning "pants/trousers."

grammarFocus.construction: купил + the plural-only noun штаны + agreeing adjective новые
grammarFocus.note: штаны (trousers) exists only in the plural and has no singular, so the adjective is plural новые and the accusative, being inanimate, matches the nominative. купить takes the accusative.

variations.note: брюки is also plural-only — more neutral and a shade smarter than штаны.
купила for a female speaker.
Counting a plural-only noun requires the collective numeral двое + genitive plural; ×два штана is impossible.

options.note: The у + genitive + nominative possessive: "I have new trousers".
взять себе (to get oneself something) is colloquial; себе is the reflexive dative.

paraphrases.simplest: Я купил новые штаны.

takeaway.pattern: plural-only nouns (штаны, брюки, очки, ножницы, деньги)
takeaway.note: With no singular, verbs and adjectives always agree in the plural (Деньги кончились, the money ran out). To count them use двое/трое + genitive plural, or a measure word like пара брюк.

keyPoint: Нервничать is imperfective, meaning "to be nervous."

grammarFocus.construction: negative imperative Не нервничай + перед + instrumental работой
grammarFocus.note: нервничать (to be nervous, to fret) is an imperfective intransitive, and negative imperatives take the imperfective, hence нервничай. перед + instrumental means "before" in time or space; the instrumental of работа is работой.

variations.note: The polite/plural form is нервничайте.
The instrumental экзаменом; the перед frame is unchanged.
волноваться also means "to worry" and is slightly broader than нервничать.

options.note: The imperative of the perfective успокоиться (to calm down) states it positively.
A set reassurance with the future будет: "everything will be fine".

paraphrases.simplest: Не нервничай перед работой.

takeaway.pattern: перед + instrumental = before, in time or space
takeaway.note: перед работой (before work) / перед домом (in front of the house). Time also allows до + genitive, but до measures the interval up to a point while перед means immediately before (до работы vs. перед работой).

keyPoint: Присесть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "sitting down briefly" (pairs with присаживаться).

grammarFocus.construction: Можно + perfective infinitive присесть + у + genitive окна
grammarFocus.note: можно is a subjectless impersonal predicate granting or seeking permission. присесть is сесть with при-, "to sit down for a moment" — a modest, tentative act. у + genitive means "by, next to"; the genitive of окно is окна.

variations.note: As a question it asks permission: "may I sit by the window?"
сесть is plain "to sit down"; присесть carries the sense of only briefly.
рядом с + instrumental is "next to" — easier to use with people than у + genitive.

options.note: The predicate adverb свободно: "is this seat free?" — the standard check.

options.ru: Вы не против, если я присяду?
options.note: Вы не против, если... is the polite permission formula; присяду is a perfective future.

paraphrases.simplest: Можно сесть у окна?

takeaway.pattern: у + genitive = by, at, at someone's place
takeaway.note: у окна (by the window) / у двери (by the door) / у врача (at the doctor's). It is the same preposition as in possessive у меня, but this locational use is just as frequent.

keyPoint: Притворяться is imperfective, meaning "to pretend" (pairs with притвориться).

grammarFocus.construction: не надо + imperfective infinitive притворяться + instrumental другом
grammarFocus.note: притворяться (to pretend to be) is a reflexive verb governing the instrumental; the instrumental of друг is другом. не надо + imperfective makes a mild prohibition: "don't pretend to be a friend".

variations.note: The base form, with другом in the instrumental as what is being feigned.
A direct negative imperative with the imperfective притворяйся.

variations.ru: Не надо притворяться, что тебе всё равно.
variations.note: A что clause lets you express the pretence as a whole sentence; всё равно is "not to care".

options.ru: Не делай вид, что ты мой друг.
options.note: делать вид, что... is the colloquial equivalent: "don't act as if".
The imperative of быть plus the instrumental честным: "just be honest".

paraphrases.simplest: Не притворяйся другом.

takeaway.note: притворяться больным (feign illness) / притворяться спящим (pretend to be asleep). Like казаться, считаться and становиться, this "appear as" family takes an instrumental complement.

keyPoint: Похитить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "kidnapping" (pairs with похищать).

grammarFocus.construction: хотели + perfective infinitive похитить + animate accusative моего друга
grammarFocus.note: похитить (to kidnap) takes the accusative. друг is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive — друга — and the possessive follows as моего. хотели is the plural past agreeing with они.

variations.note: The base form; the point is the agreement моего друга in the animate accusative.
For a feminine noun, мою сестру; animate feminine singular accusative ends in -у / -ю.
An impersonal plural with the accusative fronted puts the victim in focus.

options.note: The noun похищение (a kidnapping) sounds bureaucratic, like a news report.
пытаться + infinitive is "they tried to"; увезти is "to take away".

paraphrases.simplest: Они хотели похитить моего друга.

takeaway.pattern: in the animate accusative the possessive goes genitive too
takeaway.note: моего друга / твою сестру / нашего сына. The whole phrase shifts, not just the noun, so decide on animacy before choosing any ending.

keyPoint: Великолепно is an intensifying adverb meaning "magnificently."

grammarFocus.construction: выглядеть + the manner adverb великолепно
grammarFocus.note: выглядеть (to look, to appear) takes an adverb or an instrumental. The adverb великолепно (splendidly) is the default; with an adjective you would need the instrumental (выглядеть великолепной). сегодня is a time adverb.

variations.note: The base form — a very common compliment.
With вы, выглядите — the polite form.
Same meaning reordered; сегодня before the verb sounds conversational.

options.note: смотреться also means "to look" — used of mirrors and photographs, colloquially.
идти + dative means "to suit", with этот образ (this look) as the subject.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты выглядишь великолепно.

takeaway.note: Ты выглядишь хорошо (adverb) / Он выглядел усталым (instrumental). The adverb describes the impression, the instrumental a state or quality. A nominative is impossible (×выглядеть хороший).

keyPoint: Безопасный is an adjective meaning "safe."

grammarFocus.construction: считать + accusative это место + instrumental безопасным
grammarFocus.note: The считать что чем frame again. место is neuter inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative. The assessing adjective goes instrumental, and the neuter instrumental is identical to the masculine: безопасным.

variations.note: The base form — an instrumental assessment of a neuter noun.
A feminine noun takes the feminine instrumental безопасной.
A что clause turns it into the impersonal predicate adverb безопасно.

options.note: можно + a negated infinitive: "is it safe not to be afraid here?"; бояться takes the genitive.
Dative + спокойно, impersonal: "do you feel at ease here?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы думаете, что здесь безопасно?

takeaway.pattern: in the instrumental, masculine and neuter share one form (-ым / -им)
takeaway.note: безопасным (m/n) / безопасной (f) / безопасными (pl). The masculine-neuter distinction disappears, so only the feminine form has to be kept apart.

keyPoint: Благодарный is an adjective meaning "grateful."

grammarFocus.construction: the short adjective благодарен + dative тебе + за + accusative помощь
grammarFocus.note: благодарен (grateful) is a short form agreeing with the subject (благодарен / благодарна / благодарны). The person thanked goes in the dative and the reason in за + accusative. помощь is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative.

variations.note: благодарна for a female speaker.
The plural благодарны, with вам in the dative.
очень intensifies the gratitude; the за phrase can be dropped.

options.note: спасибо + dative + за + accusative — the everyday way to thank someone.
ценить + accusative, "I really value your help" — a slightly more formal thanks.

paraphrases.simplest: Спасибо за помощь.

takeaway.pattern: благодарен кому за что (dative + за + accusative)
takeaway.note: спасибо uses the same frame (спасибо тебе за всё). Gratitude in Russian always runs "person = dative, reason = за + accusative", so learn the pair and reuse it.

keyPoint: По-прежнему is an adverb meaning "still, as before."

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb по-прежнему + imperfective present живёт
grammarFocus.note: по-прежнему (as before, still) is formed from по- + прежний and is written with a hyphen. жить conjugates with an added в: живу / живёшь / живёт. здесь is a locational adverb.

variations.note: The base form: "she still lives here".
всё ещё is more colloquial than по-прежнему, with much the same meaning.
A plural subject takes живут.

options.note: так и + verb is a colloquial emphatic: "she's gone on living here all along".
никуда не + perfective past states it from the negative: "she hasn't moved anywhere".

paraphrases.simplest: Она всё ещё живёт здесь.

takeaway.note: по-прежнему, по-русски, по-моему, по-новому. These hyphenated adverbs mean "in such-and-such a way" and never decline.

keyPoint: Дождаться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "waiting until someone arrives" (pairs with дожидаться).

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past дождался + genitive тебя
grammarFocus.note: дождаться (to wait until someone finally comes) is a reflexive perfective governing the genitive; тебя is the genitive of ты (identical to the accusative). The prefix до- adds "all the way to the end", so the waiting succeeded.

variations.note: The base form: дождался for a man, дождалась for a woman.
The imperfective ждать also takes genitive or accusative, but describes only the waiting, with no outcome.
Negated, it means the waiting ended without success: "I gave up waiting for you".

options.note: The perfective увидеть states only the result: "I finally saw you".
всё-таки (after all) stresses that it took some doing.

paraphrases.simplest: Я ждал тебя здесь.

takeaway.pattern: ждать (waiting as process) vs. дождаться + genitive (waiting rewarded)
takeaway.note: до- marks attainment (дождаться, добиться, доехать). дождаться governs the genitive, which shows clearly on nouns — дождаться автобуса, дождаться ответа — even if тебя happens to look the same as the accusative.

keyPoint: Вовремя is an adverb meaning "on time."

replies.gloss: Thanks, I tried not to be late.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past пришёл + adverb вовремя + time adverb сегодня
grammarFocus.note: The masculine past of прийти (to arrive) is the irregular пришёл. вовремя (on time) is written as one word, in contrast with во время (during). сегодня is also an adverb.

variations.note: пришла for a woman; the forms are пришёл / пришла / пришло / пришли.
With вы the past is always the plural пришли.
опоздать (to be late) is the opposite — learn it alongside вовремя.

options.note: The same thing from the negative side: "you weren't late today".
A set phrase with как раз (just): "you're right on time", with no copula in the present.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты пришёл вовремя.

takeaway.pattern: вовремя (one word, adverb) vs. во время + genitive (during)
takeaway.note: Он пришёл вовремя (he arrived on time) / Он позвонил во время урока (he rang during the lesson). A classic near-homophone pair distinguished only by the spacing.

keyPoint: Причинить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "causing" (pairs with причинять).

replies.ru: Я знаю, что ты не хотел.
replies.gloss: I know you didn't mean to.

grammarFocus.construction: не хотел + perfective infinitive причинить + accusative боль
grammarFocus.note: причинить (to cause) is perfective and takes the accusative; причинить боль (to cause pain) is set. боль is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative. The person affected is added in the dative (причинить тебе боль).

variations.ru: Я не хотел причинить тебе боль.
variations.note: Adding the dative тебе makes the affected person explicit.
хотела for a female speaker.
With вред (harm): "I didn't mean to do any harm" — причинить вред is equally set.

options.note: обидеть takes the accusative, "to hurt someone's feelings" — far more everyday.
было больно is an impersonal past: "sorry if it hurt".

paraphrases.simplest: Я не хотел тебя обидеть.

takeaway.note: причинить боль / вред / неудобство / ущерб — all of them "inflict something bad". It never takes a positive object (×причинить радость), so treat причинить as reserved for harm.

keyPoint: Застрять is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting stuck" (pairs with застревать).

replies.gloss: How long have you been there?

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past застряли + на + prepositional дороге
grammarFocus.note: застрять (to get stuck) is a perfective intransitive, with the place given by на or в + prepositional. The prepositional of дорога is дороге, and на дороге means "on the road".

variations.note: The base form: "we got stuck on the road".
в пробке (in a traffic jam) uses в + prepositional — by far the commonest pairing.
в лифте (in the lift): enclosed spaces take в.

options.note: двигаться (to move) with дальше (further) explains the situation instead.
задержать + accusative, "the jam held us up" — a transitive recast with пробка as subject.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы застряли в пробке.

takeaway.note: в пробке / в лифте / на дороге / на мосту. Enclosed spaces take в, surfaces and routes take на. застрять only states location and never takes a directional accusative.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Сериал is a masculine noun meaning "TV series."

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present смотрим + accusative новый сериал
grammarFocus.note: смотреть takes the accusative. сериал is masculine inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative and новый stays unchanged. The present can mean "we are watching now" or "we watch regularly".

variations.note: The base form: "we're watching a new series".
The perfective посмотрели means watching it through to the end.
The plural новые сериалы is inanimate, so again nominative-shaped.

options.note: начать + imperfective infinitive marks the start: "we've started watching".
Dative + нравится + nominative shifts the topic to liking it.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы смотрим новый сериал.

takeaway.pattern: the Russian present does not separate progressive from habitual
takeaway.note: Мы смотрим сериал covers both "we're watching it now" and "we watch it regularly". Context or adverbs like сейчас / обычно make the difference; there is no dedicated be -ing form.

keyPoint: Ерунда is a feminine noun meaning "nonsense, trivial matter."

replies.ru: Не совсем, у меня другое мнение.
replies.gloss: Not quite, I have a different opinion.

grammarFocus.construction: Вы думаете + omitted что + the zero-copula это ерунда
grammarFocus.note: что may be dropped in speech but the comma stays. ерунда (nonsense, a trifle) is feminine, and with no present copula это ерунда means "that's nonsense". Predicate nouns are nominative.

variations.note: With что restored — the written form.
считать takes accusative + instrumental, hence ерундой — the construction changes the case.
Reordered, with the parenthetical по-вашему set off by a comma.

options.note: The predicate adverb неважно judges it as unimportant.
казаться + instrumental пустяком; пустяк is "a trifle".

paraphrases.simplest: Вы думаете, это ерунда?

takeaway.pattern: думать что... takes a nominative predicate; считать takes the instrumental
takeaway.note: Вы думаете, что это ерунда (nominative) vs. Вы считаете это ерундой (instrumental). Same thought, different frames — the verb settles the case.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Тренер is a masculine noun meaning "coach/trainer."

grammarFocus.construction: знать + animate accusative хорошего тренера
grammarFocus.note: знать takes the accusative. тренер is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive — тренера — and the adjective follows as хорошего. The sentence is the standard way to ask for a recommendation.

variations.note: The base form; the agreement in the animate accusative is the point.
The feminine тренерша is colloquial; animate feminine singular accusative ends in -ую / -у.
The plural is animate too, so genitive-shaped: хороших тренеров.

options.note: порекомендовать + accusative: "could you recommend one?" — politer and more specific.
у + genitive + есть + nominative: "do you know a coach personally?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы знаете хорошего тренера?

takeaway.pattern: the animate accusative puts adjectives in genitive form too (-ого / -его)
takeaway.note: хорошего тренера / нового врача / моего брата. Inanimates keep the nominative shape (хороший фильм), so person or thing changes the whole ending.

keyPoint: Срочно is an adverb meaning "urgently."

replies.gloss: Yes, I have an important meeting.

grammarFocus.construction: adverb срочно + the indefinite куда-то + imperfective present спешите
grammarFocus.note: спешить (to hurry) is intransitive, and the destination is given by the indefinite directional adverb куда-то ("somewhere"). The -то suffix means the place is real but unspecified. срочно (urgently) is a manner adverb.

variations.note: The base form without срочно: "are you off somewhere in a hurry?"
куда-нибудь is "anywhere at all" — vaguer than куда-то.
на + accusative names the destination: "are you rushing to work?"

options.note: торопиться also means "to hurry" and is just as common in speech.
мало + genitive времени: "are you short of time?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы куда-то спешите?

takeaway.note: The stem changes with direction, location and source. The -то vs. -нибудь contrast (real but unknown vs. any at all) works the same here as with pronouns.

keyPoint: Супер is an indeclinable adjective/exclamation borrowed from English "super."

grammarFocus.construction: Вы думаете + zero copula + the indeclinable predicate супер
grammarFocus.note: супер is an indeclinable borrowing from English that works as both adjective and predicate in speech (этот фильм супер = this film is great). It never declines or agrees. что is absent here, but the comma remains.

variations.note: The base form, with the colloquial evaluation word as the predicate.
отличный is the normative adjective — the choice when tidying up the style.
Dative + понравился, with этот фильм as the subject.

options.note: классный (great) is also colloquial but, unlike супер, it agrees and declines.

options.ru: Вы в восторге от этого фильма?
options.note: быть в восторге от + genitive is "to be thrilled by" — a more formal set phrase.

paraphrases.simplest: Вам понравился этот фильм?

takeaway.pattern: супер / окей / класс are indeclinable colloquial evaluators
takeaway.note: Convenient because they never change, but strictly spoken register. In writing or at work use отличный / прекрасный / замечательный instead.

keyPoint: Дурацкий is a colloquial adjective meaning "silly, stupid."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past задали + accusative дурацкий вопрос
grammarFocus.note: задать вопрос (to ask a question) takes the accusative, and the person asked goes in the dative (задать вопрос ему). вопрос is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. дурацкий (stupid) is colloquial and rather rude.

variations.note: глупый is the more neutral word; дурацкий is blunt and dismissive.
Adding the dative ему shows the two-slot frame: "did you ask him a question?"
With ты, задал for a man, задала for a woman.

options.note: спросить + accusative; что-то глупое is a neuter indefinite pronoun plus adjective.
неудачный (ill-chosen) softens it; past был + nominative predicate.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы задали глупый вопрос?

takeaway.pattern: задать вопрос кому (accusative thing + dative person)
takeaway.note: спросить кого puts the person in the accusative, while задать вопрос кому puts them in the dative — opposite cases. Learn the pair: Я спросил его / Я задал ему вопрос.

keyPoint: Чудесный is an adjective meaning "wonderful, marvelous."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past выбрали + accusative чудесное место
grammarFocus.note: выбрать (to choose) is perfective and takes the accusative. место is neuter inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative and the adjective is the neuter чудесное. The exclamation mark makes it a compliment.

variations.note: The base form: "you've picked a wonderful spot!"
With a masculine noun, чудесный — the adjective agrees in gender.
Какое + neuter adjective makes it an exclamation: "what a wonderful place!"

options.note: The predicate adverb чудесно, impersonal: "it's lovely here!"
The noun выбор (choice) gives a short compliment, left in the nominative.

paraphrases.simplest: Отличный выбор!

takeaway.note: чудесное место / новое окно / хорошее дело. Since the accusative matches the nominative, neuter nouns never show the difference between the two.

keyPoint: Наверх is an adverb of direction meaning "up, upstairs."

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Иди + directional adverb наверх + к + dative ко мне
grammarFocus.note: иди is the imperative of идти. наверх means "upwards" (the locational form is наверху). к + dative means "to someone", and the dative of я is мне — with к becoming ко before the consonant cluster.

variations.note: The base form, combining a directional adverb with к + dative.
The polite/plural form идите.
The perfective imperative of подняться: "come up to me".

options.note: зайти is "to drop by" and pairs naturally with ко мне.
наверху is the locational form: "I'm waiting for you upstairs".

paraphrases.simplest: Иди ко мне.

takeaway.pattern: ко мне is к with a phonetic buffer
takeaway.note: к becomes ко before awkward consonant clusters (ко мне, ко всем, ко вторнику). The same happens with с → со (со мной), в → во (во всём) and о → об / обо (об этом, обо всём).

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Дьявол is a masculine noun meaning "devil."

replies.ru: Не совсем, но это интересная тема.
replies.gloss: Not really, but it's an interesting topic.

grammarFocus.construction: верить в + animate accusative дьявола
grammarFocus.note: верить в + accusative means believing in the existence of something. дьявол is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive: дьявола. The point is that the animacy rule still applies after a preposition.

variations.note: The base form, with the animate accusative дьявола.
Бог is animate too, hence Бога, conventionally capitalised.
чудеса (miracles) is inanimate, so it keeps the nominative shape — the contrast is visible.

options.note: Spelling it out with существовать; the что clause takes a comma.
The short plural религиозны: "are you religious?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы верите в дьявола?

takeaway.pattern: the animacy rule survives after prepositions
takeaway.note: в дьявола / за друга / про шерифов — once a preposition calls for the accusative, animates still show genitive forms. Decide the case first, then check animacy.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Куртка is a feminine noun meaning "jacket."

grammarFocus.construction: видели + the possessive мою + accusative куртку
grammarFocus.note: куртка (jacket) is feminine with the accusative куртку, and мою is the matching feminine accusative possessive. Because it is about something lost, a negated question is the politer option.

variations.note: The negated question — the polite formula for lost property.
The masculine шарф keeps мой unchanged (inanimate, so nominative-shaped).
With ты, видел for a man, видела for a woman.

options.ru: Вы не знаете, где моя куртка?
options.note: Вы не знаете, где... politely asks location; inside the clause the noun is nominative.
положить (to put) with куда, musing aloud: "where did I put that jacket?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы не видели мою куртку?

takeaway.note: мою куртку / твою сумку / нашу машину. Masculine inanimates show no change (мой шарф), so the noun's gender decides how visible the accusative is.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Чушь is a feminine noun meaning "nonsense."

replies.gloss: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.

replies.ru: Почему ты думаешь, что это чушь?
replies.gloss: Why do you think it's nonsense?

grammarFocus.construction: negative imperative Не говори + accusative эту чушь
grammarFocus.note: Negative imperatives take the imperfective, говори. чушь (rubbish) is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative, and the demonstrative is эту (feminine singular accusative). A negative imperative can keep the accusative; the genitive is not required.

variations.note: The base form: "don't talk that rubbish".
The polite/plural говорите.
The genitive plural глупостей — the alternative negated pattern: "don't talk nonsense".

options.note: перестать + imperfective infinitive: "stop talking nonsense"; ерунду is accusative.
полная чушь (utter rubbish) judges the content instead; nominative predicate.

paraphrases.simplest: Не говори ерунду.

takeaway.pattern: a negated imperative may take either accusative or genitive
takeaway.note: Не говори эту чушь (a specific thing, accusative) vs. Не говори глупостей (vague and general, genitive plural). The more specific the object, the more likely the accusative.

keyPoint: Расстаться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "breaking up" (pairs with расставаться).

grammarFocus.construction: решить + perfective infinitive расстаться + time adverb вчера
grammarFocus.note: решить + infinitive means "decided to". расстаться (to part) is a reciprocal perfective with -ся, and the other person takes с + instrumental (расстаться с ним). вчера is a time adverb.

variations.note: The base form: "we decided yesterday to split up".
Stating the parting itself rather than the decision; perfective past.
с + instrumental с ней names the other person — obligatory with a singular subject.

options.note: разойтись is "to go separate ways" — gentler and broader than расстаться.
между + instrumental нами with the short participle кончено: "it's over between us".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы расстались вчера.

takeaway.note: решить уехать (decide to leave) / решить задачу (solve a problem). The same verb shifts meaning depending on what follows it.

keyPoint: Красиво is an adverb meaning "beautifully."

replies.gloss: Is this a special song for you?

grammarFocus.construction: time adverb сегодня + manner adverb красиво + imperfective present поёшь
grammarFocus.note: красиво (beautifully) is a manner adverb modifying the verb. петь conjugates irregularly with ё: пою / поёшь / поёт. When two adverbs stack up, the natural order is time then manner.

variations.note: The base form: "you're singing beautifully today".
With вы, поёте — the polite form.
The perfective past спела (feminine): "you sang that beautifully" — judging one performance.

options.note: у + genitive + nominative, with the adjective красивый modifying the noun.
Dative + нравится plus a как clause: "I like the way you sing".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты красиво поёшь.

takeaway.pattern: adverbs in -о modify verbs; adjectives modify nouns
takeaway.note: красиво поёшь (adverb) vs. красивый голос (adjective). The -о form doubles as both adverb and short neuter, so judge the role by what it attaches to.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Полдень is a masculine noun meaning "noon."

replies.ru: Что ты будешь делать до этого?
replies.gloss: What will you do until then?

grammarFocus.construction: perfective future вернусь + в + accusative полдень
grammarFocus.note: вернуться (to come back) is a reflexive perfective, so the conjugated form itself is the future (вернусь = I'll be back). в полдень (at noon) is a в + accusative time expression; полдень is masculine with accusative = nominative.

variations.note: The base form: "I'll be back at noon".
полночь (midnight) is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative — same pattern.
в + accusative два часа, "at two o'clock" — clock times take в + accusative.

options.note: The future of быть plus a locational adverb: "I'll be here at noon".
к + dative полудню means "by noon" — a deadline rather than a point.

paraphrases.simplest: Я вернусь в полдень.

takeaway.pattern: clock times and weekdays take в + accusative; deadlines take к + dative
takeaway.note: в полдень / в среду / в два часа (a point in time) vs. к полудню / к среде (by then). в is "at", к is "by".

keyPoint: Дважды is an adverb meaning "twice."

grammarFocus.construction: the frequency adverb дважды + imperfective past звонил + dative тебе
grammarFocus.note: дважды (twice) is a frequency adverb, the bookish equivalent of два раза. звонить governs the dative, hence тебе. The imperfective past reports the repeated act of calling and sits naturally with дважды.

variations.note: два раза is the colloquial version; дважды is written and slightly formal.
звонила for a female speaker.
The perfective позвонил with дважды also works, treating each call as completed.

options.note: дозвониться uses до- for attainment, "to get through": "I tried to reach you".
Negating брать трубку (to pick up): "you didn't answer" — stated from the other side.

paraphrases.simplest: Я два раза звонил тебе.

takeaway.pattern: однажды / дважды / трижды (formal) = один раз / два раза / три раза (colloquial)
takeaway.note: From four up only the numeral + раз form is normal (четыре раза); четырежды is rare. And звонить always takes the dative — never ×звонил тебя.

keyPoint: Дружище is an affectionate term of address derived from друг (friend), meaning "buddy, pal."

grammarFocus.construction: the address Дружище + the adverb опять + zero copula
grammarFocus.note: дружище is an augmentative, affectionate form of друг — "mate, buddy". As an address it takes a comma. With no present copula, ты опять здесь? is simply "you're here again?"

variations.note: The base form — casual address to a close male friend.
друг is neutral; дружище is markedly familiar and not for anyone senior.
снова is a slightly more neutral synonym of опять, with the address dropped.

options.note: Какими судьбами? is an instrumental idiom, "what brings you here?", for a surprise reunion.
Что, ... ? is a colloquial challenge; the perfective пришёл states the arrival.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты опять здесь?

takeaway.note: Where -ик / -очка diminish, -ище enlarges or intensifies affection. дружище is close to "brother" in tone — and decidedly informal.

skeleton.note: 3rd person plural present, the target word

keyPoint: Потрясать is imperfective, meaning "to shock/amaze" (pairs with потрясти).

replies.gloss: Yes, especially with a surprise ending.

grammarFocus.construction: the relative pronoun которые + imperfective present потрясают
grammarFocus.note: который agrees in gender and number with its antecedent — here истории (feminine plural) — while its case comes from its role in the clause: subject, so nominative plural которые. потрясать (to shake, to stun) takes the accusative but can also stand objectless, "to be stunning".

variations.note: The base form, with которые as the clause subject.

variations.ru: Вы любите истории, которые вас потрясают?
variations.note: Adding the accusative вас names who is shaken.
The active participle потрясающие compresses the whole clause into one word.

options.note: шокирующий is a borrowed-root adjective: "shocking".
любить, когда... is the set "to like it when..."; the comma is obligatory.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы любите потрясающие истории?

takeaway.pattern: который agrees with the antecedent but takes its case from the clause
takeaway.note: книга, которая лежит (nominative) / книга, которую я читаю (accusative) / книга, о которой я говорю (prepositional). Agreement and case are separate decisions.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Пушка is a feminine noun meaning "cannon."

replies.gloss: Yes, that was an impressive scene.

grammarFocus.construction: видели + accusative пушку + в + prepositional фильме
grammarFocus.note: пушка (cannon; slangily a gun) is feminine with the accusative пушку. в фильме is the locative prepositional. The word properly means a cannon, but in crime films it is slang for a handgun.

variations.note: The base form — readable as either cannon or gun, depending on context.
пистолет is the neutral word for a handgun, avoiding the slang.
эту пушку narrows it down, with feminine singular accusative agreement.

options.note: оружие (weaponry) is a neuter collective; было + nominative is existential.

options.ru: Вы заметили, чем он был вооружён?
options.note: чем (instrumental interrogative) with the short participle вооружён: "what he was armed with".

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели пистолет в фильме?

takeaway.note: The literal sense (артиллерийская пушка) coexists with the slang one. The slang belongs to crime-drama register, so say пистолет or оружие to stay neutral.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, plural accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Монстр is a masculine noun borrowed from English "monster."

replies.gloss: A little, especially in the dark.

grammarFocus.construction: бояться + genitive plural монстров
grammarFocus.note: бояться (to fear) is a reflexive verb governing the genitive. монстр is animate masculine, and its genitive plural is монстров. The crucial point is that it takes the genitive, not the accusative.

variations.note: The base form, with the genitive plural монстров.
The genitive темноты: "are you afraid of the dark?"
The genitive demonstrative этого — бояться always takes the genitive.

options.note: Dative + страшно, impersonal, plus от + genitive: "do monsters frighten you?"
пугать + accusative reverses the roles: "do monsters scare you?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы боитесь монстров?

takeaway.note: бояться собак / бояться смерти / бояться ошибки. Only a few emotion verbs take the genitive — бояться, стесняться, стыдиться — but they are frequent, so learn them as a set.

keyPoint: Трус is a masculine noun meaning "coward."

replies.ru: Я никогда и не думал этого.

grammarFocus.construction: negated zero copula + the predicate noun трус
grammarFocus.note: With no present-tense copula, negation is simply не + noun: Я не трус, "I am not a coward". трус is an animate masculine noun but stays nominative as a predicate. In the past it would be был не трусом (instrumental).

variations.note: The base form — a common flat denial.
The feminine трусиха, colloquial in tone.
The past takes the instrumental трусом, because быть is present.

options.note: Negating бояться states the condition: "I'm not afraid".

options.ru: Я докажу, что я не трус.
options.note: доказать что... is "to prove that"; the clause takes a comma.

paraphrases.simplest: Я не трус.

takeaway.pattern: a negated predicate noun stays nominative in the present
takeaway.note: Я не врач / Это не проблема — just add не before the nominative. Once быть appears in the past or future, it switches to the instrumental (Он не был врачом).

keyPoint: Болтать is imperfective, meaning "to chat" (pairs with поболтать).

replies.gloss: What do you usually talk about?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + imperfective infinitive болтать + после + genitive работы
grammarFocus.note: любить + infinitive always takes the imperfective, since a preference is habitual. болтать (to chat) is a colloquial imperfective-only verb. после + genitive means "after", and the genitive of работа is работы.

variations.note: The base form: "we love chatting after work".
The perfective поболтать means "have a bit of a chat"; the imperfective is standard after любить, but this is heard colloquially.
With the frequency adverb часто, stated as a fact rather than a preference.

options.note: общаться (to socialise) is more neutral than болтать; dative + нравится.
With поговорить (talk a while) and the time phrase moved to the front.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы любим болтать после работы.

takeaway.pattern: после + genitive (after), перед + instrumental (before), во время + genitive (during)
takeaway.note: Each time preposition takes a different case. Drilling после работы / перед работой / во время работы with one noun fixes all three.

keyPoint: Сдаваться is imperfective, meaning "to give up" (pairs with сдаться).

grammarFocus.construction: не собираюсь + imperfective infinitive сдаваться
grammarFocus.note: собираться + infinitive means "to intend to", and negating it expresses firm resolve. сдаваться (to surrender, to give up) is the imperfective reflexive; the perfective is сдаться. Negated intention fits the imperfective.

variations.note: The base form: "I have no intention of giving up".
Negating the perfective future сдамся is blunter: "I will not surrender".
A plural subject takes собираемся.

options.note: Imperfective future with до конца: "I'll fight to the end".
Negating the perfective future of отступить: "I won't back down".

paraphrases.simplest: Я не сдамся.

takeaway.note: Я собираюсь уехать (I'm going to leave). The verb literally means "to gather", but with an infinitive it expresses intention; не собираюсь is an emphatic refusal.

keyPoint: Скучный is an adjective meaning "boring."

grammarFocus.construction: считать + accusative этот фильм + instrumental скучным
grammarFocus.note: The считать что чем frame, with the assessing adjective in the instrumental. фильм is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and the masculine instrumental of скучный is скучным.

variations.note: The base form, with скучным carrying the verdict.
A feminine noun takes the feminine instrumental скучной.
Dative + было скучно, impersonal: "were you bored?", asking about the feeling.

options.note: Dative + понравился, negated — a tentative way to ask for an opinion.
увлечь + accusative is "to captivate"; negated: "it didn't draw you in?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вам было скучно?

takeaway.pattern: скучный (boring, of a thing) vs. скучно (bored, impersonal)
takeaway.note: Фильм скучный (the film is boring — a property) vs. Мне скучно (I'm bored — a state). Properties take adjectives; a person's feelings take dative + predicate adverb.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Миссия is a feminine noun meaning "mission."

grammarFocus.construction: понимать + accusative нашу общую миссию
grammarFocus.note: понимать takes the accusative. миссия is feminine with the accusative миссию, and both modifiers — the possessive нашу and the adjective общую — take the same feminine singular accusative ending. Stacked modifiers simply repeat the pattern.

variations.note: The base form, with two modifiers sharing one ending.
задача (task) is also feminine, accusative задачу.
The masculine план gives наш общий план, identical to the nominative.

options.note: The short form ясна plus a dative: "is our mission clear to you?", with миссия as nominative subject.
разделять + accusative is "to share (a goal)"; цель is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы понимаете нашу миссию?

takeaway.pattern: every modifier agrees with the noun
takeaway.note: нашу общую миссию / этот новый дом / моих старых друзей. However many possessives, adjectives or numerals pile up, they all match the noun's gender, number and case.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Тарелка is a feminine noun meaning "plate."

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Поставь + accusative тарелку + на + accusative стол
grammarFocus.note: The imperative of поставить (to stand something up). The destination takes на + accusative for direction; на столе (prepositional) would mean "on the table" as a location. тарелка is feminine with the accusative тарелку.

variations.note: The polite/plural form поставьте.
положить is "to lay flat"; a plate normally takes поставить, though положить is also used.
стоять + prepositional states the location — the contrast with the directional accusative.

options.note: можешь + infinitive recasts it as a polite request.
A verbless dash construction, common in spoken instructions.

paraphrases.simplest: Поставь тарелку на стол.

takeaway.note: поставить что куда (accusative) → стоять где (prepositional), and likewise положить / лежать. Putting takes the directional accusative; being there takes the locative prepositional.

keyPoint: Повсюду is an adverb meaning "everywhere."

grammarFocus.construction: вижу + accusative plural цветы + the place adverb повсюду
grammarFocus.note: цветы (flowers) is inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative. повсюду (everywhere) is a locational adverb needing neither preposition nor case. Note also that the singular цветок has an irregular plural, цветы.

variations.note: The base form: "I see flowers everywhere".
The singular цветок with на + prepositional — the stems differ between singular and plural.
A verbless nominal sentence; the present needs no быть.

options.note: везде is the more colloquial synonym of повсюду.
в + prepositional plural цветах: "everything around is covered in flowers"; вокруг is an adverb.

paraphrases.simplest: Цветы повсюду.

takeaway.note: Quite a few nouns change stem in the plural: человек → люди, ребёнок → дети, цветок → цветы. The plural has to be learnt separately.

keyPoint: Сдаться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "giving up" (pairs with сдаваться).

grammarFocus.construction: не можем + perfective infinitive сдаться
grammarFocus.note: сдаться (to surrender) is the perfective reflexive, with сдаваться as its imperfective. не можем + a perfective infinitive expresses moral impossibility: "we cannot bring ourselves to".

variations.note: The base form: "we can't give up".
должны + imperfective infinitive: "we must not give up" — negated obligation.
A singular subject takes могу.

options.note: нельзя + imperfective infinitive, impersonal: "giving up is not allowed".
надо + держаться (to hold on) states the positive alternative.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы не можем сдаться.

takeaway.pattern: нельзя + perfective = impossible; нельзя + imperfective = forbidden
takeaway.note: Нельзя сдаться (it's impossible to surrender) vs. Нельзя сдаваться (one must not give up). Aspect alone flips "cannot" into "must not" — a key contrast.

keyPoint: Упустить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "missing" something (pairs with упускать).

replies.ru: Я помогу тебе не упустить это.
replies.gloss: I'll help you not miss it.

grammarFocus.construction: бояться + perfective infinitive упустить + accusative момент
grammarFocus.note: бояться takes the genitive with a noun, but with an infinitive the case question disappears. упустить (to miss, to let slip) is perfective and takes the accusative; момент is masculine inanimate, hence nominative-shaped. The phrase means fearing to miss the moment.

variations.note: The base form, with бояться plus an infinitive.
шанс is likewise masculine inanimate — same pattern.
Another бояться + infinitive: "I'm afraid of being late".

options.note: Negating хотеть turns fear into intention.
надо + a negated infinitive: "we mustn't let the moment slip".

paraphrases.simplest: Я боюсь упустить момент.

takeaway.pattern: бояться + genitive (a noun) vs. бояться + infinitive (an action)
takeaway.note: боюсь собак (afraid of dogs, genitive) / боюсь упустить (afraid of missing out, infinitive). The genitive government shows only with nouns, so look at what follows.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Ловушка is a feminine noun meaning "trap."

replies.gloss: Yes, we need to be careful.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present видите + place adverb здесь + accusative ловушку
grammarFocus.note: видеть takes the accusative. ловушка (trap) is feminine with the accusative ловушку. здесь is a locational adverb. The present видите checks what is visible right now.

variations.note: The base form: "do you see a trap here?"
Under negation the object becomes genitive: ловушки.
With ты, видишь — only the ending changes.

options.note: The есть + nominative existential: "is there a trap here?"

options.ru: Вам не кажется, что это ловушка?
options.note: Dative + кажется plus a что clause: "don't you think it's a trap?"

paraphrases.simplest: Здесь есть ловушка?

takeaway.pattern: an object under negation may go genitive
takeaway.note: Я вижу ловушку (accusative) / Я не вижу ловушки (genitive). The genitive of negation survives with verbs of perception and possession, though a specific object can keep the accusative.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, plural accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Совпадение is a neuter noun meaning "coincidence."

grammarFocus.construction: верить в + accusative plural совпадения
grammarFocus.note: верить в + accusative means believing in the existence of something. совпадение (coincidence) is neuter, and the accusative plural совпадения matches the nominative. Neuter nouns never distinguish nominative from accusative, singular or plural.

variations.note: The base form, with the neuter plural accusative совпадения.
случайность (chance) is a feminine -ь noun whose accusative plural also matches the nominative.
In a что clause it reverts to the nominative singular совпадение.

options.note: считать + accusative + instrumental случайностью — the construction changes the case.
The neuter perfective past of совпасть: "did it just happen to coincide?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы верите в совпадения?

takeaway.pattern: neuter nouns: nominative = accusative in both numbers
takeaway.note: совпадение / совпадения, место / места, окно / окна. Since the forms never differ, word order and the verb tell you which role the noun plays.

keyPoint: Похороны is a plural-only noun meaning "funeral."

grammarFocus.construction: the plural-only noun похороны + the future of быть, будут
grammarFocus.note: похороны (a funeral) exists only in the plural, so the verb agrees in the plural: будут. The possessive его is indeclinable. завтра is a time adverb. Future existence is будет / будут + nominative.

variations.note: The base form; the plural agreement будут is the point.
The past is likewise plural, были: "the funeral was yesterday".
когда asks the date, with the possessive dropped.

options.note: похоронить + accusative as an impersonal plural: "he will be buried tomorrow".
состояться (to take place) is the verb of formal announcements; прощание (the farewell service) is neuter singular.

paraphrases.simplest: Похороны будут завтра.

takeaway.note: With no singular, verbs and adjectives are always plural (Каникулы начались, the holidays have started). часы is plural-only in the sense of "clock", distinct from the plural of час (hour).

keyPoint: Ведьма is a feminine noun meaning "witch."

replies.gloss: That's just a figure of speech, right?

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + adjective настоящая + the predicate noun ведьма
grammarFocus.note: No present-tense copula. настоящая ведьма is feminine singular nominative, and the predicate noun stays nominative. эта женщина is the subject. Figuratively it calls someone "an absolute witch".

variations.note: The base form, with a nominative predicate noun.
With the past была the phrase turns instrumental: настоящей ведьмой.
For a man, настоящий колдун — the whole phrase shifts gender.

options.note: The long form злая used predicatively — colloquial: "she's simply nasty".
с + instrumental with невозможно + infinitive: "there's no reasoning with her" — concrete rather than abusive.

paraphrases.simplest: Эта женщина настоящая ведьма.

takeaway.note: настоящий друг (a true friend) / настоящий кошмар (an absolute nightmare). It intensifies in either direction, so context decides whether the verdict is good or bad.

keyPoint: Вампир is a masculine noun meaning "vampire."

grammarFocus.construction: выглядеть + как + nominative вампир
grammarFocus.note: Besides an adverb or instrumental, выглядеть can take как + nominative, "to look like". Nothing after как is governed, so вампир stays nominative. A short comparative phrase with как takes no preceding comma.

variations.note: The base form, как + nominative.
The instrumental усталым states a condition, with no как.
как + adjective + nominative; the modifier is nominative too.

options.note: похож на + accusative means "you resemble"; the short form похож agrees in gender and number.

options.ru: У тебя вид как у вампира.
options.note: вид (appearance) with как у + genitive: "you have the look of a vampire".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты похож на вампира.

takeaway.pattern: как + nominative (like) vs. похож на + accusative (resembles)
takeaway.note: как leaves the case alone, but похож demands на + accusative. Он как ребёнок / Он похож на ребёнка — the same comparison, different frames.

keyPoint: Одеваться is imperfective, meaning "to get dressed" (pairs with одеться).

replies.gloss: How much time do you need?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + imperfective infinitive одеваться + manner adverb быстро
grammarFocus.note: любить + infinitive takes the imperfective, since preferences are habitual. одеваться is одевать plus -ся, a reflexive that takes no object: you dress yourself. быстро is a manner adverb.

variations.note: The base form: "I like getting dressed quickly".
красиво (nicely) turns it into "I like dressing well".
The plain present states the fact; одеваюсь is the reflexive first person.

options.note: Dative + нравится + infinitive: "I enjoy dressing quickly".
собираться is "to get ready" — broader than just dressing.

paraphrases.simplest: Я одеваюсь быстро.

takeaway.note: Я одеваю ребёнка (I dress the child) / Я одеваюсь (I get dressed). For putting on a specific garment there is a separate verb, надевать что: надеть пальто.

keyPoint: Повесить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "hanging" something (pairs with вешать).

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Повесь + accusative это + на + accusative дверь
grammarFocus.note: повесь is the imperative of повесить (to hang). The destination takes на + accusative for direction, and дверь, a feminine -ь noun, has an identical accusative. на двери (prepositional) would mean it is hanging there.

variations.note: The polite/plural form повесьте.
The accusative стену: "hang it on the wall".
висеть + prepositional states location — the contrast with the directional accusative.

options.note: можешь + infinitive recasts it as a request.
пусть + third person: "let it hang on the door", with the locative prepositional.

paraphrases.simplest: Повесь это на дверь.

takeaway.note: The transitive member takes на / в + accusative for direction; the intransitive one takes на / в + prepositional for location. Learn the three pairs together and the case switch becomes automatic.

keyPoint: Винить is imperfective, denoting the state of blaming; the related обвинить means "to accuse/charge," a distinct sense.

grammarFocus.construction: не надо + imperfective infinitive винить + the reflexive pronoun себя
grammarFocus.note: винить (to blame) takes the accusative, with the charge in в + prepositional. себя is the reflexive pronoun pointing back to the subject and has no nominative. не надо + imperfective makes a gentle prohibition.

variations.note: The base form: "don't blame yourself".
A direct negative imperative with the imperfective вини.

variations.ru: Не надо винить себя в этом.
variations.note: в + prepositional в этом names what for: "don't blame yourself for this".

options.note: A zero-copula nominal: "it isn't your fault".

options.ru: Ты ни в чём не виноват.
options.note: ни в чём не with the short form виноват: "you're not to blame for anything" — the obligatory double negative.

paraphrases.simplest: Не вини себя.

takeaway.pattern: себя points back to the subject; the verb sets its case
takeaway.note: No nominative: genitive/accusative себя, dative себе, instrumental собой, prepositional себе. Он винит себя (accusative) / Он купил себе книгу (dative) / Он недоволен собой (instrumental).

keyPoint: Завести is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting (a pet)" (pairs with заводить).

replies.gloss: Are you ready for that responsibility?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive завести + animate accusative собаку
grammarFocus.note: завести собаку is the set phrase for getting a dog (завести = to take on an animal or a habit). собака is an animate feminine noun, but feminine singulars take -у regardless of animacy: собаку.

variations.note: The base form: "I want to get a dog".
кот is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive: кота — the contrast with feminine nouns.
The animate accusative plural is genitive-shaped: собак.

options.ru: Я хочу взять собаку из приюта.
options.note: из + genitive приюта (from a shelter); взять here is "to take in".
Dative + хочется + accusative: "I feel like getting a dog", impersonally hedged.

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу завести собаку.

takeaway.pattern: even animate feminine singulars take -у / -ю in the accusative
takeaway.note: собаку, сестру, женщину — the animate/inanimate distinction simply doesn't surface there. Genitive-shaped accusatives occur only in the masculine singular and in the plural of all genders.

keyPoint: Передумать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "changing one's mind" (pairs with передумывать).

replies.gloss: Okay, we'll take that into account.

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb ещё + time adverb вчера + perfective past передумал
grammarFocus.note: передумать (to change one's mind) is perfective, with пере- supplying "redo". ещё вчера means "already yesterday" — ещё adds the sense of "as early as then".

variations.note: The base form: "I'd already changed my mind yesterday".
передумала for a female speaker, with ещё dropped.
уже давно (long since) widens the time frame.

options.note: изменить решение (to change a decision) takes the accusative and is more formal.
больше не (no longer) with the genitive этого — negated хотеть tends to take the genitive.

paraphrases.simplest: Я передумал вчера.

takeaway.pattern: ещё вчера / ещё тогда = "already back then"
takeaway.note: Beyond "still", ещё combines with time words to stress how early something happened: Я ещё вчера всё понял, I had it all worked out as early as yesterday.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Магия is a feminine noun meaning "magic."

grammarFocus.construction: верить в + accusative магию
grammarFocus.note: верить в + accusative means believing in the existence of something. магия is feminine with the accusative магию. Since в takes the accusative here, feminine singulars end in -ю.

variations.note: The base form, with the feminine singular accusative магию.
The accusative судьбу — the same frame with a different object.
The neuter plural чудеса matches the nominative; gender and number change the shape.

options.note: Spelling it out with существовать; the что clause takes a comma.
сверхъестественное is an adjective used as a noun (the supernatural), with an identical accusative.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы верите в магию?

takeaway.pattern: feminine nouns in -ия take -ию in the accusative
takeaway.note: магия → магию, история → историю, фамилия → фамилию. In the genitive, dative and prepositional they end in -ии (в магии), so the accusative in -ию is the odd one out.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Арест is a masculine noun meaning "arrest."

grammarFocus.construction: видели + accusative арест + в + prepositional фильме
grammarFocus.note: арест (arrest) is masculine inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative. в фильме is the locative prepositional. The perfective видели asks about a single fact of seeing.

variations.note: The base form: "did you see the arrest in the film?"
сцена ареста uses a genitive modifier: "the arrest scene".
A как clause with an impersonal plural: "did you see him being arrested?"

options.note: кого-то (animate indefinite accusative) with an impersonal plural: "was someone arrested in the film?"
с + instrumental арестом, "a scene with an arrest"; была + nominative is existential.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели арест в фильме?

takeaway.pattern: noun + genitive (сцена ареста) vs. a как clause
takeaway.note: Action nouns (арест, нападение, побег) compress neatly into "noun + genitive", while a как clause lets you say who did what to whom. Choose by register and detail.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Молиться is imperfective, meaning "to pray" (pairs with помолиться).

replies.gloss: What exactly do you pray for?

grammarFocus.construction: молиться + за + accusative нашу семью
grammarFocus.note: молиться (to pray) is reflexive, and the person prayed for takes за + accusative, not the dative. семья is feminine with the accusative семью, and нашу is the matching possessive. Praying to someone takes the dative: молиться Богу.

variations.note: The base form, за + accusative for "on behalf of our family".
за + accusative тебя, praying for a person directly.
The dative Богу is "to pray to God" — a different relation entirely.

options.note: просить за + accusative is "to plead on behalf of" — usable outside religious contexts.
думать о + prepositional: "I'm thinking of our family" — a gentler recast.

paraphrases.simplest: Я молюсь за нашу семью.

takeaway.pattern: молиться за кого (accusative) vs. молиться кому (dative)
takeaway.note: за + accusative is "for whose sake", the dative "to whom". болеть за кого (to support a team) and бороться за что (to fight for something) belong to the same за family.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Фунт is a masculine noun meaning "pound" (weight or currency).

grammarFocus.construction: платить + accusative (sum) + за + accusative (goods)
grammarFocus.note: платить (to pay) puts the sum in the accusative and what you are paying for in за + accusative. фунт (pound) is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and кофе is indeclinable, so за кофе never changes.

variations.note: The base form, with both slots filled.

variations.ru: Вы платите два фунта за кофе?
variations.note: After 2-4 the noun goes genitive singular: фунта.
From five up it is the genitive plural фунтов; the perfective заплатили asks about the result.

options.note: стоить + accusative states the price, with кофе as subject.

options.ru: Вы отдаёте фунт за чашку кофе?
options.note: отдавать (to hand over) with за + accusative чашку кофе: "a pound for one cup?"

paraphrases.simplest: Кофе стоит фунт?

takeaway.pattern: платить сколько за что (accusative + за + accusative)
takeaway.note: платить деньги за товар. за + accusative means "in exchange for". A third slot, whom you pay, goes in the dative (платить продавцу).

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Справляться is imperfective, meaning "to handle/manage" (pairs with справиться).

grammarFocus.construction: справляться с + instrumental работой + manner adverb хорошо
grammarFocus.note: справляться (to cope, to manage) is a reflexive verb governing с + instrumental; the instrumental of работа is работой. Its perfective is справиться. хорошо says how well it is going.

variations.note: The base form: "you're handling the job well".
The perfective справился + с + instrumental задачей: "you got the task done".
It works without an object too: "you're managing beautifully".

options.note: получаться + у + genitive means "it's going well for you", with an implicit subject.
работать + adverb praises it bluntly: "you work excellently".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты хорошо справляешься с работой.

takeaway.note: справляться с работой / с трудностями / с ребёнком. с + instrumental frames "to deal with", the same pattern as бороться с, спорить с and встречаться с.

skeleton.note: 1st person plural present, the target word

keyPoint: Торопиться is imperfective, meaning "to hurry" (pairs with поторопиться).

replies.gloss: I can give you a ride.

grammarFocus.construction: торопиться + на + accusative работу + the intensifier очень
grammarFocus.note: торопиться (to hurry) is reflexive, and the destination takes на + accusative for direction; the accusative of работа is работу. For location it would be на работе (prepositional), "at work". очень adds degree.

variations.note: The base form, with directional на + accusative.
домой is a directional adverb, so no preposition is needed.
на работе is the locative prepositional — the contrast with direction.

options.note: спешить also means "to hurry" and is interchangeable here.
опаздывать на + accusative is "to be late for" — explaining why the rush.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы торопимся на работу.

takeaway.pattern: на работу (direction, accusative) vs. на работе (location, prepositional)
takeaway.note: идти на работу / быть на работе. The same на switches role by case, exactly as в does (в школу / в школе), according to whether the verb moves or stays.

keyPoint: Влюбиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "falling in love" (pairs with влюбляться).

replies.gloss: Do you think it happens easily?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive влюбиться
grammarFocus.note: влюбиться (to fall in love) is a reflexive perfective, and the person takes в + accusative (влюбиться в неё). With no object, Хотите влюбиться? asks in general terms. The imperfective is влюбляться.

variations.note: The base form: "do you want to fall in love?"
в + animate accusative кого-нибудь, "in someone" — the indefinite pronoun is genitive-shaped.
The perfective past: "have you fallen in love?" — влюбился for a man, влюбилась for a woman.

options.note: полюбить takes the accusative and means "to come to love" — more deliberate and gentler.
Dative + хочется + genitive любви: "do you long for love?", impersonally hedged.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы хотите влюбиться?

takeaway.pattern: влюбиться в + accusative vs. любить + accusative
takeaway.note: влюбиться в неё (fall for her — the preposition is obligatory) / любить её (love her — bare accusative). The "falling" verb needs directional в; the "loving" verb takes a direct object.

keyPoint: Задержать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "detaining" someone (pairs with задерживать).

grammarFocus.construction: видели + a как clause + the impersonal plural задержали + animate accusative его
grammarFocus.note: видеть, как... is the set way to say "to see someone doing something", and the comma before как is obligatory. задержали is a subjectless third person plural — an impersonal construction, "they detained him". его is the animate accusative, identical to the genitive.

variations.note: The base form; the impersonal plural names no agent.

variations.ru: Вы видели, как полиция его задержала?
variations.note: With полиция as subject the agent is explicit and the verb agrees as feminine singular, задержала.
The action noun задержание compresses the clause into one word; neuter, so the accusative matches.

options.note: быть свидетелем + genitive, "to be a witness to", with свидетелем in the instrumental as predicate.
при + prepositional вас means "in your presence" — a different way to frame it.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели, как его задержали?

takeaway.note: Я видел, как он ушёл (I saw him leave) / Я слышал, как она пела (I heard her singing). Where English uses a bare infinitive after a verb of perception, Russian uses a как clause.

keyPoint: Удивительно is a parenthetical adverb meaning "surprisingly."

grammarFocus.construction: the predicate adverb Удивительно + но + всё помню
grammarFocus.note: Удивительно, но... is the set "surprisingly, ..." — an impersonal predicate adverb plus the adversative но. помнить (to remember) is an imperfective-only state verb taking the accusative, and всё is the neuter pronoun in the accusative.

variations.note: The base form, joined by comma + но.
Странно (oddly) fits the same frame.

variations.ru: Я, как ни странно, всё помню.
variations.note: как ни странно (strange to say) is a parenthetical, fenced by commas on both sides.

options.note: на удивление (surprisingly) is a на + accusative adverbial parenthetical.
The double negative: "I haven't forgotten anything" — ничего requires не.

paraphrases.simplest: Я всё помню.

takeaway.pattern: помнить (to remember, a state) vs. вспомнить (to recall, an event)
takeaway.note: помнить is imperfective-only and means holding something in memory; вспомнить is the perfective moment of recall. Learn Я помню alongside Я вспомнил.

keyPoint: Поблагодарить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "thanking" (pairs with благодарить).

replies.gloss: I'll pass that on to him.

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive поблагодарить + animate accusative вашего врача
grammarFocus.note: поблагодарить (to thank) is perfective and takes the accusative, with the reason in за + accusative. врач is animate masculine, so the accusative copies the genitive — врача — and the possessive follows as вашего.

variations.note: The base form, with animate accusative agreement.

variations.ru: Я хочу поблагодарить вас за помощь.
variations.note: за + accusative помощь adds what you are thanking them for.
A feminine noun gives вашу медсестру; animate feminine singular accusative ends in -у / -ю.

options.note: передать + dative врачу: "pass on my thanks to your doctor"; спасибо is indeclinable.
благодарен + dative; as a short form it agrees in gender and number.

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу поблагодарить вашего врача.

takeaway.pattern: благодарить кого (accusative) vs. быть благодарным кому (dative)
takeaway.note: The verb благодарить takes the accusative, the adjective благодарен the dative. Same gratitude, different case depending on the part of speech.

keyPoint: Стыдно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's shameful."

grammarFocus.construction: the impersonal стыдно + infinitive лгать, inside a что clause
grammarFocus.note: стыдно (shameful) is a subjectless predicate adverb that pairs with an infinitive: "it is shameful to lie". лгать (to lie) is imperfective and takes a dative for the person lied to (лгать мне). A comma separates it from Вы понимаете.

variations.note: The base form: impersonal стыдно plus an infinitive.
Adding the dative Вам turns it on the hearer: "aren't you ashamed to lie?"
нельзя + imperfective infinitive recasts it as a prohibition: "that lying is not allowed".

options.note: врать is the colloquial form of лгать and плохо a predicate adverb — more everyday.
Как вам не стыдно? is the set reproach: "how are you not ashamed?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы понимаете, что врать плохо?

takeaway.pattern: predicate adverb + infinitive (стыдно лгать, трудно понять)
takeaway.note: The basic way to pass judgement without a subject. Add the person in the dative (Мне стыдно). Both лгать and врать govern the dative, with врать the colloquial one.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Чек is a masculine noun meaning "receipt/check."

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Дайте + dative мне + accusative чек
grammarFocus.note: дайте is the polite/plural imperative of дать. As a verb of giving it takes two slots: the dative (мне) and the accusative (чек). чек is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. пожалуйста is set off by a comma.

variations.note: The base form — standard at a shop or counter.
дай (singular) for someone you are close to.
можно + dative + accusative drops the verb — more tentative.

options.note: выписать чек is "to make out a receipt" — a businesslike request.
Dative + нужен + nominative; нужен agrees with чек (masculine).

paraphrases.simplest: Дайте мне чек, пожалуйста.

takeaway.pattern: пожалуйста is a parenthetical and takes commas
takeaway.note: Дайте мне чек, пожалуйста / Скажите, пожалуйста, где выход. At the end it takes one comma before it; mid-sentence it is fenced on both sides.

keyPoint: По-настоящему is an adverb meaning "truly, really."

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb по-настоящему + любить + accusative эту работу
grammarFocus.note: по-настоящему (truly, genuinely) is a hyphenated adverb intensifying the verb. работа is feminine with the accusative работу, and the demonstrative matches as эту. любить + accusative means to love or like something.

variations.note: The base form; по-настоящему stresses how genuine it is.
очень is the neutral intensifier; по-настоящему implies "not superficially".
Dative + нравится + nominative, so the job becomes the subject.

options.note: для + genitive with всё: "this job is everything to me".
гордиться + instrumental своей работой: "I'm proud of my work".

paraphrases.simplest: Я очень люблю эту работу.

takeaway.pattern: adverbs in по- + adjective + -ому (по-настоящему, по-новому, по-разному)
takeaway.note: Written with a hyphen and never declined. They mean "in such a manner", so по-настоящему is literally "in a genuine way" — hence "truly".

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Разбираться is imperfective, meaning "to be knowledgeable about" (pairs with разобраться).

replies.gloss: Thanks, I've been doing it a long time.

grammarFocus.construction: разбираться в + prepositional музыке + manner adverb хорошо
grammarFocus.note: разбираться (to know a subject well) is a reflexive verb governing в + prepositional; the prepositional of музыка is музыке. Its perfective разобраться means "to get to the bottom of"; for an ongoing state the imperfective is used.

variations.note: The base form: "you really know your music".
плохо (badly) with в технике — negative assessments use the same frame.
The perfective разобрался: "I've worked this question out" — a single achievement.

options.note: знаток (connoisseur) + genitive музыки, as a zero-copula predicate noun.
знать о + prepositional: "you know a lot about music".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты хорошо разбираешься в музыке.

takeaway.note: разбираться в музыке / в людях / в компьютерах — the sense is "seeing into" something, hence в + prepositional. участвовать в and нуждаться в share the frame.

keyPoint: М-р is an abbreviation of мистер (Mr.).

grammarFocus.construction: the abbreviation м-р + a predicate noun + the tag верно?
grammarFocus.note: м-р is the written abbreviation of мистер, used for foreign men. With no present copula, Вы м-р Джон means "you are Mr John". The final верно? is the set confirmation tag, separated by a comma.

variations.note: The abbreviation spelled out — мистер in full prose.

variations.ru: Вы мистер Джон, не так ли?
variations.note: не так ли? is a more formal tag: "is that not so?"
The particle ведь gives the same "you are, aren't you?" effect.

options.note: Opening with Простите makes the approach polite.

options.ru: Если не ошибаюсь, вы мистер Джон.
options.note: Если не ошибаюсь (if I'm not mistaken) is a parenthetical, set off by a comma.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы мистер Джон?

takeaway.pattern: confirmation tags (верно? / не так ли? / да?)
takeaway.note: The equivalents of English "isn't it?". верно? and да? are colloquial, не так ли? belongs to formal writing, and all of them take a preceding comma.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Банда is a feminine noun meaning "gang."

grammarFocus.construction: видели + accusative банду + в + prepositional этом фильме
grammarFocus.note: банда (gang) is feminine with the accusative банду. в этом фильме is в + prepositional for location, with the demonstrative agreeing as этом. The perfective видели asks about a single fact.

variations.ru: Вы видели банду в этом фильме?
variations.note: The base form, with a feminine accusative and a locative prepositional.

variations.ru: Вы видели бандитов в этом фильме?
variations.note: бандит is animate masculine, so the accusative plural is genitive-shaped: бандитов.
Recast with была + nominative as an existential.

options.note: The impersonal plural показали: "was a gang shown in the film?"
про + accusative asks about the subject matter: "is it a film about a gang?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели банду в этом фильме?

takeaway.note: этот фильм (nominative), этот фильм (inanimate accusative), в этом фильме (prepositional), этого фильма (genitive). The demonstrative often shows the case more clearly than the noun.

keyPoint: По-другому is an adverb meaning "differently."

grammarFocus.construction: Давай + perfective first person plural сделаем + the adverb по-другому
grammarFocus.note: Давай + a perfective first person plural makes a proposal, "let's". сделаем is from сделать. по-другому (differently) is a hyphenated adverb that never declines, and всё is accusative.

variations.note: The base form — a proposal to someone close.
давайте is the polite/plural form.
The parenthetical Может softens it into a tentative suggestion.

options.note: другой способ (another way) is accusative; попробуем is a perfective first person plural.
изменить подход (to change the approach) takes the accusative.

paraphrases.simplest: Давай сделаем по-другому.

takeaway.pattern: Давай(те) + perfective first person plural = let's
takeaway.note: Давай пойдём / Давайте начнём. With an imperfective you instead use давай + infinitive (Давай говорить по-русски). давай for ты, давайте for вы.

keyPoint: Выбросить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "throwing away" (pairs with выбрасывать).

replies.gloss: Okay, I'll take care of it.
Maybe we should give it to someone?

grammarFocus.construction: надо + perfective infinitive выбросить + accusative эту старую вещь
grammarFocus.note: надо is an impersonal predicate, "it is necessary to". выбросить (to throw out) is perfective and takes the accusative. вещь is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative, so эту and старую are what show the case.

variations.note: The base form, where only the modifiers reveal the case.
Dative нам plus the plural эти вещи — inanimate, so nominative-shaped.
можно + infinitive recasts it as permission: "this can be thrown out".

options.note: избавиться от + genitive is "to get rid of"; пора + infinitive means "it's time to".
не нужна is a short form agreeing with вещь (feminine): "it isn't needed any more".

paraphrases.simplest: Надо выбросить эту вещь.

takeaway.pattern: with feminine -ь nouns, the modifiers carry the case
takeaway.note: вещь, дверь, ночь, любовь look identical in nominative and accusative. Only the ending on a demonstrative or adjective — эту вещь vs. эта вещь — tells you which it is.

keyPoint: Симпатичный is an adjective meaning "likeable, attractive."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the adjective симпатичный + predicate noun человек
grammarFocus.note: No copula in the present. симпатичный (likeable, nice) is the long form agreeing with человек (masculine singular nominative), and очень adds degree. Note that it does not mean English "sympathetic".

variations.note: The base form — a compliment to a man.
A feminine noun takes симпатичная.
With the past были the phrase turns instrumental: симпатичным человеком.

options.note: приятный (pleasant, agreeable) fits the same frame.
с + instrumental plus the predicate adverb приятно + infinitive: "you're pleasant to talk to".

paraphrases.simplest: Вы очень приятный человек.

takeaway.note: English "sympathetic" is сочувствующий. симпатичный is about looks or manner being appealing — a classic false friend.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Кусочек is a diminutive of кусок (piece).

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Дай + dative мне + accusative кусочек + partitive genitive хлеба
grammarFocus.note: кусочек хлеба is "a piece of bread", with the whole in the genitive (the partitive genitive). кусочек is the diminutive of кусок. дать takes its usual dative + accusative slots.

variations.note: The plain кусок; кусочек adds smallness and warmth.
The polite/plural imperative дайте.
The partitive genitive хлеба alone means "some bread" — the quantity word can be dropped.

options.note: можно + dative + accusative, asking permission with no verb.
отрезать + partitive genitive: "cut me some bread".

paraphrases.simplest: Дай мне кусочек хлеба.

takeaway.pattern: quantity noun + genitive (кусок хлеба, чашка чая, бутылка воды)
takeaway.note: The substance goes in the genitive after a measure. Drop the measure and the genitive alone still signals "some" (Дай воды, give me some water).

keyPoint: Безумный is an adjective meaning "crazy, insane."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past придумали + accusative безумный план
