grammarFocus.note: придумать (to think up) is perfective and takes the accusative. план is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and безумный (insane) stays unchanged. The prefix при- adds the sense of arriving at an idea.

variations.note: The base form: "you've come up with an insane plan".
идея is feminine, so the accusative is безумную идею.
кто asks who devised it; the verb defaults to the masculine singular придумал.

options.note: A zero-copula nominal stating only the verdict.
предложить (to propose) with рискованный (risky) — more neutral.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы придумали безумный план.

takeaway.note: при- turns thinking into arriving at a result. The cases differ too: думать о чём takes the prepositional, придумать что the accusative.

skeleton.note: future 1st person plural, the target word

keyPoint: Поиграть is a perfective delimitative of играть, meaning "to play for a while."

grammarFocus.construction: Давай + perfective first person plural поиграем + после + genitive работы
grammarFocus.note: поиграть is играть with по-, "to play for a while". Давай + first person plural makes the proposal. после + genitive работы is "after work". What you play takes в + accusative (поиграть в футбол).

variations.note: The base form: "let's play a bit after work".
в + accusative шахматы names the game — games and sports take в.
Instruments take на + prepositional (играть на гитаре) — a different preposition.

options.note: The parenthetical Может makes it a tentative suggestion.
есть время + infinitive asks whether there is time to play.

paraphrases.simplest: Давай поиграем после работы.

takeaway.pattern: играть в + accusative (games) vs. играть на + prepositional (instruments)
takeaway.note: играть в футбол / в карты / в шахматы, but играть на гитаре / на пианино. One verb, two frames — a textbook split.

keyPoint: Прочь is an adverb meaning "away."

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Уходи + adverb прочь + из + genitive моего дома
grammarFocus.note: уходи is the imperfective imperative of уходить (to leave), ordering a departure under way — "get out". прочь (away) is a directional adverb reinforcing it. из + genitive means "out of", with the possessive agreeing as моего.

variations.note: Without прочь — still forceful enough.
The polite/plural form уходите.
The perfective imperative уйди demands one completed departure; отсюда (from here) is an adverb.

options.note: покинуть + accusative is the formal "to vacate" — the wording of an official demand.
просить + accusative + infinitive: "I'm asking you to leave" — politely put.

paraphrases.simplest: Уходи из моего дома.

takeaway.note: The imperfective urges you to get on with it or keep at it; the perfective demands one completed act. Both can throw someone out, but уходи sounds more urgent.

keyPoint: Дерзить is imperfective, meaning "to talk back/be impertinent" (pairs with надерзить).

grammarFocus.construction: не надо + imperfective infinitive дерзить + dative своей маме
grammarFocus.note: дерзить (to be cheeky) governs the dative as an imperfective. The dative of мама is маме, and the reflexive possessive своей is feminine dative. свой refers back to the subject — so the addressee's own mother.

variations.note: The base form, with маме as the dative target.
A direct negative imperative; the dative of мать is матери.

variations.ru: Не надо так говорить с мамой.
variations.note: Recast with говорить с + instrumental: "don't talk to your mother like that".

options.note: The imperative будь + comparative вежливее + с + instrumental: "be more polite with your mother".
грубить also governs the dative and means being rude — practically synonymous.

paraphrases.simplest: Не груби маме.

takeaway.pattern: дерзить / грубить / хамить all govern the dative
takeaway.note: Verbs of being rude take the dative: дерзить учителю, грубить продавцу, хамить клиенту. Never the accusative — ×дерзить маму is wrong.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, prepositional, the target word

keyPoint: Травма is a feminine noun meaning "trauma, injury."

replies.gloss: Yes, that's a very personal topic.
How long ago did that happen?

grammarFocus.construction: говорить о + prepositional травме
grammarFocus.note: говорить о + prepositional is "to talk about". травма is feminine with the prepositional травме. The present говорите checks what is being discussed right now. о becomes об before a vowel.

variations.note: The base form, with the prepositional травме.
Before a vowel о becomes об: об операции.
про + accusative травму is the colloquial version, with spoken word order.

options.note: иметь в виду + accusative is the set "do you mean".
речь идёт о + prepositional is a formal "is this about...?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы говорите о травме?

takeaway.pattern: choosing between о, об and обо
takeaway.note: о before consonants (о работе), об before vowels (об этом, об операции), обо before words like всём (обо всём, обо мне). It is purely about ease of pronunciation.

keyPoint: По-твоему is an adverb meaning "in your opinion."

grammarFocus.construction: the parenthetical По-твоему inside a quotation + the predicate adverb удобно
grammarFocus.note: По-твоему (in your opinion) is a hyphenated adverb working as a parenthetical, set off by a comma. удобно is a predicate adverb, "convenient, comfortable". The quotation is introduced by a colon and «».

variations.note: The core without the quotation: parenthetical plus impersonal clause.
The polite form по-вашему.
Dative Тебе + удобно names who finds it comfortable.

options.note: считать + accusative + instrumental удобным — the construction changes the case.
Как ты думаешь is a parenthetical opener, set off by a comma.

paraphrases.simplest: По-твоему, это удобно?

takeaway.note: They mean "in my / your opinion" and must be separated by commas. They never decline and can sit at the start or inside the sentence.

keyPoint: Неплохой is an adjective meaning "not bad, pretty good."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past выбрали + accusative неплохой фильм
grammarFocus.note: неплохой (not bad) is не + плохой fused into one word — a measured compliment. фильм is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. выбрать takes the accusative as a perfective.

variations.note: The base form: "you've picked a decent film".
A feminine noun takes неплохую книгу.
хороший is open praise; неплохой is understated.

options.note: оказаться + instrumental неплохим: "the film turned out not bad".
A nominal sentence with выбор as subject: "good choice".

paraphrases.simplest: Вы выбрали хороший фильм.

takeaway.pattern: не fused onto an adjective (неплохой, нехороший, немаленький)
takeaway.note: Written solid it softens the verdict; written apart, не плохой implies a contrast ("not bad, but..."). In practice неплохой usually means "quite good".

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Издеваться is imperfective, meaning 'to bully or mock' (paired with поиздеваться).

replies.gloss: Why do people act like that?

grammarFocus.construction: Нельзя + imperfective infinitive издеваться + над + instrumental людьми
grammarFocus.note: издеваться (to mock, to bully) is a reflexive verb governing над + instrumental. The instrumental of люди is the irregular людьми. нельзя + imperfective expresses prohibition.

variations.note: The base form: "you mustn't bully people".
A negative imperative with над + instrumental ним: "don't mock him".
смеяться над + instrumental uses the same frame: "you mustn't laugh at others".

options.note: уважать + accusative states the positive: "people deserve respect".
The predicate adverb жестоко judges the behaviour: "that's cruel".

paraphrases.simplest: Нельзя издеваться над людьми.

takeaway.pattern: verbs taking над + instrumental (издеваться, смеяться, работать, думать)
takeaway.note: над literally means "above", so издеваться над кем is mocking someone from above, смеяться над чем is laughing at something, работать над чем is working on it — all a sense of hovering over the object.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Пообещать is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'promising' (paired with обещать).

replies.gloss: When will you be able to help?

grammarFocus.construction: могу + perfective infinitive пообещать + dative тебе + accusative помощь
grammarFocus.note: пообещать (to promise) takes two slots as a perfective: the dative for the person and the accusative for what is promised. помощь is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative. могу + infinitive frames the offer.

variations.note: The base form, with both dative and accusative.
The imperfective present обещаю performs the promise as you speak.
A что clause spells out the content; помогу is a perfective future.

options.note: A perfective future with обещаю tacked on — the natural spoken version.
рассчитывать на + accusative is "to count on": "you can count on me".

paraphrases.simplest: Я обещаю тебе помощь.

takeaway.note: The two-slot verbs of giving — дать, сказать, обещать, передать — all pair a dative person with an accusative thing. Complex content can open into a что clause (обещать, что приду).

skeleton.note: masculine noun, plural accusative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Демон is a masculine noun meaning 'demon.'

grammarFocus.construction: про + animate accusative plural демонов
grammarFocus.note: про + accusative is the colloquial "about". демон is animate masculine, so the accusative plural copies the genitive: демонов. фильмы is the accusative plural object of любить, identical to the nominative.

variations.note: The base form, with the animate accusative plural демонов.
о + prepositional plural демонах is the bookish version.
магия is inanimate feminine, so the accusative is магию — the contrast is visible.

options.note: ужасы (horror) is an inanimate accusative plural — the whole thing in one genre word.
Dative + нравится + nominative мистика: "do you like the occult?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы любите фильмы про демонов?

takeaway.pattern: the animacy rule still applies after про + accusative
takeaway.note: про демонов (animate, genitive-shaped) vs. про магию (inanimate, ordinary accusative). The preposition sets the case; animacy sets the form.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Пожениться is perfective, marking the single completed act of 'getting married' (as a couple) (paired with жениться).

grammarFocus.construction: решить + perfective infinitive пожениться + the instrumental time phrase этим летом
grammarFocus.note: пожениться (to get married) is a reciprocal verb used only with plural subjects — the two people marry each other. этим летом is an instrumental time expression, "this summer", with no preposition.

variations.note: The base form; a plural subject is obligatory.
A male singular subject takes жениться на + prepositional: "to marry her".
A woman uses выйти замуж за + accusative — three different patterns by gender.

options.note: сыграть свадьбу (to hold a wedding) takes the accusative — a colloquial set phrase.
The у + genitive + nominative possessive: "we're having a wedding in the summer".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы решили пожениться летом.

takeaway.pattern: пожениться (plural) / жениться на + prepositional (man) / выйти замуж за + accusative (woman)
takeaway.note: "To marry" splits three ways by the subject's gender and number: двое поженились / он женился на ней / она вышла замуж за него. The frames have to be learnt whole.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ужинать is imperfective, meaning 'to have dinner' (paired with поужинать).

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective future Будем ужинать + adverbs вместе and сегодня
grammarFocus.note: With the subject dropped, Будем ужинать is a first person plural future, "let's have dinner together". ужинать is imperfective, so буду + infinitive is its only future. вместе and сегодня are both adverbs.

variations.note: The base form, with мы understood.
With the subject stated; the meaning is unchanged.
The perfective поужинаем with давай makes it an explicit invitation.

options.note: The present used for a settled plan: "tonight we're eating together".
на + accusative ужин: "come over for dinner" — the standard invitation.

paraphrases.simplest: Давай поужинаем вместе.

takeaway.pattern: the present can express a scheduled future
takeaway.note: Сегодня ужинаем вместе / Завтра едем в Москву. Fixed plans can take the present, just as English says "I'm flying tomorrow".

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Руль is a masculine noun meaning 'steering wheel.'

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Держи + accusative руль + instrumental обеими руками
grammarFocus.note: держать (to hold) takes the accusative, and the means goes in the instrumental. The feminine обе (both) has the instrumental обеими, and рука the instrumental plural руками. Masculine and neuter would use оба → обоими.

variations.note: The base form; the instrumental numeral обеими is the point.
The polite/plural imperative держите.
With the accusative pronoun его; the instrumental phrase is unchanged.

options.note: The negated imperative of отпускать: "don't let go of the wheel".
A nominal sentence: "hands on the wheel", with на + prepositional руле for location.

paraphrases.simplest: Держи руль двумя руками.

takeaway.note: оба брата / обе руки, and both decline: обоих / обеих, обоим / обеим, обоими / обеими. Like два / две, this numeral is sensitive to gender.

skeleton.note: adverb, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Наедине is an adverb meaning 'alone together, privately.'

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive поговорить + adverb наедине
grammarFocus.note: поговорить is говорить with по-, "to have a talk". наедине (in private, just the two of us) is an adverb and never declines. The other person takes с + instrumental (поговорить с тобой).

variations.note: The base form: "I'd like to talk in private".

variations.ru: Я хочу поговорить с тобой наедине.
variations.note: с + instrumental тобой names the person.
можно + infinitive asks permission — more tentative.

options.note: без + genitive plural свидетелей (without witnesses) spells out наедине.
выйти with на + accusative минуту: "shall we step out for a minute?" — moving the conversation.

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу поговорить наедине.

takeaway.pattern: поговорить (have a talk) vs. говорить (talk, be talking)
takeaway.note: по- supplies "one bounded portion", so поговорить is having a conversation once. Unlike обсудить (to thrash out), it suggests something light.

skeleton.note: interjection, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ммм is an interjection expressing enjoyment or satisfaction.

grammarFocus.construction: the interjection Ммм inside a quotation + the predicate adverb вкусно
grammarFocus.note: вкусно is the short neuter form used as a predicate adverb, an impersonal "it's tasty" with no subject. The adjective вкусный modifies nouns instead (вкусный суп). Ммм is the interjection for savouring something.

variations.note: The core without the quotation: interjection plus impersonal clause.
With это as subject; the predicate stays adverbial.
An exclamation with the adjective вкусный modifying the noun.

options.note: Dative + нравится: "I really like it" — usable beyond food.
Как + predicate adverb makes an exclamation: "how delicious!"

paraphrases.simplest: Очень вкусно!

takeaway.note: Очень вкусно judges the situation; Вкусный суп describes the thing. The -о form takes no subject, the -ый form agrees with its noun.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Отвалить is a slang perfective verb meaning 'to leave, get out.'

replies.gloss: Why are you in such a hurry?

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal Пора + perfective infinitive отвалить + adverb отсюда
grammarFocus.note: пора + infinitive is the impersonal "it's time to". отвалить properly means a boat casting off, but colloquially it is a rough "to clear off". отсюда (from here) is an adverb.

variations.note: With уходить it is neutral — the only version for work or strangers.
The perfective уйти frames it as one completed departure.
Dative Нам + пора alone: "we should be going" — the most compact form.

options.note: пора + imperfective infinitive — a gentle way to wrap things up.
выбираться (to extricate oneself) with давай: "let's get out of here".

paraphrases.simplest: Нам пора идти.

takeaway.pattern: отвалить is coarse slang — recognition only
takeaway.note: Отвали! ("get lost") is distinctly aggressive. What is worth keeping is the impersonal пора + infinitive; say уходить or идти when you use it yourself.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Пожар is a masculine noun meaning 'fire.'

grammarFocus.construction: видели + accusative пожар + в + prepositional plural новостях
grammarFocus.note: пожар (fire) is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. в новостях is the set в + prepositional plural, "on the news"; новости is normally used in the plural.

variations.note: The base form, with в новостях as the source.
по + dative телевизору is "on TV" — a different preposition for a different medium.
читать о + prepositional пожаре: "did you read about the fire?"

options.note: The impersonal plural показали: "did they show the fire on the news?"
про + accusative пожар, colloquial: "did you hear about the fire?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видели пожар в новостях?

takeaway.pattern: в новостях / по телевизору / в интернете
takeaway.note: Each medium has its own fixed phrasing: news content takes в новостях, broadcast channels по телевизору / по радио, and the web в интернете (на сайте). Learn preposition and case together.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Перерыв is a masculine noun meaning 'a break, recess.'

grammarFocus.construction: Давай + perfective first person plural сделаем + accusative небольшой перерыв
grammarFocus.note: Давай + a perfective first person plural proposes something. сделать перерыв (to take a break) is a set phrase with the accusative. небольшой (smallish) is не + большой written solid, agreeing with перерыв (masculine inanimate).

variations.note: The base form: "let's take a short break".
давайте is the polite/plural form — what you would say in a meeting.
The parenthetical Может makes it a tentative suggestion.

options.note: отдохнуть (to rest) with немного — a verb-centred recast.
Dative + нужен + nominative; нужен agrees with перерыв (masculine).

paraphrases.simplest: Давай сделаем перерыв.

takeaway.pattern: сделать + noun as a light-verb phrase
takeaway.note: сделать перерыв (take a break), сделать выбор (make a choice), сделать вывод (draw a conclusion). The verb and noun form one meaning, and the noun is always accusative.

skeleton.note: 1st person plural present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Направляться is imperfective, meaning 'to head toward' (paired with направиться).

replies.gloss: How long will the trip take?

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present направляемся + directional adverb домой + после + genitive
grammarFocus.note: направляться (to head for) is reflexive, with the destination in в / на + accusative or a directional adverb. домой needs no preposition. после работы is после + genitive. The present can also state a plan.

variations.note: The base form — somewhat formal, even official in tone.
идти is the everyday choice: "we're going home after work".
в + accusative центр names the destination as a noun.

options.note: ехать is travel by vehicle; on foot it would be идти.
Verbless and colloquial; с + genitive работы means "from work".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы идём домой после работы.

takeaway.pattern: направляться is formal; идти / ехать are everyday
takeaway.note: направляться куда belongs to reports and announcements. In conversation pick идти (on foot) or ехать (by vehicle).

skeleton.note: neuter noun, plural accusative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Извинение is a neuter noun meaning 'apology.'

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Прими + accusative plural мои извинения
grammarFocus.note: The imperative of принять (to accept) is прими (singular) / примите (polite). извинения (apologies) is neuter plural with an accusative identical to the nominative, and мои agrees in the plural. The whole thing is a set apology.

variations.note: The polite примите — the form for a formal apology.
Without пожалуйста, for someone close.
просить прощения takes the genitive — "I beg your pardon".

options.note: The imperative извини + accusative меня — the everyday apology.
Dative + жаль, impersonal: "I'm very sorry".

paraphrases.simplest: Извини меня, пожалуйста.

takeaway.note: Извини (casual) < Простите (polite) < Примите мои извинения / Прошу прощения (formal, weighty). Match the register to the gravity of the offence.

skeleton.note: 2nd person plural present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Поживать is imperfective, meaning 'to be getting on, living,' frequent in the set phrase как поживаешь ('how are you doing?').

replies.gloss: And how are things with you?

grammarFocus.construction: the question word Как + imperfective present поживаете
grammarFocus.note: поживать is an archaic verb for "to live, to get on", surviving mainly in Как вы поживаете? — the polite "how are you?". In practice it is used almost exclusively in this question. сегодня is a time adverb.

variations.note: The base form without сегодня — a polite greeting.
With ты, поживаешь; usable with friends, though it sounds a little old-fashioned.
The everyday "how's things?"; дела is nominative plural.

options.note: Adding the possessive ваши makes it politer; дела stays plural.
чувствовать себя + adverb asks about health — for when someone is unwell.

paraphrases.simplest: Как дела?

takeaway.pattern: Как дела? / Как поживаете? / Как вы себя чувствуете?
takeaway.note: The first is everyday, the second polite and slightly dated, the third strictly about health. Don't swap the last one in as a greeting.

skeleton.note: impersonal predicate, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Холодно is an impersonal predicate meaning 'it is cold.'

replies.gloss: Yes, you need to dress warmer.

grammarFocus.construction: the impersonal холодно + place adverb снаружи, inside a что clause
grammarFocus.note: холодно is a predicate adverb forming a subjectless clause, "it's cold". снаружи (outside) is locational and contrasts with the directional наружу. A comma separates the clause from the main verb.

variations.note: The base form: impersonal холодно plus a locational adverb.

variations.ru: Вы понимаете, что на улице холодно?
variations.note: на улице (outdoors) is the far more usual phrasing; prepositional.
Dative Вам + не холодно asks about the hearer's own sensation.

options.note: The noun холод (cold) with какой gives an exclamatory question: "how cold it is out there".
мороз (hard frost) in the nominative, plus the imperative оденьтесь (wrap up).

paraphrases.simplest: На улице холодно.

takeaway.note: The same pairing as внутри / внутрь and дома / домой. In daily speech, "outside" is overwhelmingly на улице.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Выслушать is perfective, marking the single completed act of 'hearing someone out' (paired with выслушивать).

grammarFocus.construction: Можешь + perfective infinitive выслушать + accusative меня
grammarFocus.note: выслушать is слушать with вы-, a perfective meaning "to hear someone out". It takes the accusative. можешь + infinitive makes the request, and сейчас is a time adverb. The aspect and prefix are what matter here.

variations.note: The base form: "can you hear me out now?"
The polite можете, with the object moved forward.
The perfective imperative выслушай: "hear me out".

options.note: есть минута + infinitive: "do you have a minute to talk?"
дать + dative + infinitive: "let me speak".

paraphrases.simplest: Можешь меня выслушать?

takeaway.pattern: слушать (listen, process) vs. выслушать (hear out, completed)
takeaway.note: вы- adds "to the full, all the way out" (выслушать, выучить, выпить). You слушать музыку but выслушать человека.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Обедать is imperfective, meaning 'to have lunch' (paired with пообедать).

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective future будем обедать + locational adverb дома
grammarFocus.note: обедать (to have lunch) is imperfective, so its future is будем + infinitive. дома (at home) is a locational adverb and never declines. The perfective пообедать instead forms its future from the conjugated form, пообедаем.

variations.note: The base form: "we'll have lunch at home".
The perfective пообедаем frames it as one completed meal.
The present serves for a habit or a settled plan.

options.note: An existential with the noun обед as subject: "lunch will be at home".
давай + perfective first person plural turns it into an invitation.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы пообедаем дома.

takeaway.pattern: завтракать / обедать / ужинать and their по- perfectives
takeaway.note: All three meal verbs are imperfective; adding по- gives the perfective "to have that meal" (позавтракать, пообедать, поужинать). Aspect decides how the future is built.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ма is a colloquial shortened form of мама ('mom').

grammarFocus.construction: the clipped colloquial vocative Ма + the adverb дома
grammarFocus.note: Ма is a shortened spoken address form of мама (as is Мам), used only in speech. Being an address it takes a comma. дома is a locational adverb, and the present needs no copula.

variations.note: Мам is the same kind of clipped vocative, somewhat more common than Ма.
The full form мама — neutral and fine in writing.
The shortest version, with no address — the standard call on arriving.

options.note: The perfective пришёл (masculine) states the arrival; пришла for a woman.
вернуться (to come back) with the address at the end — word order is free.

paraphrases.simplest: Я дома!

takeaway.pattern: clipped vocatives in speech (Мам, Пап, Саш, Тань)
takeaway.note: Dropping the final vowel of a kinship term or name makes an address form usable only for calling out (×Мам пришла is impossible). It signals closeness and never appears in writing.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Парочка is a diminutive of пара ('pair'), meaning 'a couple.'

grammarFocus.construction: видите + place adverb там + accusative парочку
grammarFocus.note: парочка is the diminutive of пара (a couple), feminine, accusative парочку. видеть takes the accusative, and там is locational. The diminutive adds a fond or teasing colouring: "that little couple".

variations.note: The base form; the diminutive парочку gives it a colloquial ring.
The plain пару — neutral.
With the pronoun их (animate accusative, genitive-shaped).

options.note: стоять + nominative states their presence, with видите? as the tag.
вон туда (over there) is a directional phrase — a recast as instruction.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видите там пару?

takeaway.pattern: the diminutives -очка / -ечка add smallness or affection
takeaway.note: пара → парочка, чашка → чашечка, минута → минуточка. Beyond size they convey the speaker's warmth or lightness, and they belong to spoken register.

skeleton.note: adjective, instrumental case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Жалкий is an adjective meaning 'pitiful, pathetic.'

grammarFocus.construction: считать + animate accusative его + instrumental жалким
grammarFocus.note: The считать кого кем frame. его is the animate accusative (genitive-shaped), and the masculine instrumental of жалкий (pitiful, pathetic) is жалким. As a judgement it is quite contemptuous, so use it about people with care.

variations.note: The base form, with жалким as the verdict.
For a woman, the feminine instrumental жалкой.
Dative + жаль + accusative: "do you feel sorry for him?" — sympathy instead of contempt.

options.note: A что clause returns the word to the nominative жалкий.
жалко is the colloquial form of жаль; negated: "don't you pity him?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы думаете, что он жалкий?

takeaway.pattern: жалкий (pathetic, contemptuous) vs. жаль / жалко (sorry, sympathetic)
takeaway.note: One root, opposite directions. Он жалкий looks down on him; Мне его жаль feels for him. Don't let the shared root blur the attitude.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Пирог is a masculine noun meaning 'pie.'

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present ем + accusative пирог
grammarFocus.note: есть (to eat) is irregular: ем / ешь / ест / едим / едите / едят. пирог is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. The present covers both the ongoing act and the habit.

variations.note: The base form: "I'm eating pie".
The perfective съел means finishing it; the prefix с- supplies completion.
The partitive genitive пирога limits it to "some of the pie".

options.note: кушать is a genteel or child-directed word for есть; adults using it of themselves sound precious.
пробовать + accusative is "to taste" — a different shade of eating.

paraphrases.simplest: Я ем пирог.

takeaway.pattern: есть conjugates irregularly (ем, ешь, ест, едим, едите, едят)
takeaway.note: Don't confuse it with быть. The past of "to eat" is ел / ела / ели and the imperative ешь / ешьте. Too frequent a verb not to memorise.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Свинья is a feminine noun meaning 'pig.'

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + long-form adjective большая + the intensifier очень
grammarFocus.note: No copula in the present. свинья (pig) is feminine, so большая agrees in gender and number. очень intensifies the adjective. Note that the noun doubles as a strong insult when aimed at a person.

variations.note: The base form — a factual statement about an animal.
With the past была the adjective predicate turns instrumental, большой.
поросёнок (piglet) is masculine, hence маленький — agreement follows gender.

options.note: Какая + feminine adjective makes an exclamation: "what a big pig!"
The genitive огромного размера (of enormous size) — a stiffer, more formal modifier.

paraphrases.simplest: Эта свинья очень большая.

takeaway.pattern: свинья names an animal but insults a person
takeaway.note: Ты свинья! means "you filthy boor" and is strong abuse. Russian has many animal insults — собака, скотина, козёл — so keep the literal and abusive uses apart.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Малышка is the feminine form of малыш ('little one'), used as an affectionate term of address.

grammarFocus.construction: the address малышка + the elliptical question как ты?
grammarFocus.note: малышка is the feminine diminutive of малыш (little one), used for a partner or a small girl. Как ты? is the verbless colloquial "how are you?". The address is fenced by commas.

variations.note: The base form, with commas on both sides of the address.
Without the address — no particular addressee implied.
малыш is the masculine form; как дела? is the neutral "how's it going?"

options.note: солнышко (little sun) is a neuter diminutive endearment, for partners or children.
настроение (mood) as subject: "how are your spirits?"

paraphrases.simplest: Привет, как ты?

takeaway.note: Strictly for intimates — never at work or with strangers, so they also mark how close you claim to be. Note that even neuter forms (солнышко) are used of people.

skeleton.note: adverb, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Чудесно is an adverb meaning 'wonderfully, marvelously.'

grammarFocus.construction: говорить, что + zero copula + the predicate adverb чудесно
grammarFocus.note: A что clause after говорить takes an obligatory comma. чудесно is the short neuter form working as a predicate adverb, with всё as subject: "everything is wonderful". The adjective чудесное would modify a noun instead.

variations.note: The base form: a что clause with an impersonal-style assessment.
хорошо gives the milder "that everything's fine".

variations.ru: Вы правда думаете, что всё чудесно?
variations.note: Adding правда (really) injects doubt.

options.note: по-вашему is a parenthetical set off by a comma: "in your view".
считать + accusative + instrumental прекрасной — a more formal recast with a noun.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы говорите, что всё хорошо?

takeaway.pattern: всё + a predicate adverb in -о = a verdict on the whole situation
takeaway.note: Всё хорошо / Всё плохо / Всё чудесно / Всё готово. The neuter singular всё pairs with a short neuter form — the commonest way to sum a situation up in two words.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Маска is a feminine noun meaning 'mask.'

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past взяли + accusative маску
grammarFocus.note: взять (to take, to bring along) is perfective and takes the accusative; its plural past is взяли. маска is feminine with the accusative маску. The sentence is the standard way to check someone has brought something.

variations.note: The base form: "did you bring a mask?"
The plural маски is inanimate, so nominative-shaped.
With ты, взял for a man, взяла for a woman.

options.note: The у + genitive + есть + nominative possessive: "do you have a mask?"
A negated question with забыть: "you didn't forget it, did you?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы взяли маску?

takeaway.note: An aspect pair with completely different stems. Я беру (I take, habitually) / Я взял (I took). давать → дать shows the same stem swap.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, prepositional case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Самоубийство is a neuter noun meaning 'suicide.'

replies.gloss: Yes, it was a heavy topic.
What exactly is the book about?

grammarFocus.construction: читать + accusative книгу + о + prepositional самоубийстве
grammarFocus.note: читать takes the accusative, and книга gives книгу. The subject matter goes in о + prepositional, so самоубийство (suicide) becomes самоубийстве. The word is heavy, so it belongs to neutral or academic contexts.

variations.note: The base form, with the topic in о + prepositional.
Replacing the topic with это avoids repeating the difficult word.

variations.ru: Вы читали что-нибудь на эту тему?
variations.note: на + accusative тему, "on this subject" — the more careful phrasing.

options.note: знаком с + instrumental, "are you familiar with this book?" — formal and neutral.
попадаться + dative is "to come one's way": "have you come across such a book?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы читали эту книгу?

takeaway.pattern: neuter nouns in -ие / -ство take -и / -е in the prepositional
takeaway.note: самоубийство → о самоубийстве, решение → о решении: the -ство type ends in -е, the -ие type in -и. For sensitive topics, на эту тему is a useful hedge.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Сжечь is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'burning' (paired with сжигать).

replies.gloss: Why do you want to burn it?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive сжечь + accusative это
grammarFocus.note: сжечь (to burn) is жечь with с-, a perfective taking the accusative. It conjugates irregularly: сожгу / сожжёшь. это is the neuter pronoun, identical in nominative and accusative.

variations.note: The base form: "I want to burn this".
Object before the infinitive — the natural colloquial order.
The perfective future сожгу with the accusative plural письма — an example of the irregular stem.

options.note: избавиться от + genitive is "to get rid of" — not necessarily by fire.
The intransitive сгореть (to burn up) with пусть: "let it burn".

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу это сжечь.

takeaway.pattern: сжечь (transitive, to burn something) vs. сгореть (intransitive, to burn up)
takeaway.note: The prefix decides transitivity: Я сжёг письмо (I burned the letter) / Письмо сгорело (the letter burned). The жечь family also conjugates irregularly, so learn the forms.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Творить is imperfective, meaning 'to create,' or colloquially 'to be up to (something troublesome)' (paired with сотворить).

replies.ru: Прости, я не хотел это делать.
replies.gloss: Sorry, I didn't mean to do that.

grammarFocus.construction: the question word Что + imperfective present творишь
grammarFocus.note: творить properly means "to create", but Что ты творишь? is the set rebuke "what on earth are you doing?". Что is the accusative object, and the imperfective present scolds something in progress.

variations.note: The base form — strong reproach or astonishment.
The polite/plural творите.
делаешь is the neutral "what are you doing?", without the reproach of творишь.

options.note: The perfective past of сойти с ума: "have you lost your mind?"
зачем presses on the purpose: "what are you doing that for?"

paraphrases.simplest: Что ты делаешь?

takeaway.pattern: творить = to create, or (in reproach) to get up to
takeaway.note: The lofty творить добро (to do good) coexists with the colloquial Что ты творишь? Context and tone flip the sense entirely.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Охотиться is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of 'hunting.' Поохотиться exists as a delimitative meaning 'to hunt for a while,' not a true pair.

grammarFocus.construction: любить + imperfective infinitive охотиться + adverb вместе
grammarFocus.note: любить + infinitive takes the imperfective, since preferences are habitual. охотиться (to hunt) is reflexive, and the prey takes на + accusative (охотиться на кабана). вместе is an adverb.

variations.note: The base form: "they love hunting together".
на + accusative кабана (animate, so genitive-shaped) names the prey.
With часто it becomes a plain statement; охотятся is third person plural.

options.note: Dative + нравится + nominative охота (the noun): "they enjoy hunting".
на + accusative охоту is "to go hunting"; ездить marks repeated trips.

paraphrases.simplest: Они любят охотиться вместе.

takeaway.note: на + accusative means "after, in pursuit of": охотиться на зверя / на преступника. A bare accusative or genitive will not do.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Пожелать is perfective, marking the single completed act of 'wishing someone something' (paired with желать).

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive пожелать + dative тебе + genitive хорошего дня
grammarFocus.note: пожелать (to wish) takes an unusual pair of slots: dative for the person, genitive for what is wished. хороший день becomes хорошего дня. It is the same genitive seen in Удачи! and Всего доброго!

variations.note: The base form; dropping я is natural.
The imperfective present желаю + genitive удачи: "I wish you luck".
The verbless genitive formula: "have a good day!"

options.note: With удачный instead — the same genitive formula, practically identical.
пусть + future with the instrumental хорошим: "may the day be a good one".

paraphrases.simplest: Хорошего дня!

takeaway.note: желать / пожелать takes the wished-for thing in the genitive. Удачи! (good luck), Спокойной ночи! (good night), Всего хорошего! (all the best) are all genitives with желать left out.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular future, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Потребоваться is perfective, marking the single completed event of 'becoming necessary' (paired with требоваться).

replies.gloss: What exactly needs to be done?

grammarFocus.construction: Вы думаете + omitted что + impersonal потребуется + час
grammarFocus.note: потребоваться (to be required) is a reflexive perfective: the person who needs something goes in the dative, and the thing needed is the subject — here час, whose nominative and accusative coincide. The comma survives the dropped что.

variations.note: The base form: "do you think it will take an hour?"
Adding the dative нам names who will need it.
занять (to take time) + accusative час — the more everyday phrasing.

options.note: сколько + genitive времени asks how long; занять takes the accusative.
хватить + genitive часа, impersonal: "will an hour be enough?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы думаете, это займёт час?

takeaway.pattern: занять (to take time, accusative) vs. хватить (to suffice, genitive)
takeaway.note: Это займёт час (it will take an hour) / Часа хватит (an hour will do). Duration takes занять + accusative, sufficiency хватить + genitive.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Дыра is a feminine noun meaning 'hole.'

grammarFocus.construction: заметили + accusative дыру + в + prepositional двери
grammarFocus.note: заметить (to notice) is perfective and takes the accusative. дыра (hole) is feminine with the accusative дыру. в двери is в + prepositional, and дверь, a feminine -ь noun, has the prepositional двери.

variations.note: The base form: "did you notice the hole in the door?"
The prepositional стене: "in the wall".
The negated question softens it: "didn't you notice?"

options.note: The есть + nominative existential: "is there a hole in the door?"
The short participle повреждена (feminine): "is the door damaged?"

paraphrases.simplest: Вы заметили дыру в двери?

takeaway.pattern: feminine -ь nouns also take -и in the prepositional
takeaway.note: дверь → в двери, ночь → в ночи, любовь → о любви. Nominative, accusative and prepositional can all look alike, so let the preposition and context decide.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ордер is a masculine noun meaning '(search) warrant, order.'

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive вас + есть + nominative ордер
grammarFocus.note: у + genitive + есть + nominative is the basic possessive: having something is expressed as existence, not with a verb. ордер (warrant) is masculine, and crucially the thing possessed stands in the nominative.

variations.note: The base form: "do you have a warrant?"
тебя (genitive) for someone you address informally.
The negative is нет + genitive ордера — negation changes the case.

options.note: The imperative покажите + accusative ордер: "show me the warrant".
предъявить (to produce) + accusative документ — official register.

paraphrases.simplest: У вас есть ордер?

takeaway.pattern: у + genitive + есть + nominative (affirmative) vs. нет + genitive (negative)
takeaway.note: У меня есть книга / У меня нет книги. The possessed noun swaps from nominative to genitive under negation — a hallmark of Russian.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Предупреждать is imperfective, meaning 'to warn' (paired with предупредить).

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective future буду предупреждать + accusative тебя
grammarFocus.note: предупреждать (to warn) is imperfective, so the future is буду + infinitive. It takes the accusative. The perfective предупредить would mean one single warning; the imperfective future implies keeping someone informed repeatedly.

variations.note: The base form: "I'll keep you posted each time".
The perfective future предупрежу: "I'll give you fair warning" — once.
заранее (in advance) makes the consideration explicit.

options.ru: Я буду тебя держать в курсе.
options.note: держать в курсе (to keep someone in the loop) is a set phrase with в + prepositional.
сообщить кому governs the dative: "I'll let you know in advance".

paraphrases.simplest: Я предупрежу тебя.

takeaway.note: Two verbs of informing, two cases: предупредить друга (warn a friend) / сообщить другу (inform a friend). The frame belongs to the verb.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Фургон is a masculine noun meaning 'van, small truck.'

replies.gloss: Yes, it's been parked there a while.

grammarFocus.construction: видите + the demonstrative тот + accusative фургон
grammarFocus.note: тот points to something distant or already known, in contrast with этот. фургон (van) is masculine inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative and тот stays put. видите is present: "can you see?"

variations.note: The base form, with тот pointing into the distance.
этот makes it "this van, nearby" — a different sense of distance.

variations.ru: Вы видите тот фургон, который стоит у входа?
variations.note: A который clause identifies it; тот ... который is the standard correlative pair.

options.note: вон (over there) with colloquial word order, as if pointing.
стоять + nominative states its presence, with заметили? as the tag.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы видите тот фургон?

takeaway.note: тот flags the antecedent and который opens the clause: тот фильм, который мы смотрели. Use it when you want to pin something down precisely.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, genitive case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Мусор is a masculine noun meaning 'trash, garbage.'

replies.gloss: We need to take out the trash.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive нас + the quantity word много + genitive мусора
grammarFocus.note: When a quantity word joins the у + genitive possessive, есть drops out and the thing possessed goes genitive. мусор (rubbish) is uncountable, hence the genitive singular мусора; countables would take the genitive plural (много книг).

variations.note: The base form, with an uncountable genitive singular.
A countable noun takes the genitive plural книг; the government is the same.
мало (little) also takes the genitive — only the direction of quantity changes.

options.note: The predicate adverb грязно, impersonal: "it's very dirty here".
вынести мусор (to take the rubbish out) takes the accusative, with надо + infinitive.

paraphrases.simplest: У нас много мусора.

takeaway.note: Uncountables take the genitive singular (много воды, мало времени), countables the genitive plural (много людей, мало книг). State a quantity and switch to the genitive.

skeleton.note: past feminine, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Надоесть is perfective, marking the single completed act of 'becoming tiresome, getting sick of' (paired with надоедать).

replies.gloss: What exactly got old for you?
Maybe it's time to change something.

grammarFocus.construction: надоесть + dative мне + nominative эта работа
grammarFocus.note: надоесть (to be sick of) governs the dative, and the thing one is tired of becomes the subject in the nominative. The roles are the reverse of English: эта работа is the subject and мне the dative. The perfective past надоела agrees with работа (feminine).

variations.note: The base form; the subject работа is feminine, hence надоела.
шум is masculine, so надоел — agreement follows the subject.
With an infinitive as subject the verb is neuter: надоело. "I'm sick of waiting."

options.note: устать от + genitive is "to be tired of", with я as subject.
измучить + accusative, "this job has worn me out" — stronger.

paraphrases.simplest: Мне надоела эта работа.

takeaway.note: The same shape as нравиться: the experiencer is dative, the thing nominative. Мне нравится эта работа (I like it) / Мне надоела эта работа (I'm sick of it) — one frame, opposite feelings.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular future, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Отстать is perfective, marking the single completed act of 'falling behind, leaving someone alone' (paired with отставать).

replies.gloss: Sorry, I didn't mean to bother you.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective future отстанешь + от + genitive меня
grammarFocus.note: отстать (to leave off, to back off) takes от + genitive; меня is the genitive of я. Used as a statement, a perfective future carries the force of a demand or warning.

variations.note: The base form — declarative in shape, a demand in effect.
The perfective imperative отстань: "leave me alone" — quite forceful.
оставить в покое (to leave in peace) takes the accusative and is gentler.

options.note: A negated imperative of трогать + accusative: "don't touch me / don't bother me".
дать + dative + infinitive: "let me be alone"; одному agrees in the dative.

paraphrases.simplest: Оставь меня в покое.

takeaway.note: от + genitive is "away from". Literally the verb means falling behind — отстать от поезда (miss the train), отстать от группы (lag behind the group). Aimed at a person it means backing off.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Стул is a masculine noun meaning 'chair.'

grammarFocus.construction: perfective future подвинешь + accusative стул
grammarFocus.note: подвинуть (to shift slightly) is perfective and takes the accusative; the prefix под- conveys a small adjustment. стул is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. A perfective future in question form works as a polite request.

variations.note: The base form — a future question doing the work of a request.
The imperative подвинь with пожалуйста — more direct.
A negated future question is the politest form: "would you mind moving the chair?"

options.note: можешь + infinitive makes the same request.
The reflexive подвинуться means "shift yourself" — for asking a person to move up.

paraphrases.simplest: Подвинь стул, пожалуйста.

takeaway.pattern: a perfective future question = a polite request
takeaway.note: Ты подвинешь стул? / Вы не поможете? Putting a future into question form turns it into a request, and adding не makes it politer still.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, genitive case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Хлеб is a masculine noun meaning 'bread.'

replies.gloss: What kind do we need exactly?

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive нас + нет + genitive хлеба
grammarFocus.note: Negated possession uses нет + genitive, so хлеб becomes хлеба. The affirmative есть takes the nominative (У нас есть хлеб), but negation always requires the genitive. нет has no tense of its own: the past is не было + genitive.

variations.note: The base form, with the genitive of negation хлеба.
The past is не было + genitive; было is always neuter singular.
The future is не будет + genitive — again impersonal and neuter singular.

options.note: The reflexive закончиться (to run out), with хлеб as nominative subject.
надо + infinitive + accusative хлеб: "we need to buy bread" — moving to action.

paraphrases.simplest: У нас нет хлеба.

takeaway.pattern: есть + nominative ⇔ нет / не было / не будет + genitive
takeaway.note: Negated existence forces the genitive and freezes the verb in the neuter singular (Его не было дома, he wasn't home). The case swap between affirmative and negative is the construction to master.

skeleton.note: adverb, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Близко is an adverb meaning 'nearby, close.'

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present живёшь + the adverb близко
grammarFocus.note: жить conjugates with an inserted в: живу / живёшь / живёт. близко (nearby) is an adverb giving a vague location. To name a reference point you need близко от + genitive or рядом с + instrumental.

variations.note: The base form: "do you live nearby?"
близко от + genitive supplies the reference point: "near the centre".
рядом (right next door) implies closer than близко.

options.note: Dative + далеко + infinitive, impersonal: "is it a long way for you?"
где asks the location outright.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты живёшь близко?

takeaway.pattern: близко от + genitive / рядом с + instrumental
takeaway.note: Both mean "near", but with different prepositions and cases: близко от дома / рядом с домом. The bare adverbs (близко, рядом) leave the reference point to context.

skeleton.note: adverb, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Когда-то is an adverb meaning 'once, at some point in the past.'

grammarFocus.construction: the time adverb Когда-то + imperfective past жил + locational здесь
grammarFocus.note: когда-то means "once, at some unspecified time" in the past. The imperfective past жил describes living there over a stretch of time. The -то suffix marks something real but unspecified.

variations.note: The base form: жил for a man, жила for a woman.
когда-нибудь is "someday" in the future, with the perfective поживу (live for a while).
раньше (formerly) points to a nearer past than когда-то.

options.note: Adding давно (long ago) stresses the distance in time.
Past был + nominative predicate: "this used to be my house".

paraphrases.simplest: Раньше я здесь жил.

takeaway.pattern: когда-то (once, in the past) vs. когда-нибудь (someday, in the future)
takeaway.note: -то points to something that already happened; -нибудь to any possible future occasion. Я когда-то был в Москве (I've been) / Я когда-нибудь поеду в Москву (I'll go someday).

skeleton.note: adverb, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Никуда is an adverb meaning 'nowhere' in a motion context, used with negation.

grammarFocus.construction: the double negative никуда не + imperfective present иду
grammarFocus.note: никуда (nowhere, directional) is a negative adverb that must appear with не. The present of идти expresses movement under way, and negated it also covers plans: "I'm not going anywhere".

variations.note: The base form: "I'm not going anywhere".
The negated perfective future states intention: "I won't be going anywhere".
нигде is the locational negative: "I wasn't anywhere" — direction and location use different words.

options.note: оставаться (to stay) states it positively.
нет + genitive планов, the negated possessive: "I have no plans".

paraphrases.simplest: Я никуда не иду.

takeaway.note: All of them require не: никуда не иду / нигде не живу / никогда не был. One negative word is never enough in Russian.

skeleton.note: particle, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Всё-таки is a concessive particle meaning 'after all, nevertheless.'

grammarFocus.construction: the adverbial всё-таки + perfective past пришёл
grammarFocus.note: всё-таки (after all, nonetheless) is a hyphenated particle-like adverb marking a result contrary to expectation. пришёл is the irregular masculine past of прийти. The exclamation mark carries the delight.

variations.note: The base form: пришёл for a man, пришла for a woman.
With вы the past is always the plural пришли.
всё же is a slightly more formal synonym of всё-таки.

options.ru: Я так рад, что ты пришёл!
options.note: рад (glad) is a short form; the что clause gives the reason.

options.ru: А я думал, ты не придёшь.
options.note: думал + clause explains the surprise: "and I thought you wouldn't come".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты всё-таки пришёл!

takeaway.pattern: всё-таки / всё же = after all, nonetheless
takeaway.note: They highlight a fact that defies expectation: Он всё-таки согласился (he agreed in the end). The hyphenated всё-таки leans colloquial, всё же literary.

skeleton.note: preposition, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Среди is a preposition meaning 'among, in the midst of,' taking the genitive case.

replies.gloss: How long have you been friends?

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + среди + genitive plural друзей
grammarFocus.note: среди (among, surrounded by) governs the genitive, and друзья gives the irregular genitive plural друзей. With no copula in the present, Я здесь среди друзей stands on its own.

variations.note: The base form, среди + genitive plural.
свои (one's own people) used as a noun, genitive plural своих.
The past adds был; the prepositional phrase is unchanged.

options.note: A nominal sentence with все мои друзья (nominative plural) as subject.
как дома (as if at home) is idiomatic: "I feel at home here".

paraphrases.simplest: Я здесь среди друзей.

takeaway.note: среди друзей / среди людей / среди книг. It means "in the midst of" and pairs with plurals or collectives. The similar между takes the instrumental instead (между нами).

skeleton.note: preposition, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Благодаря is a preposition meaning 'thanks to,' taking the dative case.

grammarFocus.construction: благодаря + dative тебе
grammarFocus.note: благодаря (thanks to) is one of the rare prepositions governing the dative — it comes from a participle of благодарить. тебе is dative. Use it for favourable causes; negative ones take из-за + genitive.

variations.note: The base form, with the dative тебе.
The polite вам, also dative.
из-за + genitive marks an unwelcome cause: "I'm late because of you".

options.ru: Если бы не ты, меня бы здесь не было.
options.note: если бы не + nominative with бы — a counterfactual: "but for you, I wouldn't be here".
A nominal sentence with заслуга (merit): "the credit is yours".

paraphrases.simplest: Я здесь благодаря тебе.

takeaway.pattern: благодаря + dative (good cause) vs. из-за + genitive (bad cause)
takeaway.note: благодаря помощи (thanks to the help) / из-за дождя (because of the rain). The evaluation decides both preposition and case, so weigh it whenever you give a reason.

skeleton.note: conjunction, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Словно is a comparative conjunction meaning 'as if, just like.'

replies.ru: Мы просто хорошо понимаем друг друга.
replies.gloss: We just understand each other well.

grammarFocus.construction: the comparative particle словно + imperfective present читаешь + accusative plural мои мысли
grammarFocus.note: словно (as if) is a comparative particle and does not affect any case government. мысли (thoughts) is feminine plural with an accusative identical to the nominative, matched by мои. читать мысли is the set "to read someone's mind".

variations.note: The base form, with словно introducing the simile.

variations.ru: Ты как будто читаешь мои мысли.
variations.note: как будто also means "as if" and is more colloquial than словно.
Drop the comparative and it becomes a flat exclamation of surprise.

options.note: без + genitive plural слов: "you understand me without words".

options.ru: Я как раз об этом думал.
options.note: как раз (just) with об этом (prepositional): "that's exactly what I was thinking".

paraphrases.simplest: Ты читаешь мои мысли!

takeaway.pattern: словно / как будто / точно = as if
takeaway.note: All three introduce comparisons without touching case government. словно is slightly literary, как будто colloquial, точно closer to "exactly as though".

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ложь is a feminine noun meaning 'a lie.'

replies.gloss: No, I'm looking for the truth.

grammarFocus.construction: верить в + accusative ложь
grammarFocus.note: верить в + accusative means "to believe in". ложь (a lie) is a feminine -ь noun whose accusative is identical to the nominative. Its genitive, however, is лжи, with the stem vowel dropping — a noun that shifts shape considerably.

variations.note: The base form; the accusative ложь matches the nominative.
Adding эту (feminine singular accusative) makes the case visible.
The dative ему means believing what he says — the preposition changes the meaning.

options.note: принимать за + accusative is "to take something for": "do you take this for the truth?"
The dative этому with правда: "do you really believe that?"

paraphrases.simplest: Ты веришь в эту ложь?

takeaway.pattern: ложь changes stem across cases (ложь / лжи / ложью)
takeaway.note: Nominative and accusative ложь, genitive/dative/prepositional лжи, instrumental ложью. The о is a fleeting vowel; любовь (любви) behaves the same way.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Воздух is a masculine noun meaning 'air.'

grammarFocus.construction: dative Мне + нужен + nominative свежий воздух
grammarFocus.note: нужен is a short-form adjective: the person who needs goes in the dative and the thing needed in the nominative, with нужен agreeing with it (нужен воздух / нужна вода / нужно время / нужны деньги). воздух is masculine.

variations.note: The base form; нужен agrees with воздух (masculine).
вода is feminine, hence нужна.
With an infinitive it is the neuter нужно: "I need to rest".

options.note: дышать takes the instrumental: "I want to breathe some fresh air".
на + accusative воздух, "I need to get outside" — verbless and colloquial.

paraphrases.simplest: Мне нужен свежий воздух.

takeaway.pattern: dative + нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны + nominative
takeaway.note: The thing needed is the subject, so нужен agrees with it. The structure inverts English "I need": Мне нужны деньги takes the plural нужны.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Звук is a masculine noun meaning 'sound.'

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present слышу + accusative странный звук
grammarFocus.note: слышать (to hear) is a verb of perception taking the accusative, and the present describes an ongoing state. звук is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and странный stays unchanged. Deliberate listening is слушать.

variations.note: The base form: "I hear a strange sound".
The past слышал: "I heard"; слышала for a woman.
Under negation the object may go genitive: звука.

options.note: Что это за + nominative is the set "what sort of ... is that?"
откуда (from where) asks about the source, with the verb left out.

paraphrases.simplest: Я слышу странный звук.

takeaway.note: The same split as видеть / смотреть. Я слышу музыку (I can hear music) / Я слушаю музыку (I'm listening to music) — the verb encodes whether it is passive or deliberate.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, prepositional case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Университет is a masculine noun meaning 'university.'

grammarFocus.construction: the reflexive учусь + в + prepositional университете
grammarFocus.note: учиться (to study, to be enrolled) is reflexive, with the place in в / на + prepositional; the prepositional of университет is университете. The subject studied, by contrast, goes in the dative (учиться русскому языку).

variations.note: The base form: "I'm at university".
The prepositional школе: "I'm at school".
изучать takes the accusative and means studying a subject — a different frame.

options.note: студент + genitive университета as a nominal sentence: "I'm a university student".
получать образование (to receive an education) takes the accusative — formal register.

paraphrases.simplest: Я учусь в университете.

уверен в + prepositional: "are you confident about this restaurant?"
