keyPoint: Родиться is biaspectual (the same form serves as both imperfective and perfective), meaning 'to be born.'

replies.ru: А я родился в другом городе.
replies.gloss: I was born in a different city.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past родился + the locational adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: родиться (to be born) is a reflexive perfective with a shifting stress: родился / родилась. The place of birth takes в / на + prepositional or an adverb like здесь. The transitive родить means "to give birth".

variations.note: The base form: родился for a man, родилась for a woman.
в + prepositional Москве gives the birthplace.
в + prepositional году gives the year: "I was born in 1990".

options.note: родом is an adverbial instrumental: "I'm from here originally".
A nominal sentence with родной (native): "this is my home town".

paraphrases.simplest: Я родился здесь.

takeaway.pattern: birthplace takes в / на + prepositional; years take в + prepositional
takeaway.note: родиться в Москве / в деревне / на Урале (the place name decides the preposition), в 1990 году, в мае. A full date puts the day in the genitive (пятого мая).

skeleton.note: imperative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Открывать is imperfective, meaning 'to open' (paired with открыть).

grammarFocus.construction: negative imperative Не открывай + accusative дверь
grammarFocus.note: Negative imperatives take the imperfective, hence открывай. The perfective Не открой would be a warning ("mind you don't open it"), a different meaning. дверь is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative.

variations.note: The base form — a general prohibition: "don't open the door".
The polite/plural открывайте.
никому (to nobody) is a negative dative — the obligatory double negative.

options.note: нельзя + imperfective infinitive, impersonal — stated as a rule.
пусть + perfective with the instrumental закрытой: "let the door stay closed".

paraphrases.simplest: Не открывай дверь.

takeaway.pattern: negative imperatives take the imperfective as a rule
takeaway.note: Не открывай (don't open — prohibition) / Не открой (be careful not to open — warning). For a prohibition, always choose the imperfective.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ставить is imperfective, meaning 'to put, park' (paired with поставить).

grammarFocus.construction: уметь + imperfective infinitive ставить + accusative машину
grammarFocus.note: уметь means "to know how to" — a skill — as opposed to мочь (circumstantial possibility). ставить машину is "to park a car". машина is feminine with the accusative машину, and the perfective is поставить.

variations.note: The base form, asking about a skill with уметь.
водить машину is "to drive a car" — the set phrase, using the multidirectional водить.
мочь + perfective asks about circumstances: "can you park here?"

options.note: парковаться (to park) is a borrowed reflexive verb — the modern phrasing.
права (a licence) is plural: "do you have a licence?" — asking about the skill indirectly.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты умеешь парковаться?

takeaway.note: Я умею плавать (I can swim — I know how) / Я могу плавать (I'm able to / allowed to swim now). уметь always takes an imperfective infinitive.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Нести is imperfective, meaning 'to carry' (paired with понести).

grammarFocus.construction: the unidirectional motion verb несу + accusative твою сумку
grammarFocus.note: нести (to carry by hand) is unidirectional, and the present несу means carrying it right now. The multidirectional counterpart is носить. сумка is feminine with the accusative сумку, matched by твою.

variations.note: The base form — carrying it at this moment.
The multidirectional носить for habit: "I always carry this bag around".
The perfective принести is "to bring"; при- adds arrival.

options.note: взять (to take) with Давай я... — offering to carry it.
у + genitive меня: "I've got your bag" — stating where it is.

paraphrases.simplest: Я несу твою сумку.

takeaway.note: Carrying verbs have the same three-tier structure as идти / ходить: нести сумку домой (carrying it home now) / носить сумку (carry it about) / принести сумку (bring it).

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Везти is imperfective, meaning 'to carry/drive (by vehicle)' (paired with повезти).

grammarFocus.construction: the unidirectional везу + accusative тебя + directional adverb домой
grammarFocus.note: везти (to transport by vehicle) is unidirectional, and везу means doing it now; the multidirectional is возить. домой is a directional adverb needing no preposition. Leading someone on foot would be вести.

variations.note: The base form — driving you home right now.
The multidirectional возить for repetition: "I drive the children to school".
The perfective отвезти is "to deliver"; от- adds taking away from here.

options.note: подвезти до + genitive: "I'll give you a lift home".
The imperative садись (get in) with поедем (let's go) — colloquial.

paraphrases.simplest: Я везу тебя домой.

takeaway.pattern: везти (vehicle, unidirectional) / возить (vehicle, multidirectional) vs. нести / носить (by hand)
takeaway.note: The root encodes the means of carrying, then splits again by directionality — four forms in all: везти чемодан (by car) / нести чемодан (by hand).

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ездить is a multidirectional motion verb with only an imperfective form (the unidirectional verb is ехать; the perfective varies by context, e.g. поехать 'to set off' / съездить 'to make a round trip').

grammarFocus.construction: the multidirectional ездить (езжу) + на + prepositional метро
grammarFocus.note: ездить (to travel back and forth by vehicle) is multidirectional, so езжу expresses a habit. The means of transport goes in на + prepositional (на метро, на машине). метро is indeclinable, so its form never changes.

variations.note: The base form — a habit: "I take the metro".
The unidirectional еду: "I'm on the metro right now".

variations.ru: Я езжу на работу на машине.
variations.note: на работу (direction, accusative) plus на машине (means, prepositional) — the same preposition in two roles.

options.note: пользоваться + instrumental метро is "to use"; the indeclinable noun looks the same.
добираться (to get there) also pairs with на + prepositional.

paraphrases.simplest: Я езжу на метро.

takeaway.pattern: means of transport takes на + prepositional (except пешком)
takeaway.note: на метро / на машине / на автобусе / на поезде. The exception is "on foot", пешком, an adverb from the instrumental that takes no preposition.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Лететь is imperfective, meaning 'to fly, be flying (to)' (paired with полететь).

grammarFocus.construction: the time adverb Завтра + the unidirectional лечу + directional adverb домой
grammarFocus.note: лететь (to fly) is unidirectional, and its present expresses a settled future plan — the classic pairing with завтра. The multidirectional is летать. домой is directional.

variations.note: The base form, with a present tense for a fixed plan.
The multidirectional летаю for repetition, with в + accusative Москву.
The perfective полечу is also future, but the present sounds more natural for a plan.

options.note: у + genitive + nominative самолёт: "I have a flight tomorrow" — colloquial.
возвращаться (to return) says "going home" without naming the means.

paraphrases.simplest: Завтра я лечу домой.

takeaway.pattern: the present of a unidirectional motion verb = a settled plan
takeaway.note: Завтра я лечу / В субботу мы едем / Вечером я иду в кино. Just like English "I'm flying tomorrow", a fixed arrangement takes the present.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Падать is imperfective, describing repeated or ongoing falling (paired with упасть).

grammarFocus.construction: любить + infinitive смотреть + a как clause + падает снег
grammarFocus.note: смотреть, как... is the set "to watch something happen", and the comma before как is obligatory. Both идёт снег and падает снег mean "it's snowing", with снег as the nominative subject. любить + infinitive takes the imperfective.

variations.ru: Ты любишь смотреть, как падает снег?
variations.note: The base form; verb-before-subject is the natural order inside the clause.

variations.ru: Ты любишь смотреть, как идёт снег?
variations.note: идёт снег is the more usual way to say "it's snowing".
The noun снегопад (snowfall) replaces the whole clause.

options.note: нравится, когда... is "do you like it when..."; the comma is required.
With зимние вечера (winter evenings) in the accusative plural.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты любишь смотреть, как идёт снег?

takeaway.note: After a verb of perception the content comes as a как clause, with its own nominative subject. English "watch the snow fall" becomes a clause in Russian.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Показывать is imperfective, meaning 'to show, give a tour of' (paired with показать).

grammarFocus.construction: показывать + dative тебе + accusative город
grammarFocus.note: показывать (to show) takes two slots: the dative for the person and the accusative for the thing. город is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. The imperfective present means showing you around right now.

variations.note: The base form, with both dative and accusative.
The perfective future покажу offers it: "I'll show you the city".
The accusative plural достопримечательности (sights), with вам in the dative.

options.note: проводить экскурсию (to give a tour) takes the accusative, with a dative for the person.
The рассказать кому что frame: "come on, I'll tell you everything".

paraphrases.simplest: Я покажу тебе город.

takeaway.note: дать, сказать, показать, объяснить, передать all share this frame. Verbs of giving and conveying use one pattern, so learn it once.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Решать is imperfective, meaning 'to decide' (paired with решить).

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present решаешь + the emphatic pronoun сам
grammarFocus.note: сам (oneself) is an emphatic pronoun agreeing with the subject in gender, number and case (сам / сама / сами). The imperfective решать presents it as an ongoing or general truth: deciding is yours to do. The perfective решить would be one decision.

variations.note: The base form: сам for a man, сама for a woman.
With вы, the plural сами.
As an imperative it hands it over: "decide for yourself".

options.note: A nominal sentence with решение: "that's your call".

options.ru: Я не буду за тебя решать.
options.note: за + accusative тебя means "on your behalf": "I won't decide for you".

paraphrases.simplest: Решай сам.

takeaway.pattern: сам (oneself, emphasising the subject) vs. себя (oneself as object)
takeaway.note: Я сам решил (I decided it myself — emphasis) / Я виню себя (I blame myself — the object of the action). сам strengthens the subject, себя receives the action.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Нуждаться is a stative imperfective verb meaning 'to need,' with no perfective counterpart.

grammarFocus.construction: нуждаться в + prepositional помощи
grammarFocus.note: нуждаться (to be in need) is a reflexive verb governing в + prepositional; the prepositional of помощь is помощи. It is formal, and everyday speech prefers dative + нужен (Мне нужна помощь).

variations.note: The base form — formal, more written than spoken.
Dative + нужна + nominative — overwhelmingly the conversational choice.
The prepositional поддержке: the same frame with a different object.

options.note: The imperative of помочь + dative: "please help me".
Dative + infinitive, impersonal: "I can't manage alone"; одному agrees in the dative.

paraphrases.simplest: Мне нужна помощь.

takeaway.pattern: нуждаться в + prepositional (formal) vs. dative + нужен + nominative (everyday)
takeaway.note: нуждаться в деньгах / Мне нужны деньги. Same meaning, different register: нуждаться for documents and journalism, нужен for conversation.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Разрешить is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'giving permission' (paired with разрешать).

grammarFocus.construction: можешь + perfective infinitive разрешить + dative мне + infinitive войти
grammarFocus.note: разрешить (to permit) takes a dative for the person and an infinitive for the action: мне is who is permitted, войти what is permitted. Two infinitives stack up, each belonging to a different verb.

variations.note: The base form, with both dative and infinitive.
The imperative разреши asks directly: "let me in".
можно + infinitive, impersonal — the shortest and most everyday version.

options.note: позволить takes the same dative + infinitive but is politer and more formal.
могу + infinitive asks about your own options, and works as a request for permission.

paraphrases.simplest: Можно войти?

takeaway.note: Verbs of permission put the person in the dative and the action in the infinitive. запретить (to forbid) uses the same frame (запретить мне курить), making a neat positive/negative pair.

skeleton.note: past masculine, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Запретить is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'forbidding' (paired with запрещать).

grammarFocus.construction: запретить + dative мне + accusative кофе
grammarFocus.note: запретить (to forbid) takes a dative for the person plus either an infinitive or an accusative for what is forbidden. кофе is indeclinable, so its form never changes. "The doctor forbade me coffee" means I'm not to drink it.

variations.note: The base form, with the (indeclinable) accusative кофе.
Adding the infinitive пить spells out the action.
разрешить reverses the meaning with the same frame.

options.note: Dative + нельзя + accusative, impersonal: "coffee is off limits for me".
больше не (no longer) states the outcome instead.

paraphrases.simplest: Мне нельзя кофе.

takeaway.note: запретить детям сладкое (forbid the children sweets) / запретить мне курить (forbid me to smoke). What is forbidden can be a noun or an action.

skeleton.note: imperative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Позвать is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'calling for someone' (paired with звать).

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Позови + dative мне + animate accusative врача
grammarFocus.note: The imperative of позвать (to call) is позови. The person called goes in the accusative (врач is animate, hence врача), and the dative мне means "for me". It is the set phrase for an emergency.

variations.note: The polite/plural позовите.
вызвать (to summon) is the dedicated verb for calling a doctor or ambulance — more official.
Dropping the dative and adding быстро (quick) makes it urgent.

options.note: нужен + nominative, impersonal: "a doctor is needed!"
скорая (ambulance) is an adjective used as a noun; accusative скорую.

paraphrases.simplest: Вызовите врача!

takeaway.note: позвать друга (call a friend over) / вызвать врача, такси, полицию (summon a professional or service). Both take the accusative, but the manner of calling differs.

skeleton.note: imperative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Кричать is imperfective, meaning 'to shout' (paired with крикнуть).

grammarFocus.construction: negative imperative Не кричи + на + accusative меня
grammarFocus.note: кричать (to shout) takes на + accusative for "to shout at someone". The negative imperative uses the imperfective кричи. The на + accusative frame marks where anger is aimed — the same as злиться на and сердиться на.

variations.note: The base form: "don't shout at me".
The polite/plural кричите.
не надо + imperfective infinitive — a milder prohibition.

options.note: The comparative adverb спокойнее offers the alternative: "speak more calmly".
повышать голос (to raise one's voice) takes the accusative; зачем presses the point.

paraphrases.simplest: Не кричи на меня.

takeaway.pattern: the target of anger takes на + accusative
takeaway.note: кричать на кого / злиться на кого / сердиться на кого / обижаться на кого. Emotions directed at a person all share this frame.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Улыбаться is imperfective, meaning 'to smile' (paired with улыбнуться).

replies.gloss: It's just a habit of mine.

grammarFocus.construction: the frequency adverb всегда + reflexive present улыбаешься
grammarFocus.note: улыбаться (to smile) is reflexive and takes no accusative; the person smiled at goes in the dative (улыбаться мне). всегда plus the present states a habit or a trait. The perfective улыбнуться is one smile.

variations.note: The base form: "you're always smiling".
The perfective улыбнулся with the dative мне: "you smiled at me".
With вы, улыбаетесь — the reflexive second person plural.

options.note: у + genitive + nominative настроение: "you're always in a good mood".
приветливый (friendly) as predicate, agreeing in gender.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты всегда улыбаешься.

takeaway.note: The recipient of a smile is dative (улыбаться ребёнку). Many verbs of expressive gesture take the dative: улыбаться, кивать, махать кому.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Встречать is imperfective, meaning 'to meet, go greet' (paired with встретить).

replies.gloss: What time does the flight land?
Want me to come with you?

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present встречаю + animate accusative друга + в + prepositional аэропорту
grammarFocus.note: встречать (to meet, to greet an arrival) takes the accusative, and друг being animate gives друга. в аэропорту uses the special locative ending -у with end stress, like в саду and на мосту.

variations.note: The base form; the special locative аэропорту is the point.
The perfective встречу gives the future: "I'll meet him".
The reflexive встречаться с + instrumental means meeting each other — a different sense.

options.ru: Я поеду в аэропорт за другом.
options.note: за + instrumental другом means "to fetch a friend" — the purpose frame.
прилетать (to fly in) with the accusative его — split into two clauses.

paraphrases.simplest: Я встречаю друга в аэропорту.

takeaway.pattern: the special locative in -у (в аэропорту, в саду, на мосту, в лесу)
takeaway.note: Some masculine nouns take -у instead of -е for location, with the stress moving to the ending. в лесу (in the forest) vs. о лесе (about the forest) — the meaning decides the ending.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Объяснять is imperfective, meaning 'to explain' (paired with объяснить).

grammarFocus.construction: объяснять + dative тебе + accusative правило
grammarFocus.note: объяснять (to explain) takes two slots: the dative for the person and the accusative for the content. правило is neuter, so accusative = nominative. The imperfective present means explaining it right now.

variations.note: The base form, with dative and accusative.
The perfective объясню offers it: "I'll explain the rule".
The accusative plural правила with вам in the dative; neuter plurals also match the nominative.

options.ru: Я расскажу тебе, как это работает.
options.note: рассказать + dative with a как clause: "I'll tell you how it works".
на + prepositional примере (with an example), switching to показать.

paraphrases.simplest: Я объясню тебе правило.

takeaway.note: дать, сказать, показать, объяснить, обещать all share the frame. English puts "to someone" after the object; Russian lets case do the work, so word order is free.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Проверять is imperfective, meaning 'to check' (paired with проверить).

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present проверяет + accusative plural работы
grammarFocus.note: проверять (to check, to mark) takes the accusative. работы here means pupils' papers; inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative. The subject учитель is masculine singular, hence проверяет.

variations.note: The base form: "the teacher is marking the papers".
учительница (a female teacher) with тетради (exercise books); the verb form is the same.
The perfective проверил: "has finished marking".

options.note: ставить оценки (to give marks) is a set phrase with the accusative.
The reflexive passive проверяются: "the papers are still being marked".

paraphrases.simplest: Учитель проверяет работы.

takeaway.pattern: работа is "work" in the singular, "papers / works" in the plural
takeaway.note: Я иду на работу (off to work) / Учитель проверяет работы (marking papers) / работы Пушкина (Pushkin's works). The plural widens the meaning.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Выбирать is imperfective, describing the process of 'choosing' (paired with выбрать).

replies.ru: Не торопись, у нас есть время.

grammarFocus.construction: the durative adverb долго + imperfective present выбираю (no object)
grammarFocus.note: долго (for a long time) measures duration and pairs with the imperfective, not the perfective. выбирать normally takes an accusative, but here the object is dropped to state a trait: "I take ages choosing".

variations.note: The base form: "it takes me ages to choose".
With the accusative подарок in the past: "I spent a long time choosing a present".
The perfective выбрал pairs with быстро, never with долго.

options.note: Dative + трудно + perfective infinitive: "I find it hard to choose".
With думать instead: "I always take a long time to think".

paraphrases.simplest: Я долго выбираю.

takeaway.pattern: долго + imperfective vs. за + accusative + perfective
takeaway.note: Я долго читал книгу (I read it for a long time) / Я прочитал книгу за два дня (I finished it in two days). Duration takes the imperfective; elapsed time takes a perfective with за.

skeleton.note: 3rd person plural present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Входить is imperfective, meaning 'to enter' (paired with войти).

replies.gloss: There are always so many people here.
Let's wait for the next train.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present входят + в + accusative метро
grammarFocus.note: входить (to enter) takes в + accusative for direction. метро is indeclinable, so the form never changes, but the case is accusative. люди is nominative plural, hence входят. The locative в метро would look identical but mean something else.

variations.note: The base form, with directional в + accusative.
на + prepositional names the means of transport: "people travel by metro" — distinct from directional в + accusative.
выходить из + genitive: "people are coming out of the metro"; метро stays unchanged.

options.note: заходить suggests dropping in — more colloquial than входить.

options.ru: На входе в метро много людей.
options.note: вход в + accusative (the entrance to) with много + genitive plural.

paraphrases.simplest: Люди входят в метро.

takeaway.pattern: входить в + accusative / выходить из + genitive
takeaway.note: Entering takes в + accusative, leaving из + genitive. With indeclinable nouns (метро, такси, кафе) the form gives nothing away, so only the verb and preposition reveal the case.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Терять is imperfective, meaning 'to lose' (paired with потерять).

replies.gloss: You need a keychain with a tracker.
I do that a lot too.

grammarFocus.construction: the frequency adverb часто + imperfective present теряю + accusative plural ключи
grammarFocus.note: терять (to lose) takes the accusative as an imperfective, and часто plus the present states a habit. ключи is an inanimate plural, so the accusative matches the nominative. The perfective потерять would be one loss.

variations.note: The base form — a habit: "I often lose my keys".
The perfective потерял: one specific loss.
With постоянно (constantly) and the accusative plural вещи.

options.note: пропадать (to go missing) is intransitive, so ключи becomes the subject.
рассеянный (absent-minded) as predicate, agreeing in gender.

paraphrases.simplest: Я часто теряю ключи.

takeaway.pattern: терять (to lose, transitive) vs. пропадать (to go missing, intransitive)
takeaway.note: Я потерял ключи (I lost the keys) / Ключи пропали (the keys have vanished). The subject shifts with where you place the responsibility.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Мечтать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of 'dreaming.' Помечтать exists as a delimitative meaning 'to daydream for a while,' not a true pair.

replies.gloss: What kind of house are you imagining?
I hope your dream comes true.

grammarFocus.construction: мечтать о + prepositional доме
grammarFocus.note: мечтать (to dream of, to long for) is an imperfective governing о + prepositional; the prepositional of дом is доме. о becomes об before a vowel. It has no perfective, so its future is буду мечтать.

variations.note: The base form, о + prepositional доме.
The prepositional путешествии: "I dream of travelling".
With an infinitive it means "I dream of buying" — no preposition needed.

options.note: хотеть + accusative puts it plainly: "I want my own house".
A nominal sentence with мечта as subject and a dash before the predicate.

спуститься (to go down) uses the same frame — the route is по + dative either way.

забыть о + prepositional means forgetting about it, not leaving it behind.

за + instrumental пальто (to fetch the coat) — the form is unchanged.

нужно + infinitive, impersonal: "one needs to take off shoes here".

принято (it is customary) is a short neuter participle: "that's our custom".

grammarFocus.note: часы (a clock or watch) is plural-only in this sense, so the verb agrees in the plural, работают, and the possessive is мои. The singular час means "an hour" — a different word altogether.

The reflexive сломаться (to break) in the plural past сломались.
The set way to ask the time; here час is the singular nominative meaning "o'clock".

takeaway.note: Мои часы новые (my watch is new — plural agreement) / Прошёл час (an hour has passed — singular). One root, two meanings split by number.

grammarFocus.note: купить (to buy) takes the accusative. кольцо is neuter, so the accusative matches the nominative and красивое is neuter too. Its genitive singular and nominative plural are both кольца, distinguished only by stress.

variations.note: The base form, with a neuter accusative.
The accusative plural кольца with красивые — inanimate, so nominative-shaped.
в + accusative подарок (as a present) is the set way to name the purpose.

options.note: выбрать shifts the focus to the choosing.
Dative нам + понравилось + nominative кольцо: "we really liked it".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы купили красивое кольцо.

takeaway.pattern: neuter nouns in -о / -е have nominative = accusative
takeaway.note: кольцо, окно, место, море. Neuters never distinguish the two cases in either number, so word order and the verb reveal the role.

keyPoint: Шея is a feminine noun meaning 'neck.'

replies.gloss: How long has it been hurting?

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive меня + болит + nominative шея
grammarFocus.note: болеть (to hurt) makes the aching body part the nominative subject, while the person in pain goes in у + genitive. шея is feminine singular, hence болит; plural parts take болят.

The plural зубы takes болят — the verb agrees with the subject.
The past болела (feminine singular): "I had a headache".

options.note: Dative + больно + infinitive, impersonal: "it hurts to turn my head".
The noun боль with в + prepositional шее: "I have a pain in my neck".

keyPoint: Плечо is a neuter noun meaning 'shoulder.'

replies.gloss: You should go see a doctor.
I can give you a massage.

grammarFocus.note: плечо (shoulder) is neuter, but болит is third person singular and looks the same regardless. Since болеть makes the aching part the subject, any singular part — neuter, feminine or masculine — takes болит; plural parts take болят.

variations.note: The base form — a neuter singular subject still takes болит.
The plural плечи takes болят, referring to both shoulders.
The perfective заболеть means the pain started; за- adds onset, and the neuter past is заболело.

options.note: мочь + infinitive describes the symptom concretely: "I can't lift my arm".
The noun боль with в + prepositional плече: "I have a pain in my shoulder".

paraphrases.simplest: У меня болит плечо.

takeaway.note: болит (it hurts now) / заболело (it started hurting) / болело (it hurt). The prefix за- marks onset — right for naming the moment a symptom began.

keyPoint: Грудь is a feminine noun meaning 'chest.'

replies.gloss: That's serious, you need a doctor.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive меня + болит + feminine nominative грудь
grammarFocus.note: грудь (chest) is a feminine noun in -ь, identical in nominative and accusative, and болит is third person singular. Chest pain is a medically important phrase worth knowing for a doctor's visit.

variations.note: The base form, with a feminine -ь noun as subject.
в + prepositional груди makes the location vaguer: "it hurts in my chest".
сердце is neuter, so the past is болело.

options.note: Dative + тяжело + infinitive, impersonal: "it's hard for me to breathe".

options.ru: Вызовите врача, у меня боль в груди.

keyPoint: Живот is a masculine noun meaning 'stomach.'

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb опять + болит + masculine nominative живот
grammarFocus.note: опять (again) marks repetition and suits chronic or recurring symptoms. живот (stomach) is masculine nominative, and болит is the third person singular agreeing with a singular subject.

variations.note: The base form, with опять marking the recurrence.
снова is the more neutral synonym of опять.

variations.ru: У меня весь день болит живот.
variations.note: весь день (all day) is an accusative time phrase, marking duration.

options.note: тошнить is an impersonal verb taking the accusative: "I feel sick", with no subject.
Dative + нужно + к + dative врачу: "I need to see a doctor".

paraphrases.simplest: У меня болит живот.

takeaway.note: опять often carries irritation, снова is neutral, and ещё раз counts the repetition ("one more time"). For recurring symptoms, опять and снова are the usual choices.

keyPoint: Кожа is a feminine noun meaning 'skin.'

variations.note: The base form — a description with есть left out.
The plural глаза takes the plural adjective красивые.
голос is masculine, hence мягкий: "he has a soft voice".

Какая with the possessive construction makes an exclamation.

options.note: есть ли is an embedded question with the particle ли: "we'll see whether there's Wi-Fi".
узнать про + accusative is the colloquial "find out about".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы проверим интернет в отеле.

takeaway.note: Accusative matches the nominative, the prepositional ends in -е (в отеле) and the genitive in -я (отеля). Feminine -ь nouns (дверь → двери) differ from the genitive onwards.

skeleton.note: neuter noun (indeclinable), accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Фото is an indeclinable neuter noun meaning 'photo.'

grammarFocus.construction: отправить + accusative это фото + dative plural друзьям
grammarFocus.note: отправить takes two slots: dative for the recipients, accusative for the thing. фото is an indeclinable neuter loanword with an identical accusative, and это marks it as neuter. The dative plural of друзья is друзьям.

variations.note: The base form, with the dative plural друзьям.
In the plural, эти фото — only эти shows the number, since фото never changes.
фотография declines normally (accusative фотографию), with the dative singular другу.

options.note: показать uses the same dative + accusative frame: "we'll show the photo to friends".
скинуть (to drop, to send) is colloquial, with в + accusative чат for the destination.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы отправим это фото друзьям.

takeaway.pattern: the indeclinable фото and its modifiers
takeaway.note: это фото (singular) / эти фото (plural). The form never changes, so only a demonstrative or adjective shows number. Use the full фотография and you get normal declension.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Телевизор is a masculine noun meaning 'television.'

replies.gloss: Why? There's an interesting movie on.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective imperative Выключи + locational здесь + accusative телевизор
grammarFocus.note: выключить (to switch off) takes the accusative, and its imperative is выключи. телевизор is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. Its opposite is включить (to switch on).

variations.note: The base form — a perfective imperative for a single action.
The polite/plural выключите with пожалуйста.
включить is "switch on" — the prefixes в- and вы- reverse the action.

options.note: можешь + infinitive recasts it as a polite request.
сделать потише (turn it down) uses a comparative adverb.

paraphrases.simplest: Выключи телевизор.

takeaway.note: The prefixes в- (in) and вы- (out) map onto switching on and off. The same pair gives входить / выходить (enter / exit) — one spatial intuition behind both.

skeleton.note: neuter noun (indeclinable), accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Радио is an indeclinable neuter noun meaning 'radio.'

replies.gloss: Which station do you listen to?

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present слушаю + the indeclinable accusative радио + instrumental утром
grammarFocus.note: слушать (to listen) is the deliberate verb and takes the accusative. радио is an indeclinable neuter loanword, so the accusative looks the same. утром is an instrumental time expression needing no preposition, and the present states a habit.

variations.note: The base form — a habit: "I listen to the radio in the morning".
музыка declines normally, accusative музыку.
слышать is the passive "I can hear the radio" — distinct from deliberate слушать.

options.note: по + dative plural утрам (of a morning) with включать naming the action.
играть (to be playing) with у + genitive: "the radio is on at my place in the morning".

paraphrases.simplest: Я слушаю радио утром.

takeaway.note: Я слушаю радио (I listen to the radio) / Я слышу радио (I can hear it). Both take the accusative; the verb says whether it is intentional.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, genitive case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Энергия is a feminine noun meaning 'energy.'

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive меня + нет + genitive энергии
grammarFocus.note: Negated possession takes нет + genitive. энергия is a feminine noun in -ия, so the genitive is энергии. The affirmative would be У меня есть энергия, in the nominative — negation swaps the case.

variations.note: The base form, with the genitive of negation энергии.
The genitive plural сил from силы: "I have no strength" — a very common phrase.
The past is не было + genitive; было is always neuter singular.

options.note: The perfective past of устать: "I'm very tired", agreeing in gender.
Dative + не хватает + genitive, impersonal: "I'm short of energy".

paraphrases.simplest: У меня нет энергии.

takeaway.note: нет времени / нет денег / нет сил / нет энергии. Negation always forces the genitive, and the verb is frozen in the neuter singular: нет, не было, не будет.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Газ is a masculine noun meaning 'gas.'

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present выключаем + accusative газ + перед + instrumental уходом
grammarFocus.note: выключать (to switch off) is imperfective, stating a habit. перед + instrumental means "before", and the instrumental of уход (departure) is уходом. An action noun lets you express time without a clause.

variations.note: The base form, with the action noun уходом for "before leaving".
Opened out into a когда clause — the comma is obligatory.
The instrumental выходом from выход, recast as an imperative.

options.note: The verbal adverb уходя (as we leave) — more written in style.
A negated imperative with забыть + perfective infinitive: "don't forget to turn off the gas".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы выключаем газ перед уходом.

takeaway.pattern: перед + instrumental with an action noun = "before doing"
takeaway.note: перед уходом / перед сном / перед обедом. An action noun replaces a subordinate clause, and после + genitive (после обеда) is its counterpart.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, genitive case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Молоко is a neuter noun meaning 'milk.'

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive нас + нет + genitive молока
grammarFocus.note: Negated possession takes нет + genitive. молоко is neuter with the genitive молока; being uncountable it has no normal plural. The affirmative is У нас есть молоко, in the nominative.

variations.note: The base form, with the neuter genitive молока.
The genitive хлеба — the same frame with another staple.
больше нет (no more) with the genitive, and the word order reversed.

options.note: The reflexive закончиться (to run out), with молоко as nominative subject.
надо + infinitive + accusative молоко: "we need to buy milk".

paraphrases.simplest: У нас нет молока.

takeaway.pattern: the genitive of uncountables (молока, хлеба, воды, времени)
takeaway.note: After negation or a quantity word they take the genitive singular (нет молока / много молока). The partitive genitive (Дай молока, give me some milk) uses the same form.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Мясо is a neuter noun meaning 'meat.'

replies.gloss: Since when are you a vegetarian?

grammarFocus.construction: negated не ем + accusative мясо
grammarFocus.note: есть (to eat) is irregular: ем / ешь / ест. мясо is neuter, so accusative = nominative. Under negation a specific object may stay accusative, but the genitive мяса is also possible (Я не ем мяса).

variations.note: The base form — a habit: "I don't eat meat".
The genitive of negation мяса sounds more sweeping and general.
A predicate noun: "I'm a vegetarian"; вегетарианка for a woman.

options.note: употреблять (to consume) is formal: "I don't consume meat".
Dative + нельзя + accusative: "meat is off limits for me" — giving a reason.

paraphrases.simplest: Я не ем мясо.

takeaway.note: Я не ем мясо (not this meat — specific) / Я не ем мяса (no meat at all — general). The more specific the object, the more likely the accusative; sweeping denials favour the genitive.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Суп is a masculine noun meaning 'soup.'

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb вместе + imperfective present едим + accusative суп
grammarFocus.note: The first person plural of есть is the irregular едим. суп is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and вместе is an adverb. For a portion you would use the genitive супа (поесть супа).

variations.note: The base form, with the first person plural едим.
The accusative plural супы with the genitive разных видов: "soups of various kinds".
The partitive genitive супа: "let's have some soup".

options.note: обедать (to have lunch) is intransitive and takes no object.
на + accusative двоих (for two) — a collective numeral, colloquial.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы вместе едим суп.

takeaway.pattern: the conjugation of есть (ем, ешь, ест, едим, едите, едят)
takeaway.note: Wholly irregular, so memorise it. The imperative is ешь / ешьте and the past ел / ела / ели — don't confuse it with the past of быть (был).

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Сыр is a masculine noun meaning 'cheese.'

replies.gloss: Which cheese do you like best?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative сыр
grammarFocus.note: любить takes the accusative. сыр (cheese) is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. It is used as an uncountable, taking the genitive сыра when a quantity is meant (много сыра).

variations.note: The base form: "I like cheese".
Adding этот narrows it down; the accusative form is unchanged.
Dative + нравится + nominative сыр — the construction makes the cheese the subject.

options.note: обожать is "to adore" — stronger than любить.
A nominal sentence with a dash: "cheese is my weakness".

paraphrases.simplest: Я люблю сыр.

takeaway.note: сыр, хлеб, мясо, молоко are normally used without counting. For quantity use the genitive (кусок сыра / много сыра); to count varieties, the plural (разные сыры).

skeleton.note: masculine noun, genitive case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Сахар is a masculine noun meaning 'sugar.'

replies.gloss: I like it without sugar too.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present пьём + accusative кофе + без + genitive сахара
grammarFocus.note: The first person plural of пить is пьём, with an irregular soft stem. без + genitive means "without", and the genitive of сахар is сахара. кофе is indeclinable, so the accusative looks the same.

variations.note: The base form, with без + genitive сахара.
с + instrumental молоком means "with milk" — the counterpart of без.
The perfective выпить means finishing the cup; вы- supplies completion.

options.note: A verbless order, with the dative нам: "coffee without sugar for us, please".
Negating добавлять + accusative сахар: "we don't add sugar".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы пьём кофе без сахара.

takeaway.note: кофе без сахара / чай с молоком. "With" and "without" appear as a case contrast — very handy when ordering.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Соль is a feminine noun meaning 'salt.'

grammarFocus.construction: perfective imperative Передай + dative мне + accusative соль
grammarFocus.note: передать (to pass) takes a dative for the person and an accusative for the thing; its imperative is передай. соль is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative. It is the standard phrase at table.

variations.note: The base form, for someone you address informally.
The polite передайте with пожалуйста; the dative may be dropped.
перец (pepper) is masculine, so accusative = nominative.

options.note: можешь + infinitive recasts it as a request.
A negated future question — the most tentative and polite version.

paraphrases.simplest: Передай мне соль.

takeaway.note: дать, передать, принести, показать all share the frame. At table it lives in set phrases: Передай соль / Передай хлеб.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Яблоко is a neuter noun meaning 'apple.'

grammarFocus.construction: imperative Дай + dative мне + the numeral одно + accusative яблоко
grammarFocus.note: дать takes a dative and an accusative. яблоко is neuter, so accusative = nominative, and the numeral одно agrees in the neuter. один behaves like an adjective and changes with the noun's gender.

variations.note: The base form, with одно agreeing with the neuter noun.
After 2-4 the noun goes genitive singular: яблока.
From five up it is the genitive plural яблок — the classic three tiers.

options.note: можно + dative + accusative, asking permission with no verb.
The perfective future of взять: "I'll take one apple" — helping yourself.

paraphrases.simplest: Дай мне яблоко.

takeaway.pattern: 1 agrees, 2-4 take genitive singular, 5+ take genitive plural
takeaway.note: одно яблоко / два яблока / пять яблок. Only один agrees like an adjective; from two up the numeral governs the noun's case.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Сигарета is a feminine noun meaning 'cigarette.'

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive тебя + есть + nominative сигарета
grammarFocus.note: Affirmative possession is у + genitive + есть + nominative, so сигарета stays nominative. The negative would be нет + genitive сигареты. Including есть makes it a question about having something at all.

variations.note: The base form — есть + nominative asks whether you have one.
The plural сигареты with the polite вас.
The negative takes нет + genitive plural сигарет.

options.note: угостить + instrumental сигаретой is "to treat someone to" — a colloquial way of asking.
можно + accusative сигарету — the shortest form, with no verb.

paraphrases.simplest: У тебя есть сигарета?

takeaway.note: У тебя есть сигарета? / У меня нет сигарет. The possessed noun swaps case between affirmative and negative — a core Russian pattern.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Температура is a feminine noun meaning 'temperature.'

replies.gloss: You should lie down and rest.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive меня + nominative высокая температура
grammarFocus.note: Describing a condition, so есть is dropped. температура is feminine, hence высокая. It is the standard medical phrase, where высокая температура means a high fever.

variations.note: The base form: "I have a high temperature".
Even without the adjective it idiomatically means "I have a fever".
The past была (feminine singular): "I had a fever".

options.note: знобить is an impersonal verb with the accusative: "I have the chills".
измерить + accusative температуру: "I need to take my temperature".

paraphrases.simplest: У меня температура.

takeaway.pattern: температура on its own means a fever
takeaway.note: У меня температура = I'm running a temperature. To say it is normal you need нормальная температура. Health conditions generally use the у кого + nominative possessive.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, prepositional case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Опасность is a feminine noun meaning 'danger.'

replies.gloss: You need to get out of here.

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + в + prepositional опасности
grammarFocus.note: быть в опасности (to be in danger) is a set в + prepositional phrase. опасность is a feminine -ь noun with the prepositional опасности. With no copula in the present, Ты в опасности stands alone.

variations.note: The base form — a nominal sentence with no verb.
The past inserts был: "you were in danger".
Dative + опасно + infinitive, impersonal: "it's dangerous for you to stay".

options.note: угрожать + dative (to threaten), with опасность as subject.
небезопасно is не fused onto the adjective, serving as a predicate adverb.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты в опасности.

takeaway.note: в опасности / в беде / в порядке / в курсе / в настроении. A state is named with a noun in в + prepositional, and in the present быть disappears.

skeleton.note: adjective, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Короткий is an adjective meaning 'short.'

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past выбрали + accusative короткий маршрут
grammarFocus.note: выбрать (to choose) takes the accusative. маршрут (route) is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and короткий stays unchanged. A comparative would be более короткий маршрут.

variations.note: The base form: "we chose the short route".
более + adjective makes the comparative: "a shorter route".
самый + adjective makes the superlative: "the shortest route".

options.note: The instrumental короткой дорогой expresses the route taken: "we went the short way".
The comparative adverb быстрее: "this way is quicker".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы выбрали короткий маршрут.

takeaway.pattern: comparative более + adjective, superlative самый + adjective
takeaway.note: более короткий (shorter) / самый короткий (shortest). The short comparative (короче) works only as a predicate, so modifying a noun requires более or самый.

skeleton.note: adjective, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Длинный is an adjective meaning 'long.'

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past прошли + accusative длинный путь
grammarFocus.note: пройти (to cover, to walk the whole way) takes the accusative, and пройти путь is a set phrase for covering a distance. путь is an irregular masculine noun whose accusative matches the nominative. Figuratively it means having come a long way.

variations.note: The base form — literal or figurative.
долгий is "long" in time; длинный is "long" in space.
The accusative gives the distance: "we walked ten kilometres".

options.note: преодолеть + accusative многое: "we overcame a great deal" — purely figurative.
Past был + instrumental нелёгким: "the road was not an easy one".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы прошли длинный путь.

takeaway.pattern: длинный (long in space) vs. долгий (long in time)
takeaway.note: длинная дорога (a long road) / долгий день (a long day). путь takes either, but choose длинный for distance and долгий for years.

skeleton.note: adjective, prepositional case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Глубокий is an adjective meaning 'deep.'

grammarFocus.construction: negated не купаемся + в + prepositional глубокой реке
grammarFocus.note: купаться (to bathe, to swim for pleasure) is reflexive, with the place in в + prepositional. The prepositional of река is реке, and глубокой is the feminine prepositional. Negation does not change the prepositional phrase.

variations.ru: Мы не купаемся в глубокой реке.
variations.note: The base form, with the feminine prepositional глубокой реке.
море is neuter with the prepositional море, and тёплом matches the masculine form.
нельзя + imperfective infinitive, impersonal: "no swimming here".

options.note: бояться + genitive глубины: "we're afraid of the depth" — giving the reason.
у + genitive берега (near the bank) limits the area.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы не купаемся в глубокой реке.

takeaway.note: купаться в море (splash about in the sea) / плавать в бассейне (swim in a pool). The verb reflects whether it is recreation or actual swimming.

skeleton.note: adjective, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Тихий is an adjective meaning 'quiet.'

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past нашли + accusative тихую улицу
grammarFocus.note: найти (to find) takes the accusative, with the plural past нашли. улица is feminine with the accusative улицу, and тихую is the feminine singular accusative — the -ую ending makes the case visible.

variations.note: The base form, with the feminine accusative тихую улицу.
район is masculine, so тихий (nominative-shaped).
место is neuter, hence тихое — the gender endings differ.

options.note: потише is a colloquial comparative: "we picked a quieter street".
The predicate adverb тихо, impersonal: "it's very quiet here".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы нашли тихую улицу.

takeaway.note: тихую улицу / новую книгу / последнюю страницу. Masculine inanimates and neuters match the nominative, so only feminine nouns show the accusative clearly.

skeleton.note: adjective, plural form, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Тёплый is an adjective meaning 'warm.'

replies.gloss: That's the best time for walks.
Let's go for a walk this evening.

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative plural тёплые вечера
grammarFocus.note: любить takes the accusative. The plural of вечер is вечера, with a stress shift; being inanimate, the accusative matches the nominative, and тёплые agrees in the plural.

variations.note: The base form, with the accusative plural тёплые вечера.
The singular is possible, but preferences usually take the plural.
в + prepositional июле narrows it to a season.

options.note: Dative + нравятся + nominative plural; the verb agrees with the subject.
The short plural хороши as predicate: "summer evenings are especially fine".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы любим тёплые вечера.

takeaway.note: Я люблю тёплые вечера / Я люблю собак / Я люблю русские фильмы. A general liking goes in the plural; the singular points to one particular thing.

skeleton.note: adjective, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Холодный is an adjective meaning 'cold.'

replies.gloss: I want to try one too.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past заказали + accusative холодный кофе
grammarFocus.note: заказать (to order) takes the accusative. кофе is indeclinable but masculine, so the adjective takes the masculine холодный (the neuter холодное кофе is colloquial drift).

variations.note: The base form; холодный is the evidence that кофе is masculine.
вода is feminine, hence the accusative холодную воду.
Even after a numeral кофе stays unchanged: два кофе, two coffees.

options.note: A verbless order, with the dative нам: "iced coffee for us, please".
можно + accusative — the colloquial way to order.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы заказали холодный кофе.

takeaway.note: холодный кофе / этот кофе / кофе остыл. Adjectives and past-tense verbs take masculine forms; the neuter (холодное кофе) is colloquial, not the norm.

skeleton.note: adjective, instrumental case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Тупой is an adjective meaning 'blunt, dull.'

grammarFocus.construction: считать + accusative этот нож + instrumental тупым
grammarFocus.note: The считать что чем frame puts the assessing adjective in the instrumental. нож (knife) is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and the masculine instrumental of тупой is тупым. Its opposite is острый (sharp).

variations.note: The base form, with тупым as the verdict.
острым reverses it; the instrumental ending is the same.
Without the считать frame it is a nominal sentence with the nominative тупой.

options.note: резать with the adverb плохо: "this knife doesn't cut well".
наточить + accusative нож: "the knife needs sharpening" — the remedy.

paraphrases.simplest: Этот нож тупой.

takeaway.note: Both stretch into metaphor: тупой вопрос (a stupid question), острый вкус (a hot taste), острый ум (a sharp mind). The instrumental of assessment pairs with считать, называть and находить.

skeleton.note: adjective, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Сладкий is an adjective meaning 'sweet.'

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present пьём + accusative сладкий чай
grammarFocus.note: The first person plural of пить is пьём. чай (tea) is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and сладкий stays unchanged. It also has the partitive forms чаю / чая for "some tea".

variations.note: The base form: "we drink sweet tea".
The colloquial partitive genitive чаю: "pour me some tea".
без + genitive сахара: "tea without sugar".

options.note: с + instrumental сахаром: "tea with sugar".
послаще is a colloquial comparative: "a bit sweeter for me, please".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы пьём сладкий чай.

takeaway.pattern: the partitive genitive in -у (чаю, сахару, супу)
takeaway.note: Some masculine nouns take a -у genitive for a portion (налить чаю). It coexists with the standard -а (вкус чая), and the -у form is the colloquial way to signal quantity.

skeleton.note: adjective, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Свежий is an adjective meaning 'fresh.'

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past купили + accusative свежий хлеб
grammarFocus.note: купить (to buy) takes the accusative. хлеб is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and свежий (fresh) stays unchanged. For an unspecified amount you can use the genitive хлеба (купить хлеба).

variations.note: The base form — a specific loaf bought.
The partitive genitive хлеба: "we bought some bread", amount unspecified.
The accusative plural булочки with свежие: "we bought fresh rolls".

options.note: A nominal sentence: "the bread is still warm" — freshness by another route.
взять (to get) with в + prepositional булочной (at the bakery).

paraphrases.simplest: Мы купили свежий хлеб.

takeaway.pattern: accusative (a specific whole) vs. partitive genitive (an unspecified amount)
takeaway.note: купить хлеб (buy the bread) / купить хлеба (buy some bread). Russian lets you choose the genitive whenever the quantity is indefinite.

keyPoint: Опасный is an adjective meaning 'dangerous.'

replies.ru: Какие места ты имеешь в виду?

grammarFocus.construction: избегать + genitive plural опасных мест + instrumental ночью
grammarFocus.note: избегать (to avoid) is an imperfective governing the genitive. The genitive plural of место is мест (zero ending), with опасных in the genitive plural too. ночью is an instrumental time expression.

variations.note: The base form, with the genitive plural опасных мест.
The genitive plural конфликтов: "we avoid conflicts".
The perfective избежать + genitive опасности: "we escaped the danger".

options.note: A negation with туда (there): "we don't go there at night" — concrete.
стараться + negated infinitive; рисковать takes the instrumental, left unexpressed here.

paraphrases.simplest: Мы избегаем опасных мест.

takeaway.note: избегать людей / конфликтов / ответа. "Avoid" takes the genitive, not the accusative. бояться, лишиться and достичь belong to the same genitive family.

keyPoint: Местный is an adjective meaning 'local.'

replies.gloss: The produce there is always fresh.
How often do you go there?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative местный рынок
grammarFocus.note: любить takes the accusative. рынок is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and местный (local) stays unchanged. Note also that the stem vowel о drops from the genitive on (рынка).

variations.note: The base form: "we love the local market".
кухня is feminine, so the accusative is местную кухню.
от + genitive рынка — an example of the dropped stem vowel.

options.note: The multidirectional ходить with на + accusative: "we often go to the market".
на + prepositional местном рынке with the neuter predicate свежее: "everything's fresh there".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы любим местный рынок.

takeaway.note: рынок, подарок, ребёнок drop the stem о or е from the genitive onwards. The vowel exists only in the nominative, so watch for it when declining.

keyPoint: Национальный is an adjective meaning 'national.'

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative plural национальные праздники
grammarFocus.note: праздник (holiday) is masculine inanimate, so the accusative plural праздники matches the nominative, with национальные agreeing. Note too that the д is silent in pronunciation ([празник]).

variations.note: The base form, with the accusative plural национальные праздники.
кухня is feminine, hence национальную.
в + accusative plural праздники means "on holidays" — a time expression.

options.note: Dative + нравятся + nominative plural — a different construction.
отмечать + accusative is "to celebrate": "we always celebrate the holidays".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы любим национальные праздники.

takeaway.note: в праздники / в выходные / в каникулы. Plural stretches of time take в + accusative plural, and single weekdays follow the same frame (в среду).

keyPoint: Частный is an adjective meaning 'private.'

replies.gloss: How much do you pay a month?

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present снимаю + accusative частный дом
grammarFocus.note: снимать means "to rent (as tenant)" and takes the accusative (снимать квартиру). дом is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and частный (private) stays unchanged.

variations.note: The base form: "I rent a private house".
квартира is feminine, so the accusative is квартиру — by far the commonest pairing.
сдавать is the opposite, "to let out" — the prefix reverses the direction.

options.note: в + prepositional съёмном доме (in a rented house), using the adjective съёмный.

options.ru: Дом не мой, я его арендую.
options.note: арендовать + accusative is the formal "to lease" — contract language.

paraphrases.simplest: Я снимаю квартиру.

takeaway.note: Я снимаю квартиру (I'm the tenant) / Я сдаю квартиру (I'm the landlord). Pick the wrong verb and the roles flip entirely.

keyPoint: Военный is an adjective meaning 'military.'

replies.gloss: Which branch does he serve in?

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the adjective военный + predicate noun человек
grammarFocus.note: военный (military) agrees with человек as a masculine singular nominative adjective, and there is no copula in the present. военный also stands alone as a noun meaning "a serviceman".

variations.note: The base form — adjective plus noun as predicate.
The adjective used as a noun: "he's a military man".
With the past был it goes instrumental: военным.

options.note: служить в + prepositional армии: "he serves in the army".
The noun офицер gives a more specific predicate.

paraphrases.simplest: Он военный.

takeaway.pattern: adjectives used as nouns (военный, учёный, знакомый, больной)
takeaway.note: They come from phrases like военный человек and keep adjectival endings even as nouns (военного, военному). Recognise them by their shape.
