keyPoint: Медицинский is an adjective meaning 'medical.'

replies.gloss: I'll call an ambulance right now.

grammarFocus.construction: dative Мне + нужна + nominative медицинская помощь
grammarFocus.note: нужен is a short-form adjective: the person needing goes in the dative, the thing needed in the nominative. помощь is a feminine -ь noun, so нужна is feminine and медицинская matches.

variations.note: The base form; нужна agrees with помощь (feminine).
врач is masculine, hence нужен.
The plural лекарства takes нужны — four forms in all.

options.note: скорая (ambulance) is an adjective used as a noun; accusative скорую — the emergency formula.
The imperative of помочь (which governs the dative): "please help!"

paraphrases.simplest: Мне нужен врач.

takeaway.pattern: нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны agree with the nominative noun
takeaway.note: нужен врач / нужна помощь / нужно время / нужны деньги. The person stays in the dative while the form follows what is needed.

skeleton.note: adjective, plural form, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Северный is an adjective meaning 'northern.'

replies.ru: Какая страна тебе нравится больше всего?
replies.gloss: Which country do you like most?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative plural северные страны
grammarFocus.note: страна (country) is feminine, and its accusative plural страны matches the nominative, with северные agreeing. Even feminine nouns show no accusative-nominative difference in the plural when inanimate.

variations.note: The base form, with the accusative plural северные страны.
The feminine singular accusative северную природу shows the -ую ending.
в + prepositional plural северных странах: "I've been in northern countries".

options.note: Dative + нравится + nominative север: "I like the north".
предпочитать + accusative: "I prefer a cold climate".

paraphrases.simplest: Я люблю северные страны.

takeaway.pattern: inanimate plurals have nominative = accusative in all genders
takeaway.note: страны, книги, дома, места all match in the plural. Only animate plurals (людей, друзей) copy the genitive — that is the one distinction to watch.

skeleton.note: adjective, plural form, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Южный is an adjective meaning 'southern.'

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative plural южные страны
grammarFocus.note: любить takes the accusative. страны is an inanimate plural, so the accusative matches the nominative, and южные agrees in the plural. южный (southern) pairs with северный (northern).

variations.note: The base form, with the accusative plural южные страны.
The noun юг (the south) in the accusative — shorter and simpler.
на + prepositional юге: "I live in the south" — compass points take на.

options.note: Dative + нравится + nominative южный климат.
предпочитать + accusative тепло (warmth), a neuter noun.

paraphrases.simplest: Я люблю южные страны.

takeaway.pattern: compass points take на + prepositional (на юге, на севере, на западе, на востоке)
takeaway.note: Location takes на + prepositional, direction на + accusative (на юг, southwards). These nouns take на, never в.

skeleton.note: adjective, plural form, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Чужой is an adjective meaning 'someone else's.'

grammarFocus.construction: negated не беру + accusative plural чужие вещи
grammarFocus.note: брать (to take) is imperfective, and its present states a habit or principle. вещи is an inanimate plural, so the accusative matches the nominative, and чужие (other people's) agrees. The object stays accusative despite the negation.

variations.note: The base form — a principle: "I don't take other people's things".
The genitive plural of negation чужих вещей sounds more absolute.
The perfective не взял denies one specific occasion.

options.ru: Это не моё, я не трогал.
options.note: Negating трогать + accusative in the past: "that's not mine, I didn't touch it".
чужое is an adjective used as a noun, with нельзя + imperfective infinitive.

paraphrases.simplest: Я не беру чужие вещи.

takeaway.note: свои вещи / чужие вещи. An important pair for contrasting ownership, and свой is special in that it refers back to the subject.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Приготовить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective готовить.

replies.gloss: How much sugar do you want?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive приготовить + the indeclinable accusative кофе
grammarFocus.note: приготовить (to prepare, to cook) takes the accusative, and приготовить кофе means making coffee. кофе is indeclinable, so the accusative looks identical. The imperfective is готовить.

variations.note: The base form — the perfective for making one cup.
The imperfective готовить + accusative ужин: "I'm making dinner".
сварить (to boil) also serves for brewing coffee — more concrete.

options.note: Хочешь, ... ? is the "shall I ...?" offer pattern.
поставить кофе is the colloquial "I'll put the coffee on".

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу приготовить кофе.

takeaway.pattern: готовить (cook, imperfective) vs. приготовить (finish cooking, perfective)
takeaway.note: Я готовлю ужин (I'm cooking) / Я приготовил ужин (I've made dinner). The reflexive готовиться к + dative is a separate verb meaning "to prepare for".

skeleton.note: 3rd person plural present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Строить is imperfective, describing the process of 'building,' paired with the perfective построить.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present строят + accusative новый дом
grammarFocus.note: строить (to build) takes the accusative as an imperfective, and the present describes work under way. дом is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, with новый unchanged. The perfective is построить.

variations.note: The base form — an action in progress.
The perfective построили: "they've built a new house".
The reflexive passive строится: "a new house is being built here".

options.note: With the noun стройка as subject and идёт marking the process.
The negated short form готов: "the house isn't finished yet".

paraphrases.simplest: Они строят новый дом.

takeaway.note: Adding -ся gives "is being done" without naming an agent: Дом строится (the house is under construction) / Магазин открывается в девять (the shop opens at nine).

skeleton.note: past masculine, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Сломать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective ломать.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past сломал + accusative телефон
grammarFocus.note: сломать (to break) takes the accusative. телефон is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. The reflexive сломаться means the thing broke by itself, shifting where the responsibility lies.

variations.note: The base form — admitting you broke it.
The reflexive сломаться leaves the agent out: "the phone broke".
сломала for a female speaker.

options.note: Negating работать states the condition: "the phone isn't working".
починить + accusative is "to repair" — naming the fix.

paraphrases.simplest: Телефон сломался.

takeaway.note: Я сломал телефон (I broke it — my fault) / Телефон сломался (it broke — just happened). The -ся lets you adjust how much blame you take.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Танцевать is imperfective, meaning 'to dance,' paired with the perfective станцевать.

replies.gloss: What kind of dancing do you like?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + imperfective infinitive танцевать
grammarFocus.note: любить + infinitive always takes the imperfective, since preferences are habitual. танцевать is an -овать verb conjugating as танцую / танцуешь. A dance partner takes с + instrumental (танцевать с ней).

variations.note: The base form: "do you like dancing?"
With уметь it asks about skill: "can you dance?"
The perfective потанцевать with давай: "let's have a dance".

options.note: Dative + нравится + infinitive: "do you enjoy dancing?"
на + accusative plural танцы means going to dance classes or events.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты любишь танцевать?

takeaway.pattern: любить + imperfective infinitive, уметь + imperfective infinitive
takeaway.note: Neither verb takes a perfective. Both a preference (любить) and a skill (уметь) are permanent traits, so they never pair with a one-off perfective.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Учить is imperfective, describing the process of 'learning, memorizing,' paired with the perfective выучить.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present учу + accusative plural новые слова
grammarFocus.note: учить (to learn by heart) takes the accusative, and учить слова means memorising vocabulary. слова is a neuter plural, so accusative = nominative, with новые agreeing. The perfective is выучить.

variations.note: The base form — ongoing or habitual study.
The perfective выучить: "I've learnt them"; вы- supplies completion.
The reflexive учиться means "to be enrolled" and takes no accusative.

options.note: запоминать + accusative focuses on the act of memorising.
расширять + accusative словарный запас (vocabulary) — formal phrasing.

paraphrases.simplest: Я учу новые слова.

takeaway.pattern: учить что (memorise) / учить кого чему (teach) / учиться (study, be enrolled)
takeaway.note: Я учу слова (I learn words) / Я учу детей русскому языку (I teach children Russian — accusative + dative) / Я учусь (I'm a student). One root, three frames.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Изучать is imperfective, describing the process of 'studying (systematically),' paired with the perfective изучить.

replies.gloss: How long have you been studying?

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present изучаю + accusative русский язык
grammarFocus.note: изучать (to study systematically) takes the accusative. русский язык is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. It implies more scholarly, structured study than учить (to memorise).

variations.note: The base form — systematic study.
учить also works but leans towards the drill of memorising.
The accusative историю with the genitive modifier России: "I study Russian history".

options.note: заниматься + instrumental русским языком: "I work on Russian".
учиться + infinitive: "I'm learning to speak Russian".

paraphrases.simplest: Я изучаю русский язык.

takeaway.pattern: изучать что (accusative) / заниматься чем (instrumental) / учиться где (prepositional)
takeaway.note: изучать физику / заниматься физикой / учиться в школе. Every "study" verb governs a different case.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Повторить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective повторять.

grammarFocus.construction: Можешь + perfective infinitive повторить + accusative это
grammarFocus.note: повторить (to repeat) takes the accusative, and можешь + infinitive makes the request. это is the neuter pronoun, identical in nominative and accusative. It is the single most useful way to ask someone to say it again.

variations.note: The base form, for someone you address informally.
The polite можете with пожалуйста; the object may be dropped.
An imperative with ещё раз (once more) — direct.

options.note: The negated past of расслышать: "sorry, I didn't catch that".
The shortest version: "what did you say?"

paraphrases.simplest: Можете повторить, пожалуйста?

takeaway.pattern: the set phrases for asking someone to repeat
takeaway.note: Повторите, пожалуйста / Можете повторить? / Простите, не расслышал. The most indispensable group for a learner, all built on the perfective повторить.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Менять is imperfective, describing the process of 'changing,' paired with the perfective поменять.

replies.gloss: Okay, let's leave it as is.

grammarFocus.construction: не хочу + imperfective infinitive менять + accusative план
grammarFocus.note: менять (to change) takes the accusative as an imperfective. план is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. A negated intention naturally takes the imperfective; the perfective изменить would deny one specific change.

variations.note: The base form: "I don't want to change the plan".
The perfective изменить denies this one change — possible but less natural than менять.
The reflexive меняться: "the plan isn't changing", with no agent.

options.note: пусть + perfective with как есть (as it is): "let's leave everything as it stands".
предпочитать + accusative прежний план (the previous plan).

paraphrases.simplest: Я не хочу менять план.

takeaway.note: Я не хочу менять / Я не хочу идти / Не надо говорить. "I don't want to" and "please don't" take the imperfective; a perfective turns it into denying one particular instance.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Меняться is imperfective, describing the process of 'changing (oneself),' paired with the perfective измениться.

grammarFocus.construction: the reflexive меняюсь + ради + genitive тебя
grammarFocus.note: меняться (to change, intransitive) is менять plus -ся and takes no object. ради + genitive means "for the sake of", so тебя is genitive.

variations.note: The base form, with ради + genitive giving the purpose.
The perfective измениться states the result: "I've changed for you".
Without -ся, менять takes an accusative: "I'm changing my habits".

options.note: становиться + instrumental другим: "I'm becoming a different person".
для + genitive тебя also means "for you" — more everyday than ради.

paraphrases.simplest: Я меняюсь ради тебя.

takeaway.note: ради любви (for love's sake — implying sacrifice or a cause) / для тебя (for your benefit). ради carries weight and a certain loftiness.

skeleton.note: 3rd person plural present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Расти is imperfective, describing the process of 'growing,' paired with the perfective вырасти.

replies.ru: Кажется, только вчера они были маленькими.
replies.gloss: It feels like they were tiny just yesterday.

grammarFocus.construction: the intensifier очень + manner adverb быстро + imperfective present растут
grammarFocus.note: расти (to grow) is an intransitive imperfective, and its present has the irregular stem растут. When two adverbs stack up, degree comes before manner. дети is a plural subject.

variations.note: The base form, with two adverbs in order.
The singular ребёнок takes растёт.
The perfective вырасти: "the children have grown up".

options.note: взрослеть (to grow up) with the idiom на глазах (before your eyes).
Как + perfective past as an exclamation: "how they've grown!"

paraphrases.simplest: Дети быстро растут.

takeaway.pattern: расти (to grow, intransitive) vs. растить (to raise, transitive)
takeaway.note: Дети растут (children grow) / Родители растят детей (parents raise children). The -ить transitive pairs with the intransitive root.

skeleton.note: past masculine, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Вырасти is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective расти.

replies.ru: Это, должно быть, особенно для тебя.
replies.gloss: This place must be special for you.
Has a lot changed since then?

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past вырос + locational здесь
grammarFocus.note: вырасти is the perfective of расти, and its masculine past вырос has no -л. The feminine is выросла and the plural выросли. The sentence is the standard way to say where you grew up.

variations.note: The base form, with the masculine past вырос (no -л).
выросла for a woman.
The plural выросли with в + prepositional деревне: "we grew up in a village".

options.note: родом is an adverbial instrumental: "I'm from here originally".
пройти with the nominative детство: "my childhood was spent here".

paraphrases.simplest: Я здесь вырос.

takeaway.pattern: masculine pasts without -л (вырос, нёс, мог, умер)
takeaway.note: Verbs with consonant-final stems drop the -л in the masculine past (вырос / выросла / выросли). The -ла / -ло / -ли endings reappear elsewhere.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Создавать is imperfective, describing the process of 'creating,' paired with the perfective создать.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present создаю + the indefinite что-то новое
grammarFocus.note: создавать (to create) takes the accusative as an imperfective. что-то (something) is a neuter indefinite pronoun, so the adjective takes the neuter новое. что-то новое and что-то интересное are frequent pairings.

variations.note: The base form: что-то with a neuter adjective.
The perfective создал: "I've created something new".
что-нибудь is "anything at all" — vaguer than что-то.

options.note: работать над + instrumental новым проектом: "I'm working on a new project".
у + genitive + есть + nominative идея: "I have a new idea".

paraphrases.simplest: Я создаю что-то новое.

takeaway.note: что-то новое / что-нибудь вкусное / ничего интересного (genitive under negation). The что- pronouns count as neuter, so the adjective must be neuter too.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Отказываться is imperfective, describing the process of 'refusing,' paired with the perfective отказаться.

grammarFocus.construction: the question word Почему + the reflexive present отказываешься
grammarFocus.note: отказываться (to refuse) is reflexive, and what you refuse takes от + genitive (отказываться от помощи). почему asks the reason. Its perfective is отказаться.

variations.note: The base form, with no object — just asking why.
от + genitive помощи names what is refused.
The perfective past отказался asks about one specific refusal.

options.note: A set phrase with против + genitive: "why are you against it?"
Dative + не нравится with что as subject: "what don't you like?"

paraphrases.simplest: Почему ты отказываешься?

takeaway.note: отказаться от помощи / от предложения / от курения. Giving something up always takes от + genitive. The separate verb отказать кому (to refuse a person) governs the dative instead.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Обмануть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective обманывать.

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive обмануть + accusative меня
grammarFocus.note: обмануть (to deceive) takes the accusative; its imperfective is обманывать. A pronoun object like меня naturally sits before the verb. The sentence is an accusation: "are you trying to trick me?"

variations.note: The base form, with the pronoun before the verb.
The imperfective present: "are you lying to me right now?"
The perfective past states it as fact: "you deceived me".

options.note: With неправда in the accusative — a gentler "are you telling an untruth?"
A zero-copula nominal: "is that a lie?"

paraphrases.simplest: Ты меня обманываешь?

takeaway.pattern: pronoun objects tend to precede the verb
takeaway.note: Ты меня обманул / Я тебя понимаю / Он нас видел. Noun objects normally follow the verb, but pronouns go before it in ordinary speech.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Прощать is imperfective, describing the process of 'forgiving,' paired with the perfective простить.

grammarFocus.construction: не хочу + imperfective infinitive прощать (no object)
grammarFocus.note: прощать (to forgive) takes the accusative as an imperfective, but here the object is dropped: the speaker rejects the act itself. The perfective is простить, and a negated wish naturally takes the imperfective.

variations.note: The base form — stated generally, with no object.
Adding the accusative его names who is not forgiven.
The perfective простить with не могу: "I can't forgive" — an inability.

options.note: The short form готов + infinitive: "I'm not ready to forgive".
The short participle обижен: "I'm still hurt" — stated as a condition.

paraphrases.simplest: Я не хочу прощать.

takeaway.pattern: прощать кого за что (accusative + за + accusative)
takeaway.note: простить друга за опоздание (forgive a friend for being late). The person is accusative, the offence за + accusative. Прости меня! is the set imperative.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Узнавать is imperfective, meaning 'to recognize,' paired with the perfective узнать.

grammarFocus.construction: negated не узнаю + accusative тебя
grammarFocus.note: узнавать / узнать (to recognise) takes the accusative. The negated present не узнаю means failing to recognise someone in front of you. The same verb also means "to find out".

variations.note: The base form, with the pronoun before the verb.
The perfective past: "I didn't recognise you (at the time)".
The other sense of узнать: "I heard the news", with the accusative новость.

options.note: The perfective past of измениться: "you've changed so much!" — giving the reason.
The short plural знакомы: "have we met?"

paraphrases.simplest: Я тебя не узнаю.

takeaway.note: Я тебя узнал (I recognised you) / Я узнал правду (I learned the truth) / Я узнаю расписание (I'll check the timetable). One verb, three senses — context decides.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Требовать is imperfective, describing the process of 'demanding,' paired with the perfective потребовать.

grammarFocus.construction: требовать + genitive ответа
grammarFocus.note: требовать (to demand) governs the genitive with abstract objects, so ответ becomes ответа. Concrete things can take the accusative (требовать деньги), but the genitive is the norm. Its perfective is потребовать.

variations.note: The base form, with the genitive ответа.
The genitive plural объяснений: "I demand an explanation".
The perfective потребовал: one act of demanding.

options.note: услышать + accusative ответ — a softer "I want to hear an answer".
An imperative asking for an explanation — the most practical version.

paraphrases.simplest: Я требую ответа.

takeaway.note: требовать внимания / объяснений (abstract, genitive); требовать документы (demand the documents, accusative also possible). With abstract nouns the genitive is the normative choice.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Появляться is imperfective, describing the process of 'appearing,' paired with the perfective появиться.

grammarFocus.construction: the frequency adverb редко + reflexive present появляешься
grammarFocus.note: появляться (to show up) is reflexive and takes no object. редко (rarely) is a frequency adverb pairing with the imperfective present. The perfective is появиться. The line is a mild reproach: "you hardly ever show up".

variations.note: The base form — frequency adverb with an imperfective present.
часто reverses the frequency.
The perfective появился: "he suddenly appeared" — a single event.

options.note: не видно + accusative тебя, impersonal: "you haven't been seen in ages".
The imperfective past of пропадать: "where have you been hiding?"

paraphrases.simplest: Ты редко появляешься.

takeaway.pattern: frequency adverbs (часто / редко / иногда / всегда / никогда) go with the imperfective
takeaway.note: A perfective names one completed act, so it clashes with adverbs of repetition. Я часто читаю is fine; ×Я часто прочитал is not.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Включить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective включать.

replies.gloss: Yes, of course, turn it on.

grammarFocus.construction: Можно + perfective infinitive включить + accusative свет
grammarFocus.note: можно is a subjectless impersonal predicate asking permission. включить (to switch on) takes the accusative, and свет is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. Its opposite is выключить.

variations.note: The base form, asking permission with можно.
An imperative making the request directly.
Можно я + perfective future names the doer: "may I turn the light on?" — very colloquial.

options.note: The impersonal темно plus a first person plural suggestion.

options.ru: Не против, если я включу свет?
options.note: Не против, если... is the polite permission formula.

paraphrases.simplest: Можно включить свет?

takeaway.pattern: можно + infinitive vs. Можно я + perfective future
takeaway.note: Можно войти? (may one come in — general) / Можно я войду? (may I come in — naming yourself). The second is extremely common in speech.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Выключить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective выключать.

replies.gloss: Yes, I'm sick of it too.

grammarFocus.construction: Можно + perfective infinitive выключить + accusative музыку
grammarFocus.note: выключить (to switch off) takes the accusative. музыка is feminine, so the accusative is музыку. можно asks permission in an impersonal clause, and включить is its opposite.

variations.note: The base form, with the feminine accusative музыку.
потише is a colloquial comparative — proposing to turn it down rather than off.
An imperative making the request directly.

options.note: A nominal sentence with громкая as predicate — giving the reason.
мешать + dative мне: "the music bothers me", with музыка as subject.

paraphrases.simplest: Можно выключить музыку?

takeaway.pattern: degrees of request (imperative → можно → не против, если)
takeaway.note: Выключи (command) < Можно выключить? (permission) < Вы не против, если я выключу? (most polite). Pick by how close you are to the person.

skeleton.note: imperative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Записать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective записывать.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective imperative Запиши + accusative мой номер
grammarFocus.note: записать (to write down) takes the accusative, with the imperative запиши. номер is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, and мой stays unchanged. The prefix за- adds the sense of putting it on record.

variations.note: The base form, for someone you address informally.
The polite запишите with the accusative адрес.
The perfective future запишу: "I'll take down your number".

options.note: сохранить (to save) + accusative — natural with a phone.
скинуть (to send over) + dative тебе — colloquial.

paraphrases.simplest: Запиши мой номер.

takeaway.note: The prefix sets the use: записать номер (take down a number) / написать письмо (write a letter) / подписать документ (sign a document).

skeleton.note: imperative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Надеть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective надевать.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective imperative Надень + accusative тёплую одежду
grammarFocus.note: надеть (to put on) takes the accusative, with the imperative надень. одежда is feminine, so the accusative is одежду, and тёплую matches. Keep it apart from одеть кого (to dress someone).

variations.note: The base form, with the feminine accusative тёплую одежду.
The polite наденьте with the accusative куртку.
одеть + animate accusative ребёнка means dressing the child; теплее is a comparative.

options.note: The reflexive одеться with теплее: "dress more warmly".
The impersonal холодно gives the reason instead.

paraphrases.simplest: Оденься теплее.

takeaway.pattern: надеть что (put on a garment) / одеть кого (dress a person) / одеться (get dressed)
takeaway.note: надеть пальто / одеть ребёнка / одеться тепло. These three are a classic trap for learners, so fix the frames in mind.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ложиться is imperfective, describing the process of 'lying down, going to bed,' paired with the perfective лечь.

grammarFocus.construction: the reflexive ложусь + infinitive спать + в + accusative час
grammarFocus.note: ложиться спать is the set phrase for going to bed, built on the reflexive ложиться (to lie down); the perfective is лечь. в час is a в + accusative time expression, and час is masculine with accusative = nominative.

variations.note: The base form — a habitual bedtime.
The perfective past лёг (no -л): "I went to bed at one".

variations.ru: Я ложусь спать в два часа.
variations.note: в два часа — after 2-4 the noun takes the genitive singular часа.

options.note: засыпать (to fall asleep) with около + genitive часа: "around one".
With поздно (late), avoiding a specific hour.

paraphrases.simplest: Я ложусь спать в час.

takeaway.pattern: clock times take в + accusative (в час, в два часа, в пять часов)
takeaway.note: 1 = в час (nominative-shaped), 2-4 = в два часа (genitive singular), 5+ = в пять часов (genitive plural). Numeral government shows up in telling the time too.

skeleton.note: imperative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Бросать is imperfective, meaning 'to throw,' paired with the perfective бросить.

grammarFocus.construction: negative imperative Не бросай + accusative это + на + accusative пол
grammarFocus.note: Negative imperatives take the imperfective бросай. бросать (to throw, to drop) takes the accusative, and the destination на + accusative. пол (floor) is masculine with accusative = nominative, but its locative is the special на полу.

variations.note: The base form, with directional на + accusative пол.
The polite form with на + accusative землю: "don't drop litter on the ground".
Location takes the special prepositional полу — the contrast with direction.

options.note: положить + на + accusative стол offers the positive alternative.
нельзя + imperfective infinitive мусорить (to litter) — stated as a rule.

paraphrases.simplest: Не бросай это на пол.

takeaway.pattern: на пол (direction, accusative) vs. на полу (location, special prepositional)
takeaway.note: упасть на пол (fall on the floor) / лежать на полу (lie on the floor). пол takes the -у locative with stress on the ending.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Ловить is imperfective, describing the process of 'trying to catch,' paired with the perfective поймать.

replies.gloss: Good luck, there aren't many around here.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present ловлю + the indeclinable accusative такси
grammarFocus.note: ловить (to catch) takes the accusative, and its present inserts an л in the first person: ловлю / ловишь. ловить такси is the set phrase for hailing a cab, and такси never declines.

variations.note: The base form — trying to hail one right now.
The perfective поймать: "I got a taxi" — note the different stem.
вызывать такси means ordering one by phone or app.

options.note: остановить + accusative машину: "I'm trying to flag down a car".
заказывать такси (to order a taxi) — the modern default.

paraphrases.simplest: Я ловлю такси.

takeaway.pattern: ловить / поймать is an aspect pair with different stems
takeaway.note: ловлю рыбу (I'm fishing) / поймал рыбу (I caught a fish). When the two aspects diverge this much, learn them as separate forms.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Выстрелить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective стрелять.

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть + perfective infinitive выстрелить + в + accusative мишень
grammarFocus.note: выстрелить (to fire a shot) is intransitive, and the target takes в + accusative. мишень is a feminine -ь noun with an identical accusative. The imperfective стрелять uses the same frame.

variations.note: The base form, with в + accusative naming the target.
уметь + imperfective infinitive asks about the skill: "can you shoot?"
в + accusative воздух: "he fired into the air".

options.note: The noun стрельба (shooting) in the accusative: "would you like to try shooting?"
сделать выстрел (to take a shot) is a light-verb phrase.

paraphrases.simplest: Вы хотите выстрелить в мишень?

takeaway.note: стрелять в мишень / в человека / в воздух. The target always takes в + accusative — it is never a bare direct object.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Напасть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective нападать.

grammarFocus.construction: мочь + perfective infinitive напасть (может of possibility)
grammarFocus.note: напасть (to attack) takes на + accusative as a perfective, though the object is left out here. может expresses possibility, "might". собака is the subject.

variations.note: The base form — a warning with no object.
на + accusative ребёнка (animate, genitive-shaped) names the target.
The perfective past напала with на + accusative меня: "the dog attacked me".

options.note: The reflexive кусаться describes a habit: "careful, the dog bites!"
The short form опасна (feminine): "this dog is dangerous".

paraphrases.simplest: Собака может напасть.

takeaway.note: напасть на прохожего / на деревню / на идею (to hit upon an idea). Both attacking and stumbling upon something take на + accusative, never a bare object.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Бороться is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of 'fighting/struggling.' Побороться exists as a delimitative meaning 'to struggle for a while,' not a true pair.

replies.ru: Что именно ты делаешь для этого?
replies.gloss: What exactly are you doing for that?

grammarFocus.construction: бороться + за + accusative свою мечту
grammarFocus.note: бороться (to fight) is a reflexive verb with no perfective, taking за + accusative (for something) or с + instrumental (against someone). мечта is feminine with the accusative мечту, and свою agrees.

variations.note: The base form, with за + accusative giving the cause.
с + instrumental болезнью: "I'm fighting an illness" — the opponent frame.
за + accusative plural права (rights) — common in social contexts.

options.note: Negating сдаваться: "I'm not giving up".
добиваться + genitive своей цели: "I'm pursuing my goal".

paraphrases.simplest: Я борюсь за свою мечту.

takeaway.pattern: бороться за что (a cause) vs. бороться с кем / чем (an opponent)
takeaway.note: бороться за свободу (fight for freedom) / бороться с врагом (fight the enemy). за means "for the sake of", с means "against".

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Проиграть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective проигрывать.

grammarFocus.construction: не хотим + perfective infinitive проиграть
grammarFocus.note: проиграть (to lose) is perfective, with the imperfective проигрывать. The opponent takes the dative (проиграть команде) and the stake the accusative (проиграть деньги). The perfective denies one particular defeat.

variations.note: The base form — determined not to lose this time.
The imperfective means "we don't want to keep losing" — repetition denied.
The dative команде names the team we lost to.

options.note: должны + perfective infinitive выиграть states it positively: "we must win".
Dative + нужна + nominative победа: "we need a victory".

paraphrases.simplest: Мы не хотим проиграть.

takeaway.note: проиграть сопернику (lose to an opponent) / проиграть матч (lose the match) / проиграть деньги (lose money). The victor takes the dative, the thing lost the accusative.

skeleton.note: 3rd person plural present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Спасать is imperfective, describing the process of 'saving,' paired with the perfective спасти.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present спасают + accusative plural жизни
grammarFocus.note: спасать (to save) takes the accusative, and the present states what the profession does. жизнь is a feminine -ь noun whose accusative plural жизни matches the nominative. врачи is a plural subject.

variations.note: The base form — a general truth in the present.
The perfective спас with accusative жизнь and dative ребёнку: "saved the child's life".
Fronting the accusative его: "he was saved by the doctors".

options.note: помогать + dative plural людям — the dative government.
A nominal sentence with a dash plus an infinitive: "that's their job".

paraphrases.simplest: Врачи спасают жизни.

takeaway.note: спасти человека (save a person) / помочь человеку (help a person). English "help" blurs them, but Russian assigns different cases, so learn each verb's frame.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Лечить is imperfective, describing the process of 'treating,' paired with the perfective вылечить.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present лечит + animate accusative plural детей
grammarFocus.note: лечить (to treat medically) takes the accusative, and the accusative plural of дети is the genitive-shaped детей. этот врач is a masculine singular subject, hence лечит. The perfective вылечить means curing completely.

variations.note: The base form, with the animate accusative plural детей.
The perfective вылечил with the animate accusative моего сына.
The reflexive лечиться у + genitive: "I'm being treated by this doctor".

options.note: The predicate noun детский врач (paediatrician); no copula in the present.
работать с + instrumental plural детьми: "he works with children".

paraphrases.simplest: Этот врач лечит детей.

takeaway.pattern: лечить кого (to treat) vs. лечиться у кого (to be treated)
takeaway.note: Врач лечит пациента / Пациент лечится у врача. Adding -ся shifts the viewpoint to the patient.

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Дышать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of 'breathing.' Подышать exists as a delimitative meaning 'to breathe for a while,' not a true pair.

grammarFocus.construction: dative Мне + the predicate adverb трудно + infinitive дышать
grammarFocus.note: трудно (difficult) is a subjectless predicate adverb, and the person affected goes in the dative. The infinitive дышать says what is difficult. дышать itself governs the instrumental, though no object appears here.

variations.note: The base form — dative plus predicate adverb plus infinitive.
тяжело also means "hard", with more of a physical heaviness.
легко (easy) reverses it within the same construction.

options.note: проблемы с + instrumental дыханием: "I have trouble breathing".
Dative + не хватает + genitive воздуха: "I can't get enough air".

paraphrases.simplest: Мне трудно дышать.

takeaway.note: Мне трудно понять / Мне легко читать / Ему интересно слушать. The experiencer is dative, the judgement an -о adverb, the content an infinitive.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Пахнуть is a stative imperfective verb meaning 'to smell (of),' with no perfective counterpart.

replies.gloss: Did you have coffee this morning?

grammarFocus.construction: пахнуть + instrumental кофе + после + genitive завтрака
grammarFocus.note: пахнуть (to smell of) takes the instrumental — пахнуть кофе means smelling of coffee. кофе is indeclinable, so the instrumental looks the same. после + genitive завтрака is "after breakfast". The impersonal Пахнет кофе is very common.

variations.note: The base form, with the instrumental кофе as the source of the smell.
The impersonal пахнет + instrumental: "it smells of coffee here" — no subject.
от + genitive тебя with the instrumental духами: "you smell of perfume".

options.note: The noun запах + genitive кофе: "I've got the smell of coffee on me".
The perfective past of выпить explains why: "I've just had coffee".

paraphrases.simplest: Здесь пахнет кофе.

takeaway.pattern: пахнуть + instrumental (the source of the smell)
takeaway.note: пахнуть духами / цветами / дымом. The kind of smell goes instrumental, and the place or person emitting it takes от + genitive. The impersonal Пахнет... is the commonest shape.

skeleton.note: imperative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Трогать is imperfective, meaning 'to touch,' paired with the perfective тронуть.

replies.gloss: I have private stuff on there.

grammarFocus.construction: negative imperative Не трогай + accusative мой телефон
grammarFocus.note: Negative imperatives take the imperfective трогай. трогать (to touch) takes the accusative, and телефон is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative, with мой unchanged. The perfective is тронуть.

variations.note: The base form: "don't touch my phone".
The polite form with the accusative plural мои вещи.
With the accusative меня: "don't touch me" — also used figuratively.

options.note: The imperative положи (put it down) with the accusative его — a concrete instruction.
убрать руки (take your hands off) — colloquial and forceful.

paraphrases.simplest: Не трогай мой телефон.

takeaway.note: Не трогай (don't touch — prohibition, imperfective) / Не тронь (don't you dare — the older perfective imperative). The verb also means "to move emotionally" (Это меня тронуло).

skeleton.note: infinitive, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Поцеловать is perfective, marking a single completed kiss, paired with the imperfective целовать.

grammarFocus.construction: Можно + perfective infinitive поцеловать + accusative тебя
grammarFocus.note: поцеловать (to kiss) takes the accusative, and можно + infinitive asks permission impersonally. Putting тебя before the verb is the natural order. The reflexive поцеловаться means kissing each other.

variations.note: The base form, with the pronoun before the verb.
Можно я + perfective future names the doer: "may I kiss you?"
The reciprocal -ся: "we kissed".

options.ru: Ты не против, если я тебя поцелую?
options.note: Ты не против, если... is the most tentative and polite way to ask.
ко мне (come to me) uses the phonetic variant of к — an invitation without words.

paraphrases.simplest: Можно тебя поцеловать?

takeaway.pattern: поцеловать кого (accusative) vs. поцеловаться с кем (instrumental)
takeaway.note: Он поцеловал её (he kissed her — one-way) / Они поцеловались (they kissed — mutual). A textbook case of -ся adding reciprocity.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, dative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Тётя is a feminine noun meaning 'aunt.'

grammarFocus.construction: the frequency adverb часто + звонить + dative тёте
grammarFocus.note: звонить governs the dative, so тётя becomes тёте. часто with the imperfective present states a habit. тётя ends in -я, and its dative ends in -е.

variations.note: The base form, with the dative тёте.
дядя also ends in -я but is grammatically masculine; the dative is дяде.
The perfective позвонил: "I rang her yesterday" — one call.

options.note: общаться с + instrumental тётей: "we're often in touch".
Мы с + instrumental is the "my aunt and I" pattern; на связи means being in contact.

paraphrases.simplest: Я часто звоню тёте.

takeaway.note: звонить маме / врачу, but звонить в банк for an institution (в + accusative). People take the dative, organisations в / на + accusative.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Возраст is a masculine noun meaning 'age.'

replies.ru: Сколько тебе лет, если не секрет?
replies.gloss: How old are you, if you don't mind sharing?

grammarFocus.construction: negated не скрываю + accusative свой возраст
grammarFocus.note: скрывать (to hide) takes the accusative as an imperfective. возраст is masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative. свой is the reflexive possessive pointing back to the subject — here я, so "my own".

variations.note: The base form, with the reflexive possessive свой.
With она as subject, свой still means "her own".
The accusative правду — a feminine noun, hence the -у ending.

options.note: нечего + infinitive, impersonal: "I have nothing to hide".
The adverb открыто (openly): "I speak frankly".

paraphrases.simplest: Я не скрываю свой возраст.

takeaway.pattern: свой (the subject's own) vs. его / её (someone else's)
takeaway.note: Он взял свою книгу (he took his own book) / Он взял его книгу (he took the other man's book). The presence of свой changes who owns it.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, genitive case, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Развод is a masculine noun meaning 'divorce.'

grammarFocus.construction: бояться + genitive развода
grammarFocus.note: бояться (to fear) is a reflexive verb governing the genitive, so развод becomes развода. The crucial point is that it takes the genitive, not the accusative. It can also take an infinitive (бояться потерять).

variations.note: The base form, with the genitive развода.
The genitive одиночества (loneliness) — the same frame.
бояться + perfective infinitive: "I'm afraid of ending up alone".

options.note: пугать + accusative меня with the nominative мысль and о + prepositional: "the thought of divorce frightens me".
The infinitive расставаться: "I don't want us to part".

paraphrases.simplest: Я боюсь развода.

takeaway.note: бояться темноты (afraid of the dark — genitive) / бояться упасть (afraid of falling — infinitive). Nouns take the genitive, actions the infinitive.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, plural accusative, the target word of this sentence

keyPoint: Праздник is a masculine noun meaning 'holiday, celebration.'

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative plural семейные праздники
grammarFocus.note: любить takes the accusative. праздники is an inanimate plural, so accusative = nominative, with семейные agreeing. семейный is the adjective formed from семья.
